body.text: ācāryakamalaśīlapraṇīto

children.translated_text: <s>Bhāvanākrama</s> (Stages of Meditation), Part One
[The prescribed practice for a beginner according to the <s>Mahāyāna sūtras</s> —
With regard to that, the <s>Bhāvanākrama</s> (Stages of Meditation) is briefly set forth.]

body.translated_text: Composed by <s>Ācārya Kamalaśīla</s>

body.text: acireṇa sarvajñatāṃ prāptukāmaiḥ saṃkṣepataḥ karuṇā, bodhicittam, pratipattiśceti triṣu sthāneṣu prayatitavyam /
body.translated_text: Those who wish to attain <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) swiftly should exert themselves in three areas, briefly stated: <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), and <s>pratipatti</s> (practice).

body.text: buddhatvasya aśeṣadharmahetumūlaṃ karuṇaiveti jñātvā sādāveva bhāvayitavyā / yathoktam āryadharmasaṃgītisūtre- "atha khalvavalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahasattvo bhagavantametadavocat- na bhagavan bodhisattvena atibahuṣu dharmeṣu śikṣitavyam / eko dharmo bhagavan bodhisattvena svārādhitaḥ supratividdhaḥ kartavyaḥ / tasya sarvabuddhadharmāḥ karatalagatā bhavanti / katama ekadharmaḥ? yaduta mahākaruṇā / mahākaruṇayā bhagavan bodhisattvānāṃ sarvabuddhadharmāḥ karatalagatā bhavanti / tadyathā bhagavan yena rājñaścakravartinaścakraratnaṃ gacchati tena sarvo balakāyo gacchati, evameva bhagavan yena bodhisattvasya mahākaruṇa gacchati, tena sarve buddhadharmā gacchanti / tadyathā bhagavan jīvitendriye sati anyeṣāmindriyāṇāṃ pravṛttirbhavati, evameva bhagavan mahākaruṇāyāṃ satyāmanyeṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ] dharmāṇāṃ pravṛttirbhavati /" iti /
body.translated_text: Knowing that <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) alone is the root and cause of all qualities of <s>Buddhahood</s>, one should cultivate it from the very beginning. As stated in the <s>Āryadharmasaṃgītisūtra</s>: "Then indeed, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'A <s>bodhisattva</s> need not train in very many <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>. If one <s>dharma</s> is well mastered and fully penetrated by the <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, then all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> come to rest in the palm of his hand. What is that one <s>dharma</s>? It is <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion). Through <s>mahākaruṇā</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> come to rest in the palm of a <s>bodhisattva's</s> hand. Just as, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, wherever the wheel-jewel of a <s>cakravartin</s> king goes, there the entire army follows, even so, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, wherever a <s>bodhisattva's</s> <s>mahākaruṇā</s> goes, there all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> follow. Just as, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, when the life-faculty exists, the other faculties function, even so, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, when <s>mahākaruṇā</s> exists, the other] <s>dharmas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> function."

body.text: āryākṣayamatinirdeśe coktam- "punaraparam, bhadanta śāradvatīputra, bodhisattvānāṃ mahākaruṇāpyakṣayā / tat kasya hetoḥ? pūrvaṅgamatvāt /
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Āryākṣayamatinirdeśa</s> it is said: "Furthermore, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is also inexhaustible. For what reason? Because it is the forerunner.

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma, bhadanta śāradvatīputra, āśvāsāḥ [praśvāsāḥ] puruṣasya jīvitendriyasya pūrvaṅgamāḥ, evameva mahāyāna-sambhāra-samudāgamāya bodhisattvasya mahākaruṇā pūrvaṅgamā" iti vistaraḥ / āryagayāśīrṣe coktam- "kimārambhā, mañjuśrīḥ, bodhisattvānāṃ caryā, kimadhiṣṭhānā ca? mañjuśrīrāha- mahākaruṇārambhā, devaputra, bodhisattvānāṃ caryā sattvādhiṣṭhānā / "iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: Just as, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, inhalation and exhalation are the forerunners of a person's life-faculty, even so <s>mahākaruṇā</s> is the forerunner of a <s>bodhisattva's</s> accumulation of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> provisions" — and so on in detail. And in the <s>Āryagayāśīrṣa</s> it is said: "What is the basis of <s>bodhisattvas'</s> practice, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, and what is its foundation? <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: <s>Mahākaruṇā</s> is the basis of <s>bodhisattvas'</s> practice, O <s>Devaputra</s>, and sentient beings are its foundation" — and so on in detail.

body.text: tathā hi tayā preryamāṇā bodhisattvāḥ svātmanirapekṣā ekāntena paropakārārthatayā atiduṣkaradīrghakālike 'pi sambhāropārjanapariśrame pravartante / tathā coktam āryaśraddhābalādhāne- "tatra [mahā]karuṇayāpi sarvasattvaparipācanārthaṃ na tat kiñcit sukhopādhānaṃ yanna parityajati / "iti / ato 'tiduṣkare pravartamāno nacireṇaiva sambhārān paripūryāvaśyameva sarvajñapadam adhigacchati / tato buddhadharmāṇāṃ karuṇaiva mūlam / mahākaruṇāparigrahādeva buddhā bhagavanto 'dhigamya sarvajñapadam aśeṣasya jagato 'rtha vikurvāṇāstiṣṭhanta iti nirvāṇāpratiṣṭhāne saiva bhagavatāṃ mahākaruṇā hetuḥ /
body.translated_text: For indeed, impelled by it, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, disregarding their own selves and solely devoted to benefiting others, engage in the labor of accumulating provisions even though it is exceedingly difficult and of long duration. As stated in the <s>Āryaśraddhābalādhāna</s>: "Moreover, through <s>mahākaruṇā</s>, for the sake of maturing all sentient beings, there is no means of happiness that one does not relinquish." Therefore, engaging in what is exceedingly difficult, one swiftly completes the accumulations and inevitably attains the state of <s>sarvajña</s> (omniscience). Thus <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) alone is the root of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. It is through the embrace of <s>mahākaruṇā</s> alone that the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, having attained the state of omniscience, remain manifesting for the benefit of all the world — thus it is <s>mahākaruṇā</s> of the <s>Bhagavāns</s> that is the cause of their non-abiding in <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: sā ca duḥkhitasattvālambanamanaskārabahulīkārato vṛddhim (upayāti) / sarve ca te sattvāstridhātukāvacarāstrividhaduḥkhatayā yathoyogam atyanta duḥkhitā eveti sarveṣveva sattveṣu bhāvanīyam / tathā ca ye tāvannārakāste vividhacirantanadīrghakālikadāhādiduḥkha [nadīṣu] nimagnā eva bhagavatā varṇitāḥ / tathā pretā api duḥsahatīvrakṣuttṛṣādiduḥkha[agni]
body.translated_text: And that [compassion] grows through repeated mental attention directed toward suffering beings. All those beings dwelling in the three realms are, according to their condition, utterly afflicted by the three kinds of suffering — thus one should meditate upon all beings. Among them, those in the hells have been described by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as submerged in the manifold, long-lasting sufferings of burning and the like, enduring for vast periods. Likewise the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), their bodies withered by the torment of unbearable, intense hunger and thirst

body.text: pīḍābhisaṃśoṣitamūrtayastīvraduḥkham anubhavanti / yena varṣaśatenāpyaśuciṃ kheṭapiṇḍanaṃ ca bhoktuṃ na labhanta ityādi varṇitaṃ bhagavatā / tiryañco 'pi paraspara[bhakṣaṇa]krodhavadhahiṃsādibhiranekavidhaṃ duḥkhamanubhavanto dṛśyanta eva / tathā hi kecinnāsikābhedanatāḍāṇabandhanādibhiratantrīkṛtaśarīrāḥ paritaḥ paripīḍayamānāḥ kathamapyanicchanto 'pi atidurvahagurubhārodvahanaparikhinnavapuṣaḥ pariklāmyanti, tathāraṇye 'pi nivasanto 'naparādhāḥ kecit kvacit [artha]to 'nviṣya hanyante / nityaṃ ca bhayavivhalamānasastatastataḥ palāyamānāstiṣṭhantītyaparimitam eṣāṃ duḥkhaṃ dṛśyatta eva / tathā mānuṣye 'pi nārakaṃ duḥkhaṃ dṛśyata eva / atra ye caurādayo 'ṅgacchedaśūlārpaṇodbandhanādibhiḥ kāryanta eva teṣāṃ nārakameva duḥkham / ye ca dāridrayadyupahatāsteṣāṃ pretānāmiva tatkṣuttarṣāḍibhirduḥkham / ye ca bhṛtyādayaḥ parāyattīkṛtātmabhāvāḥ, ye ca balibhirākramya pīḍayante teṣāṃ tiraścāmiva tāḍanāvarodhanādi duḥkham / tathā paryeṣṭikṛtam anyo 'nyadrohopaghātādi kṛtaṃ priyaviprayogāpriyasaṃyogakṛtaṃ cāprameyameṣāṃ duḥkham / ye kvacid īśvarāḥ sukhitā iva lapyante te 'pi viparyavasānasampado vividhakudṛṣṭigahananimagnā nārakādiduḥkhānubhavahetuvividha kleśakarmāṇyupacinvantaḥ prapātasthāstarava iva duḥkhahetau [api] vartamānāḥ paramārthato duḥkhitā eva /
body.translated_text: experience intense suffering. It has been described by the <s>Bhagavān</s> that even in a hundred years they cannot obtain impure food or a morsel of phlegm, and so forth. Animals too are plainly seen experiencing manifold suffering through mutual devouring, rage, slaughter, and injury. For some, their bodies rendered powerless by piercing of the nose, beating, and binding, tormented on all sides, are exhausted despite their unwillingness by carrying unbearably heavy burdens; likewise some, dwelling in the wilderness and having committed no offense, are hunted down and killed for profit. Their minds perpetually agitated by fear, fleeing here and there, they persist — thus the suffering of these beings is plainly seen to be immeasurable. Likewise, in the human realm too, hellish suffering is plainly seen. Those who are subjected to amputation of limbs, impalement on stakes, hanging, and the like by thieves and others — their suffering is verily that of hell-beings. Those afflicted by poverty — their suffering from hunger, thirst, and the like is like that of <s>pretas</s>. Those who are servants and others whose very existence is subject to another's will, and those who are oppressed and crushed by the powerful — their suffering of beating, confinement, and the like is like that of animals. Furthermore, the immeasurable suffering of these beings arises from pursuit of livelihood, from mutual hostility and harm, from separation from the beloved and union with the undesirable. Those who are lords somewhere and appear to be happy — they too, their fortunes ending in reversal, plunged into the thicket of various wrong views, accumulating the manifold <s>kleśa-karmas</s> (affliction-actions) that cause the experience of hellish and other sufferings, standing at a precipice like trees, though situated in the cause of suffering, are in the ultimate sense nothing but sufferers.

body.text: devā api ye tāvat kāmāvacarāste 'pi tīvrakāmāgnisandīptamānasā ākṣiptacittā ivāsvacchacetasaḥ kṣaṇamapi samādhānaṃ cetasāṃ na labhante / teṣāṃ praśamasukhadhanadaridrāṇāṃ kīdṛśaṃ nāma tat sukham? nityacyavanapatanādibhayaśokopahatāḥ kathaṃ sukhitā nāma? ye ca rūpārūpāvacarāste 'pi
body.translated_text: As for the <s>devas</s> (gods), those of the <s>Kāmāvacara</s> (desire realm), their minds ablaze with the fierce fire of desire, their consciousness seized and turbid, cannot attain even a moment's composure of mind. For those who are destitute of the wealth of the happiness of tranquility, what kind of happiness can there be? Afflicted by grief and the fear of constantly falling and declining, how can they be called happy? And those of the <s>Rūpa</s> and <s>Arūpāvacara</s> (form and formless realms) — they too,

body.text: yadi nāma kiyatkālaṃ duḥkhaduḥkhatāṃ vyatītāstathāpyatyantaṃ kāmāvacarāṇām anuśayānām aprahāṇāt teṣāṃ punarapi nārakādivinipātasambhavād vipariṇāmaduḥkham astyeva / sarve nāma devamanuṣyāḥ kleśakarmādipāratantryāt te saṃskāraduḥkhatayā duḥkhitā eva /
body.translated_text: even though for some period they have transcended the suffering of manifest pain, nevertheless, since the latent tendencies of the desire realm have not been abandoned, the possibility of falling again into the hells and other lower states remains, and thus the suffering of change certainly exists for them. All <s>devas</s> and humans, being subject to the power of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s>, and the like — they suffer through the pervasive suffering of conditioned existence.

body.text: tadevaṃ sakalameva jagad duḥkhagnijvālāvalīḍham ityavetya yathā mama duḥkhamapriyaṃ tathānyeṣāmapriyamiti cintayatā sarveṣveva sattveṣu kṛpā bhāvanīyā / prathamaṃ tāvad mitrapakṣeṣu pūrvoktā vividhaduḥkhānubhaveṣvanupaśyatā bhāvanīyā /
body.translated_text: Thus, having understood that the entire world is licked by the flames of the fire of suffering, one should reflect: "Just as suffering is unwelcome to me, so it is unwelcome to others," and cultivate compassion toward all beings. First, one should cultivate it toward those in the category of friends, observing them as experiencing the various sufferings described above.

body.text: tataḥ sattvasamatayā viśeṣamapaśyatānādimati ca saṃsāre na kaścit sattvo yo na me śataśo bandhurabhūditi paricintayatā vyasteṣu bhāvanīyā / yadā mitrapakṣeṣviva vyasteṣu [api] tulyā karuṇā pravṛttā bhavati, tadā śatrupakṣe 'pi tathaiva sattvasamatādimanasikāreṇa bhāvanīyā / yadā ca śatrupakṣe 'pi mitrapakṣavat samapravṛttā bhavati, tadā kramaśo daśasu dikṣu sarvasattveṣu [api] bhāvayet / yadā ca duḥkhitabālapriyeṣviva duḥkhoddharaṇecchākārā svarasavāhinī sarvasattveṣu samapravṛttā kṛpā bhavati, tadā sā niṣpannā bhavati mahākaruṇāvyapadeśaṃ ca labhate / yathā akṣayamatisūtre ca varṇitam / ayaṃ ca kṛpābhāvanākramo bhagavatābhidharmasūtrādau varṇitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, seeing no distinction due to the equality of all beings and reflecting that in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s> there is no being who has not been one's relative a hundred times over, one should cultivate it toward neutral beings. When compassion arises equally toward neutral beings as toward friends, then one should cultivate it toward enemies as well, through the same mental attention to the equality of beings. When it arises equally toward enemies as toward friends, then one should gradually cultivate it toward all beings in the ten directions. When compassion — having the character of wishing to remove suffering, flowing spontaneously — arises equally toward all beings as toward a beloved suffering child, then it has been perfected and receives the designation <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion). As described in the <s>Akṣayamatisūtra</s>. And this method of cultivating compassion has been described by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the <s>Abhidharmasūtra</s> and elsewhere.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ kṛpābhyāsabalāt sakalasattvābhyuddharaṇapratijñayānuttarasamyaksambodhiprārthanākāram ayatnata eva bodhicittamutpadyate / yathoktam āryadaśadharmasūtre- "sattvān atrāṇān aśaraṇān advīpān dṛṣṭvā karuṇāyai cittamupasthāpya yāvadanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayati" iti / yadi nāma parasamādāpanādināpi bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhicittamutpadyate, tathāpi kṛpāvegato yat svayameva bodhisattvasya bodhicittamutpadyate
body.translated_text: Through the power of such sustained practice of compassion, <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) arises effortlessly in the form of aspiration for <s>anuttara-samyak-sambodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening), with the resolve to liberate all beings. As stated in the <s>Āryadaśadharmasūtra</s>: "Having seen beings without protection, without refuge, without shelter, arousing the mind toward compassion, one generates the mind toward <s>anuttara-samyak-sambodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening)." Although <s>bodhicitta</s> may arise in a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> through being inspired by others and the like, nevertheless, when <s>bodhicitta</s> arises spontaneously in a <s>bodhisattva</s> through the force of compassion

body.text: tad bhagavatā āryatathāgatajñānamudrāsamādhau viśiṣṭataratvena varṇitam /
body.translated_text: that has been described by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the <s>Āryatathāgatajñānamudrāsamādhi</s> as being of a superior kind.

body.text: tadetad bodhicittaṃ pratipattivikalamapi saṃsāre mahāphalaṃ bhagavatā varṇitam / tathā coktaṃ maitreyavimokṣe- "tad yathāpi nāma, kulaputra, bhinnamapi vajraratnaṃ sarvam ativiśiṣṭaṃ suvarṇālaṅkāramabhibhavati, vajraratnanāma ca na vijahāti, sarvadāridrayaṃ ca vinivartayati / evameva, kulaputra, pratipattibhinnamapi sarvajñatācittotpādavajraratnaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaguṇasuvarṇālaṅkāram abhibhavati / bodhicittanāma na vijahāti, saṃsārādāridrayaṃ ca vinivartayati" iti /
body.translated_text: This <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening-mind), even when devoid of practice, has been praised by the Blessed One as bearing great fruit in <s>saṃsāra</s>. As it is stated in the <s>Maitreyavimokṣa</s>: 'Just as, O son of good family, even a broken <s>vajra</s>-jewel surpasses all gold ornaments, does not lose the name "<s>vajra</s>-jewel," and removes all poverty — so too, O son of good family, even when the <s>vajra</s>-jewel of the arising of the mind directed toward omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā-cittotpāda</s>) is broken by [lack of] practice, it surpasses the gold ornament of all the qualities of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, does not lose the name "<s>bodhicitta</s>," and removes the poverty of <s>saṃsāra</s>.'

body.text: yo 'pi pāramitāsu sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā śikṣitum asamarthaḥ, tenāpi bodhicittam utpādanīyameva, upāyaparigraheṇa mahāphalatvāt / yathā coktam āryarājāvavādakasūtre- "yāsmāt tvaṃ mahārāja, bahukṛtyo bahukaraṇiyaḥ, asahaḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā dānapāramitāyāṃ śikṣitum, yāvat prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitum / tasmāttarhi tvaṃ mahārāja evameva sambodhau chandaṃ śraddhāṃ prārthanāṃ praṇidhiṃ ca, gacchannapi tiṣṭhannapi niṣaṇṇo 'pi śayāno 'pi jāgradapi bhuñjāno 'pi pibannapi, satatasamitam anusmara, manasikuru bhāvaya / sarvabuddhabodhisattvārya śrāvakapratyekabuddhapṛthagjanānām ātmanaśca atītānāgatapratyutpannāni kuśalamūlāni piṇḍayitvā, anumodasva agrayā anumodanayā / anumodya ca sarvabuddhabodhisattvapratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakāṇāṃ pūjākarmāṇi niryātaya / niryātya ca sarvasattvasādhāraṇāni kuru / tataḥ sarvasattvānāṃ yāvat sarvajñatāpratilambhāya sarvabuddhadharmaparipūraṇāya dine
body.translated_text: Even one who is entirely unable to train in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) in every way should still generate <s>bodhicitta</s>, since it bears great fruit when accompanied by skillful means (<s>upāya</s>). As it is stated in the <s>Āryarājāvavādaka-sūtra</s>: 'Since you, O great king, have many duties and many tasks [and are] unable to train in the <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) in every way, up to training in the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) — therefore, O great king, in just this way, whether going, standing, sitting, lying down, waking, eating, or drinking, constantly and continuously recollect, attend to, and cultivate the aspiration, faith, longing, and resolve for awakening (<s>saṃbodhi</s>). Having gathered together all the roots of merit — past, future, and present — of all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and ordinary beings, as well as your own, rejoice with the supreme rejoicing. Having rejoiced, dedicate the acts of worship to all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>. Having dedicated, make [them] shared among all beings. Then, for the attainment of omniscience by all beings, for the fulfillment of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, three times a day

body.text: traikālyam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmaya / evaṃ khalu tvaṃ mahārāja, pratipanna, san rājyaṃ ca kārayiṣyasi, rājyakṛtyāni ca na hāpayisyasi, [bodhisambhārāṃśca paripūrayiṣyāsi]" / ityādi kamuktvāha- "atha khalu punastvaṃ mahārāja, samyaksambodhicittakuśalamūlavipākena anekakṛtyo deveṣu upapanno 'bhūḥ / anekakṛtyo manuṣyeṣu upapanno 'bhūḥ / sarvāsu ca devamanuṣyopapattiṣu ādhipatyaṃ kārayiṣyasi" / iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: transfer [the merit] to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Thus engaged, O great king, you will govern the kingdom and will not neglect royal duties, [and will fulfill the accumulations for awakening].' And so forth, saying further: 'Moreover, O great king, through the ripening of the root of merit of the mind of perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhicitta</s>), you have been reborn many times among the gods, and many times among humans; and in all rebirths among gods and humans, you will exercise sovereignty.' Thus in detail.

body.text: yat punaḥ pratipattisāraṃ bodhicittaṃ tad atitarāṃ vipulaṃ phalam iti siddhim / ata eva āryavīradattaparipṛcchāyām uktam-
body.translated_text: Now, that <s>bodhicitta</s> whose essence is practice (<s>pratipatti</s>) bears exceedingly vast fruit — this is established. For this very reason, it is stated in the <s>Āryavīradattaparipṛcchā</s>:

children.text: bodhicittād vai yat puṇyaṃ tacca rūpi bhaved yadi /
children.translated_text: If the merit arising from <s>bodhicitta</s> were to take form,
it would fill the entire realm of space and overflow beyond it.
If a person were to fill <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>
with jewels and offer them to the Lords of the World,

body.text:
yaścaikaḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā cittaṃ bodhāya nāmati /
iyaṃ viśiṣyate pūjā yasyā anto na vidyate // iti /
body.translated_text: yet one who, with palms joined, inclines the mind toward awakening — this worship is superior, and its limit cannot be found.

body.text: yathā āryagaṇḍavyūhe varṇitam- "bodhicittaṃ kulaputra! bījabhūtaṃ sarvabuddhadharmāṇām" iti vistaraḥ / tacca bodhicittaṃ dvividhaṃ praṇīdhicittaṃ prasthānacittaṃ ca / āryagaṇḍavyūhe varṇitam, tathā- "rdurlabhāste, kulaputra, sattvāḥ sattvaloke ye 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau praṇidadhati iti / tato 'pi durlabhatamāste sattvā ye 'nuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim abhisamprasthitāḥ" iti / sakalajagato hitāya buddho bhaveyamiti prathamataraṃ prārthanākārā cetanā
body.translated_text: As described in the <s>Āryagaṇḍavyūha</s>: '<s>Bodhicitta</s>, O son of good family, is the seed of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>' — and so forth in detail. And that <s>bodhicitta</s> is of two kinds: the aspiration-mind (<s>praṇidhicitta</s>) and the setting-forth-mind (<s>prasthānacittam</s>). As described in the <s>Āryagaṇḍavyūha</s>: 'Rare, O son of good family, are those beings in the world of beings who aspire to unsurpassed perfect awakening; rarer still are those beings who have set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.' The initial aspiration-like volition (<s>cetanā</s>) [expressed as] 'May I become a <s>Buddha</s> for the benefit of the entire world' —

body.text: tatpraṇidhicittam / yataḥ prabhṛti saṃvaragrahaṇe vartamānāḥ sambhāreṣu dṛśyante tatprasthānacittam /
body.translated_text: that is the aspiration-mind (<s>praṇidhicitta</s>). From the point at which [bodhisattvas], while undertaking the vows (<s>saṃvara</s>), are seen [engaged] in the accumulations [of merit and wisdom] — that is the setting-forth-mind (<s>prasthānacittam</s>).

body.text: saṃvaraśca vijñātapratibalasaṃvarasthitāt kalyāṇamitrāt parato grāhyaḥ / asati pratirūpe grāhake buddhabodhisattvān āmukhīkṛtya yathā mañjuśrīyāmbararājabhūtena bodhicittamutpāditaṃ tathotpādanīyaḥ / evamutpāditabodhicitto bodhisattvaḥ svayameva dānādi dadāti pratipattau prayokṣyate, na hi svayamadāntaḥ parān damayatīti mattvā / na cāpi vinā pratipattyā bodhiravāpyate / yathoktam āryagayāśīrṣe- "pratipattisārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ bodhirnāpratipattisārāṇām" iti / āryasamādhirāje coktam- "tasmāt pratipattisāro bhaviṣyāmi ityevaṃ tvayā kumāra, śikṣitavyam / tat kasya hetoḥ? pratipattisārasya hi, kumāra, na durlabhā bhavatyanutarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ" iti /
body.translated_text: The vow (<s>saṃvara</s>) should be received from a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) who is established in the vow and whose capacities are known. In the absence of a suitable recipient, one should generate <s>bodhicitta</s> facing the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, just as <s>Mañjuśrī</s> generated <s>bodhicitta</s> when he was [the king] <s>Ambarā</s>. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has thus generated <s>bodhicitta</s> engages in practice, himself giving generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and so forth, thinking: 'One who has not tamed himself cannot tame others.' Nor is awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) attained without practice. As stated in the <s>Āryagayāśīrṣa</s>: 'Awakening [belongs] to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> whose essence is practice, not to those whose essence is not practice.' And in the <s>Āryasamādhirāja</s> it is stated: 'Therefore, O prince, you should train [thinking] "I shall be one whose essence is practice." For what reason? For one whose essence is practice, O prince, unsurpassed perfect awakening is not difficult to attain.'

body.text: sā ca pratipattirbodhisattvasya pāramitāpramāṇasaṅgrahavastvādibhedena akṣayamatiratnameghādisūtreṣu vistareṇa varṇitā / tathā laukikaśilpādisthāneṣvapi yāvad bodhisattvena śikṣitavyam / kiṃ punarlokottareṣu dhyānādiṣu / anyathā kathaṃ sarvākāraṃ sattvārthaṃ kuryuḥ / sā ceyaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa bodhiattvasya prajñopāyarūpā pratipattirna prajñāmātraṃ nopāyamātram / yathā āryavimalakirtinirdeśe- "prajñārahita upāya upāyarahitā ca prajñā bodhisattvānāṃ bandhanam" ityuktam / upāyasahitā prajñā prajñāsahitā upāyo mokṣatvena varṇitaḥ / āryagayāśīrṣe coktam- "dvāvimau bodhisattvānāṃ saṃkṣiptau mārgau / dvābhyāṃ mārgābhyāṃ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ
body.translated_text: That practice of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in its divisions of <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), means of gathering [disciples] (<s>saṅgrahavastu</s>), and so forth, has been described in detail in the <s>Akṣayamati-</s>, <s>Ratnamegha-</s>, and other <s>sūtras</s>. Likewise, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train even in worldly fields such as crafts and the like — how much more so in supramundane [attainments] such as <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and so forth! Otherwise, how could they accomplish the benefit of beings in all its aspects? And this practice of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in brief, takes the form of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) — not wisdom alone, nor skillful means alone. As stated in the <s>Āryavimalakīrtinirdeśa</s>: 'Skillful means devoid of wisdom, and wisdom devoid of skillful means — these are bondage for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.' Wisdom accompanied by skillful means and skillful means accompanied by wisdom are praised as liberation. And in the <s>Āryagayāśīrṣa</s> it is stated: 'These are the two paths of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in brief. Endowed with [these] two paths, <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> will swiftly attain unsurpassed

body.text: samyaksaṃbodhim abhisambhotsyante / katamau dvau, upāyaśca prajñā ca / "iti /
body.translated_text: perfect awakening. What are the two? Skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>).'

body.text: tatra prajñāpāramitāṃ tyaktvā dānādipāramitāsaṅgrahavastvādikaṃ sarvameva kṣetrapariśuddhimahābhoga[bahu] parivārasampatsattvaparipākanirmāṇādikasakalābhyudayadharmasaṅgrāhakaṃ kuśalam upāya ucyante / prajñā tu tasyaiva copāyasyāviparītasvabhāvaparicchedahetuḥ / tayā hi samyagupāyaṃ vivicyāviparyasto yathāvat svaparārthānuṣṭhānād viṣamiva mantraparigṛhītaṃ bhuñjāno na saṃkliśyate / tathā coktamatraiva sutre- "upāyaḥ saṅgrahajñānam prajñā paricchedajñānam /" iti / āryaśraddhābalādhāne coktam- "upāyakauśalaṃ katamam? yat saṅgrahaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ / prajñā katamā? yat sarvadharmāṇām asambhadena kauśalam" iti / etau prajñopāyau dvāvapi sarvakālameva sevanīyau bhūmipraviṣṭairapi na tu prajñāmātraṃ nopāyamātram / yataḥ sarvāsveva daśasu bhūmiṣu bodhisattvasya pāramitāsamudācāraḥ paṭhito dadhabhūmikādau "na ca pariśeṣāsu na samudācarati" iti vacanāt /
body.translated_text: Therein, leaving aside the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), all the rest — the <s>pāramitās</s> of <s>dāna</s> (giving) and so forth, the means of gathering [disciples], and the like — all that wholesome [activity] which encompasses the complete collection of prosperity-<s>dharmas</s> such as the purification of [buddha-]fields, great enjoyment, abundance of retinue, the ripening of beings, miraculous display, and so forth — [all this] is called skillful means (<s>upāya</s>). Wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), on the other hand, is the cause of the correct discernment of the non-erroneous nature of that very skillful means. For by correctly discerning the skillful means through [wisdom], one who carries out the benefit of self and others properly and without error — like one who eats poison that has been rendered [harmless] by a <s>mantra</s> — is not defiled. As stated in this very <s>sūtra</s>: 'Skillful means is the knowledge of gathering (<s>saṅgraha-jñāna</s>); wisdom is the knowledge of discernment (<s>pariccheda-jñāna</s>).' And in the <s>Āryaśraddhābalādhāna</s> it is stated: 'What is skill in means? That which is the gathering of all <s>dharmas</s>. What is wisdom? That which is skill in the non-attachment to all <s>dharmas</s>.' These two — wisdom and skillful means — should both be cultivated at all times, even by those who have entered the [bodhisattva] stages (<s>bhūmi</s>) — not wisdom alone, nor skillful means alone. For the practice of all the <s>pāramitās</s> by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is taught in each and every one of the ten stages, as stated in the beginning with the <s>Dadabhūmika</s> (Tenth Stage) and elsewhere: 'And [the bodhisattva] does not fail to practice the remaining [perfections].'

body.text: aṣṭamyāṃ ca bhūmau bodhisattvasya śāntavihāriṇo buddhairvyuttthānaṃ tad virudhyeta / tacca tatastatra pāṭhād avagantavyam / [tathā coktaṃ tatraiva sūtre] "tasya khalu bho jinaputra, bodhisattvasya evamimāmacalāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanugatasya pūrvapraṇidhānabalādhānasthitasya buddhā bhagavantastasmin dharmamukhastrotasi tathāgatajñānopasaṃhāraṃ kurvanti / evaṃ caina bruvanti- sādhu
body.translated_text: And on the eighth stage (<s>bhūmi</s>), the <s>Buddhas</s> rouse the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who abides in quiescence — [otherwise] that [quiescence] would be contrary [to the bodhisattva path]. This should be understood from the reading in that very [text]. [As stated in that same sūtra:] 'When, O son of the Conqueror, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has entered this immovable (<s>acalā</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stage, established by the power of his former aspirations, the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, bring about in him the application of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge in that stream of <s>Dharma</s>-doors. And they address him thus: "Well done,

body.text: sādhu kulaputra / eṣā paramārthakṣāntirbuddhadharmānugamāya / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra, yā asmākaṃ daśabalacaturvaiśāradyabuddhadharmasamṛddiḥ, sā tava nāsti / tasyā buddhadharmasamṛddheḥ paryeṣaṇāya abhiyogaṃ kuru, vīryamārabhasva / etadeva kṣāntimukhaṃ monmokṣīḥ / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra, kiṃ cāpi tvayaivaṃ śāntavimokṣavihāro 'nuprāptaḥ, imān punaraśāntānapraśāntān bālapṛthagjanān nānākleśasamudācāraprāptān vividhavitarkopahatamānasān samanvāhara, apekṣasva / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra, pūrvapraṇidhānamanusmara sattvārthasaṃprāpaṇaṃ jñānamukhācintyatāṃ ca / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra, eṣā sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmatā / utpādādvā tathāgatānāmanutpādādvā sthitaivaiṣā dharmatā dharmadhātusthitiḥ yadidaṃ sarvadharmaśūnyatā sarvadharmānupalabdhiḥ / naitayā tathāgatā eva kevalaṃ prabhāvyante, sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhā api hyetāmavikalpadharmatāmanuprāpnuvanti /
body.translated_text: Well done, son of good family! This is the <s>paramārthakṣānti</s> (ultimate forbearance) for following the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. But furthermore, son of good family, the wealth of <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> that we possess—the ten powers, four fearlessnesses—that you do not have. Exert yourself in seeking that wealth of <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, arouse vigor! Do not release this gateway of forbearance alone. But furthermore, son of good family, although you have attained the abiding in peaceful liberation, consider and look upon these unpeaceful, unquieted, foolish ordinary beings who have arrived at the arising of manifold <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), whose minds are afflicted by various wrong conceptions. But furthermore, son of good family, remember your former vows, the accomplishment of the welfare of beings, and the inconceivable gateways of knowledge. But furthermore, son of good family, this is the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all <s>dharmas</s>. Whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or not, this <s>dharmatā</s> remains established, the abiding of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), namely the <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of all <s>dharmas</s>, the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. It is not by this alone that <s>Tathāgatas</s> are distinguished; all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> also attain this non-conceptual <s>dharmatā</s>.

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra, prekṣasva tāvat tvamasmākaṃ kāyāpramāṇatāṃ ca jñānāpramāṇatāṃ ca buddhakṣetrāpramāṇatāṃ ca jñānābhinirhārāpramāṇatāṃ ca prabhāmaṇḍalāpramāṇatāṃ ca svarāṅgaviśuddhayapramāṇatāṃ ca / tathaiva tvamapyabhinirhāramutpādaya / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra, ekastveṣa āloko yo 'yaṃ sarvadharmānirvikalpālokaḥ / īdṛśāstu kulaputra, dharmālokāstathāgatānāmaparyantagatā aparyantakṛtā aparyantabaddhāḥ, yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā nāsti, gaṇanā, pramāṇamupaniṣadaupamyaṃ nāsti, tesāmadhigamāya abhinirhāramutpādaya / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra, prekṣasva tāvad daśasu dikṣu apramāṇakṣetratāṃ ca apramāṇasattvatāṃ ca apramāṇadharmavibhaktitāṃ ca / tatsarvamanugaṇaya / yathāvattayā abhinirhāramutpādaya / "iti hi bho jinaputra, te buddhā bhagavanta
body.translated_text: But furthermore, son of good family, behold now our immeasurability of body, immeasurability of knowledge, immeasurability of <s>buddha-kṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), immeasurability of knowledge-manifestation, immeasurability of the halo of radiance, and immeasurability of the purity of voice and limbs. Generate aspiration in the same way yourself. But furthermore, son of good family, this is but one light—this light of non-conceptual illumination of all <s>dharmas</s>. But, son of good family, the lights of <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are of limitless extent, limitless accomplishment, limitless scope, of which there is no count, no reckoning, no measure, no comparison, no analogy—generate aspiration for the realization of those. But furthermore, son of good family, behold now in the ten directions the immeasurability of fields, immeasurability of beings, and immeasurability of the diversity of <s>dharma</s>. Comprehend all of that. Generate aspiration accordingly." Thus indeed, O son of the <s>Jina</s>, those blessed <s>Buddhas</s>

body.text: evaṃ bhūmyanugatasya bodhisattvasya evaṃ pramukhānyaprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni jñānābhinirhāramukhānyupasaṃharanti, yairjñānābhinirhāramukhairbodhisattvo 'pramāṇajñānavibhaktito 'bhinirhārakarmābhiniṣpadayati / ' ārocayāmi te bho jinaputra, prativedayāmi / te ced buddhā bhagavantastaṃ bodhisattvamevaṃ sarvajñajñānābhinirhāramukheṣu nāvatārayeyustadevāsya parinirvāṇaṃ bhavetsarvasattvakāryapratiprasrabdhiśca /" iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: bring forth to the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has progressed through the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) such innumerable, incalculable gateways of knowledge-manifestation, by which gateways of knowledge-manifestation the <s>bodhisattva</s> accomplishes the work of manifestation through immeasurable divisions of knowledge. 'I declare to you, O son of the <s>Jina</s>, I make known: if those blessed <s>Buddhas</s> were not to introduce that <s>bodhisattva</s> into these gateways of all-knowing knowledge-manifestation, that would be his <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and the abandonment of the welfare of all beings." Thus in detail.

body.text: yacca āryavimalakīrtinirdeśe gayāśīrṣe coktaṃ tadapi pūrvoktaṃ virudhyate, evaṃ sāmānyenaiva tatrābhidhānāt / yat sarvadharmasaṅgrahavaipulye coktaṃ tadapi virudhyate / eva / tatroktam- "sūkṣmaṃ hi mañjuśrīḥ, saddharmapratikṣepakarmāvaraṇam / yo hi kaścinmañjuśrīḥ, tathāgatabhāṣite dharma ekasmin śobhanasaṃjñām utpādayati / ekasminnaśobhasaṃjñām utpādayati / sa saddharmaṃ pratikṣipati / tena saddharmaṃ pratikṣipatā tathāgato 'bhyākhyāto bhavati" iti vistaram uktvā āha- "yo 'yaṃ maitreya, ṣaṭpāramitāsamudāgamo bodhisattvānāṃ bodhāya taṃ te mohapuruṣā evaṃ vakṣyanti / prajñāpāramitāyāmeva bodhisattvena śikṣitavyam, kiṃ śeṣābhiḥ pāramitābhiriti / te 'nyā mupāyapāramitāṃ dūṣayitavyāṃ manyante / tat kiṃ manyase, ajita! duṣprajñaḥ sa kāśirājo 'bhūd yena kapotārtha śyenāya svamāṃsāni dattāni? maitreya āha, no hīdam, bhagavan / bhagavānāha- yāni mayā maitreya, bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā ṣaṭpāramitāsaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlānyupacitāni / apakṛtaṃ nu taiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ? maitreya āha- no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavān āha, tvaṃ tāvad ajita, dānāpāramitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṃ kalpān samudāgataḥ / yāvat prajñāpāramitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṃ kalpān samudāgataḥ, tat te mohapuruṣā evaṃ vakṣyanti- ekanayenaiva
body.translated_text: And what was said in the <s>Ārya-Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s> and at <s>Gayāśīrṣa</s>, that too contradicts the aforementioned [one-sided view], since it is stated there in a general manner. What was said in the <s>Sarvadharmasaṅgrahavaipulya</s>, that too contradicts [it]. Indeed. There it is stated: "Subtle indeed, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the karmic obstruction of rejecting the true <s>Dharma</s>. For whoever, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, generates the perception of 'good' regarding one <s>dharma</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> and generates the perception of 'not good' regarding another, he rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. By rejecting the true <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is slandered." Having stated this in detail, it says: "That which, <s>Maitreya</s>, is the full accomplishment of the six <s>pāramitās</s> for the awakening of <s>bodhisattvas</s>—those deluded men will say thus: 'A <s>bodhisattva</s> should train only in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; what is the use of the other <s>pāramitās</s>?' They think the other <s>upāya-pāramitā</s> (perfection of skillful means) should be deprecated. What do you think, <s>Ajita</s>? Was that king of <s>Kāśī</s> of poor wisdom, who gave his own flesh to the hawk for the sake of the pigeon? <s>Maitreya</s> said: No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: <s>Maitreya</s>, the roots of merit connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s> that I accumulated while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> path—were those roots of merit harmful? <s>Maitreya</s> said: No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: You yourself, <s>Ajita</s>, completed sixty <s>kalpas</s> in <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), and likewise sixty <s>kalpas</s> in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>—yet those deluded men will say: 'Awakening is by one approach alone,

body.text: bodhiryaduta śūnyatānayena" iti vistaraḥ / vairocanābhisambodhau coktam- 'tadetat sarvajñajñānaṃ karuṇāmūlaṃ bodhicittahetukam upāyaparyavasānam" iti / tasmādubhayaṃ sarvakālameva bodhisattvena sevanīyam /
body.translated_text: namely the approach of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness).'" Thus in detail. And in the <s>Vairocanābhisambodhi</s> it is said: 'That all-knowing knowledge has compassion as its root, <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind) as its cause, and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) as its culmination.' Therefore both [<s>prajñā</s> and <s>upāya</s>] must be cultivated by the <s>bodhisattva</s> at all times.

body.text: evaṃ hi bhagavatām apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇaṃ sidhyati / tathā hi dānāderūpāyasya rūpakāyakṣetraparivārādimahābhogatāphalasampatparigrahād bhagavatāṃ na nirvāṇe 'vasthānam / prajñayā ca sakalaviparyāsaprahāṇād na saṃsāre 'vasthānaṃ viparyāsamūlatvāt saṃsārasya / anyā ca prajñopāyasvarūpayā pratipadā samāropāpavādāntavivarjanena madhyamā pratipad udbhāvitā / prajñayā samāropāntasya varjanād upāyenāpavādāntasya varjanāt / ata eva āryadharmasaṅgītāvuktam- "lakṣaṇānuvyañjanarūpakāyapariniṣpādanābhirataśca bhavati, na dharmakāyābhisamayamātrābhirataḥ" iti / punaruktam- "prajñopāyajanitastathāgatānāṃ parapratyayataḥ saṃbhavo 'nugantavyaḥ" iti /
body.translated_text: For thus is the <s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s> (non-abiding nirvāṇa) of the Blessed Ones accomplished. For through <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) such as giving and so forth, by embracing the fruition of great enjoyment—the magnificent body, field, retinue, and so on—the Blessed Ones do not remain in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), by the abandonment of all distorted views, they do not remain in <s>saṃsāra</s>, since <s>saṃsāra</s> has distorted views as its root. Moreover, the practice that has the nature of both <s>prajñā</s> and <s>upāya</s> is proclaimed as the middle path, by avoiding the extremes of superimposition and denial. Through <s>prajñā</s>, the extreme of superimposition is avoided; through <s>upāya</s>, the extreme of denial is avoided. Therefore it is stated in the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṅgīti</s>: "One should delight in the perfection of the form body with its marks and minor marks, not merely in the realization of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>." And again it is stated: "The arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s> from the conditions of others, born of <s>prajñā</s> and <s>upāya</s>, should be understood."

body.text: yat punaruktam- "kolopamaṃ dharmaparyāyam ājānadbhirdharmā eva prahātavyāḥ, prāg evādharmāḥ" iti / tad viparītābhiniveśaprahāṇataḥ prahātavyā ityabhiprāyāduktam, na tu prayojanasampadanārthamapi nāśrayaṇiyam / tathā coktam- "dharmaḥ pragrahītavyo nodgrahītavyaḥ" iti / nonmārgeṇa pragrahītavya ityarthaḥ / yaccāpi kvacid dānādi sāṃsārikaphalatvena varṇitaṃ tat prajñārahitānāṃ dānādīnāṃ pūrvam uktaṃ tāvanmātrakuśalamūlasantuṣṭāṃścādhikṛtyottara kuśalamūle protsāhanārtham / anyathā [ārya-]vimalakīrtinīrdeśaḥ [ādi pūrvoktaḥ] sarva eva virudhyate / tasmāttu dvāvapi prajñopāyau sevanīyāviti sthitam /
body.translated_text: As for what was stated: "Those who understand the <s>Dharma</s> discourse as a raft should abandon even <s>dharmas</s>, how much more non-<s>dharmas</s>"—that was said with the intention that they should be abandoned through the abandonment of distorted attachment, not that one should not rely on them even for accomplishing their purpose. And thus it is stated: "The <s>Dharma</s> should be grasped, not seized." The meaning is: it should not be grasped through the wrong path. And although in some places giving and so forth are described as having <s>saṃsāric</s> fruits, that was said regarding giving and so forth devoid of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), as previously explained, and for the purpose of encouraging those who are content with merely that measure of merit toward higher roots of merit. Otherwise, the <s>Ārya-Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s> and the other [sūtras] previously mentioned would all be contradicted. Therefore it is established that both <s>prajñā</s> and <s>upāya</s> must be cultivated.

body.text: tatra prajñāparigṛhītā dānādayaḥ pāramitāvyapadeśaṃ labhante nānyatheti / ato dānadipariśuddhaye samādhānam āsthāya prajñopādānārthaṃ yatnaṃ kurvīta /
body.translated_text: Therein, giving and the other [perfections] accompanied by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) receive the designation '<s>pāramitā</s>' (perfection), and not otherwise. Therefore, for the purification of giving and the rest, one should apply oneself to concentration and strive for the acquisition of <s>prajñā</s>.

body.text: tatra prathamaṃ tāvat śrutamayī prajñotpādanīyā / tayā hi tāvad āgamārtham avadhārayati / tataścintāmayyā prajñayānītaneyārthaṃ nirvedhayati / tatastayā niścitya bhūtamarthaṃ bhāvayennābhūtam / anyathā hi viparītasyāpi bhavānād vicikitsāyāścāvyapagamāt samyagjñānodayo na syāt / tataśca vyarthaiva bhāvanā syāt / yathā tīrtīkānām / uktaṃ ca bhagavatā samādhirāje-
body.translated_text: Therein, first of all, <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of hearing) should be generated. For by that, one first ascertains the meaning of scripture. Then, by <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of reflection), one penetrates the meaning of what has been set forth. Then, having ascertained the true meaning by that [reflective wisdom], one should meditate on the real, not the unreal. For otherwise, from meditating on what is distorted and from the non-removal of doubt, the arising of right knowledge would not occur. And then meditation would be utterly fruitless—as is the case with the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist practitioners). And the Blessed One said in the <s>Samādhirāja</s>:

body.text:
nairātmyadharmān yadi pratyavekṣate tān pratyavekṣya yadi bhāvayet /
sa heturnirvāṇaphalasya prāptaye yo anyaheturna sa bhoti śāntaye // iti /
body.translated_text:
If one examines the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness), and having examined them, meditates upon them—
that is the cause for attaining the fruit of <s>nirvāṇa</s>; no other cause leads to peace.

body.text: tasmāccintāmayyā prajñayā yuktayāgamābhyāṃ pratyavekṣya bhūtameva vastusvarūpaṃ bhāvanīyam / vastūnāṃ svarūpaṃ ca paramārthato 'nutpāda evāgamato yuktitaśca niścitam /
body.translated_text: Therefore, having examined through <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of reflection), by reasoning and scripture, one should meditate on the true nature of things alone. And the own-nature of things is ultimately determined as <s>anutpāda</s> (non-arising) itself, both from scripture and from reasoning.

body.text: tatrāgamato yathoktam āryadharmasaṅgītau- "anutpādaḥ satyamasatyam anye dharmāḥ" iti / etacca paramārthānukūlatvād anutpādaḥ satyamityuktam / paramārthatastu notpādo nāpyanutpādaḥ, tasy sarvyavahārātītatvāt / punaścātraiva coktam- "utpādanirodhābhiniviṣṭaḥ kulaputra, lokasanniveśaḥ,
body.translated_text: Therein, from scripture, as stated in the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṅgīti</s>: "<s>Anutpāda</s> (non-arising) is truth; other <s>dharmas</s> are untruth." And this is said—'non-arising is truth'—because it accords with ultimate reality. But ultimately there is neither arising nor non-arising, since that [ultimate] transcends all conventional expression. And again in the same [text] it is stated: "Son of good family, the worldly convention is fixated on arising and cessation.

body.text: tasmāt tathāgato mahākāruṇiko lokasyottrāsapadaparihārāthaṃ vyavahāravaśād uktavān, utpadyate nirudhyate ceti na cātra kasyacid dharmasyotpādaḥ" iti / aryabuddhasaṅgītau coktam- "katamā yoniśaḥ pṛcchā, katamā yoniḥ? āha anutpādo yoniḥ, tasya pṛcchā yoniśaḥ pṛccha" / punaratraivoktam- "cakāramukhaḥ sarvadharmāścyutyutpattivigatāḥ / abhāvamukhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ, svabhāvaśūnyatām upādāya" iti / āryasatyadvayavibhāge cānutpādasamatayā sarvadharmāṇāṃ samatā bhavati / prajñāpāramitāyāṃ coktam- "rūpaṃ subhūte, rūpasvabhāvena śūnyam, yāvad vijñānaṃ vijñānasvabhāvena śūnyamiti svalakṣaṇaśūnyatām upādāya" iti / hastikakṣye coktam-
body.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, out of great compassion, in order to remove the grounds of terror for the world, spoke in accordance with conventional usage, saying 'it arises' and 'it ceases,' but there is no arising of any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever." And in the <s>Ārya-buddhasaṅgīti</s> it is said: "What is proper inquiry? What is the source? He replied: non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>) is the source; inquiry into that is proper inquiry." And again in the same text it is said: "Through the syllable 'ca,' all <s>dharmas</s> are free from passing away and arising. All <s>dharmas</s> have non-existence as their entrance, inasmuch as they are empty of own-nature (<s>svabhāva-śūnyatā</s>)." And in the <s>Ārya-satyadvaya-vibhāga</s>, the sameness of all <s>dharmas</s> obtains through the sameness of non-arising. And in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> it is said: "Form, <s>Subhūti</s>, is empty of the own-nature of form; likewise consciousness is empty of the own-nature of consciousness" — this is said with reference to emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā</s>). And in the <s>Hastikakṣya</s> it is said:

body.text:
na kaścillabhyate bhāvo yasyotpādasya saṃbhavaḥ /
asaṃbhaveṣu dharmeṣu bālaḥ sambhavamicchati // iti /
body.translated_text:
No entity whatsoever is found for which arising is possible;
regarding <s>dharmas</s> that have no origination, the fool desires origination.

body.text: pitāputrasamāgame coktam- "sarva ete dharmāḥ sarve samāstraikālyasamatayā / atīte 'dhvani sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvarahitā yāvat pratyutpanne 'dhvani" iti / evaṃ tavad āgamataḥ pratyavekṣaṇīyam / yuktyā hi sthirīkṛtasyāgamārthasyānyairapohitam aśakyatvāt / ato yuktyāpi pratyavekṣanīyam /
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Pitāputra-samāgama</s> it is said: "All these <s>dharmas</s> are all equal through the sameness of the three times. In the past time all <s>dharmas</s> are devoid of own-nature, and likewise in the present time." Thus, first one should investigate by means of scripture (<s>āgama</s>). For since the meaning of scripture, once established by reasoning (<s>yukti</s>), cannot be refuted by others, one should also investigate by means of reasoning.

body.text: tatra saṃkṣepato yuktirucyate / utpādo bhāvānāmahetuko vā syāt sahetuko vā / na tāvad ahetukaḥ kādācitkatvadarśanāt / kāraṇānapekṣā hi viśeṣābhāvād utpādakālavat sadā sarvatraiva ca bhāvāḥ kiṃ na bhaveyuḥ / abhāvakālād aviśeṣād vā utpādakāle 'pi naiva bhaveyuḥ / evaṃ tāvanna nirhetuko yuktaḥ / nāpi sahetukaḥ / tathā hi yastāvadīśvarādistīrthikairnityo hetuḥ kalpitastato bhāvā na jāyante krameṇotpādadarśanāt / na
body.translated_text: Therein, reasoning is stated in brief. The arising of entities would be either without cause or with cause. First, it is not without cause, because arising is observed only occasionally. For if things were independent of causes, then since there would be no distinguishing factor, why would entities not exist always and everywhere, just as at the time of arising? Or, since there is no difference from the time of non-existence, they should not exist even at the time of arising. Thus, causeless arising is not reasonable. Nor is arising with cause reasonable. For consider: the eternal cause postulated by the <s>tīrthikas</s> such as <s>Īśvara</s> and so forth — entities are not born from that, because arising is observed to occur sequentially. And

body.text: tvavikalakāraṇasya [phalasya] krameṇotpādo yukto nirapekṣatvāt / nāpīśvarādeḥ svayaṃ samarthasya parāpekṣāḥ / nityatvena parairanupakāryatvāt / anupakāriṇi cāpekṣāyogāt / ata eveśvarādīnāṃ sarvasāmarthyaśūnyatvād vandhyāpūtrādivad niḥsvabhāvatvameva / arthakriyāsamarthatvād vastunaḥ / teṣāṃ kvacidapi kārye na krameṇa sāmarthyaṃ yathā vicāritam / nāpi yaugapadyena, tathā hi sarvakāryaṃ sakṛd utpādyoktarakāle 'pi yadyutpattisamartha evāsau tadā punarapi samarthasvabhāvānuvṛttau pūrvavat kāryotpattiprasaṅgaḥ / ananuvṛttau vā pūrvasvabhāvaparityāgād anityatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: sequential arising of an effect from a cause whose conditions are complete is not reasonable, because it is independent of anything further. Nor does <s>Īśvara</s> and the like, being capable in itself, have dependence on others, because being eternal, it cannot be assisted by others; and dependence on that which does not assist is illogical. For this very reason, <s>Īśvara</s> and the like, being devoid of all capacity, are without own-nature, just like the son of a barren woman, since a real entity must be capable of producing effects. Their capacity for any effect whatsoever does not obtain sequentially, as has been analyzed. Nor does it obtain simultaneously, for if all effects were produced at once, and if at a later time too it were still capable of producing, then since its capable nature persists as before, there would be the absurd consequence of the same effects arising again. Or if it did not persist, then since the former nature would be abandoned, there would be the absurd consequence of impermanence.

body.text: tasmānna nityaṃ nāma kiñcid vastu vidyate / ata evoktaṃ bhagavatā- "asatsamāropaḥ punarmahāmate! ākāśanirodhanirvāṇa[ādi]akṛtakabhāvābhiniveśasamāropaḥ" iti / tasmānna nityād eṣāmutpādo yuktaḥ / nāpyanityāttatrātītānāgatayoravastutvānn tāvattato janma yuktam ahetukatvaprasaṅgāt / nāpi vartamānāt, samānāsamānakālayostata utpādāyogāt / tathā hi na tāvat samānakālaṃ kāraṇaṃ svabhāvavat kāryasyāpi tatsamānakālabhāvitayā niṣpannatvāt / nāpi bhinnakālam, kālantaravyavadhānenotpāde 'tītāderevotpattiprasaṅgāt / avyavadhānenāpyutpāde sarvātmānā yadyavyavadhāṇaṃ tadaikasminneva kṣaṇe sarvakṣaṇānām anupraveśāt kalpasya kṣaṇamātratāprasaṅgaḥ / yathā paramāṇoḥ sarvātmanā saṃyogo piṇḍasyāṇumātratāprasaṅgaḥ / athaikadeśanena, tadā kṣaṇasya sāvayavatvaprasaṅgaḥ / svato 'pi notpadyante, nirhetukapakṣeṇaivāsya pakṣasya saṅgṛhītatvāt svātmani ca kāritravirodhāt / nāpyubhayataḥ ubhayapakṣabhāvidoṣadvaya [saṅgraha]prasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: Therefore, no entity whatsoever that is eternal exists. Thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: "The superimposition of what is unreal, <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the superimposition of attachment to uncreated entities such as space, cessation, and <s>nirvāṇa</s>." Therefore, arising of these from an eternal cause is not reasonable. Nor is arising from an impermanent cause reasonable: First, arising from the past and future is not reasonable, since they lack real existence — the absurd consequence of causelessness would follow. Nor from the present, because arising from it is impossible whether simultaneous or non-simultaneous. For a cause that is simultaneous and possesses own-nature — the effect too, being existent at that same time, is already accomplished. Nor at a different time, because if arising occurred with an interval of time, there would be the absurd consequence of arising even from the past and so forth. And if arising occurred without interval, then if the absence of interval were complete, all moments would merge into a single moment, leading to the absurd consequence that a cosmic age (<s>kalpa</s>) would be a mere moment — just as complete contact of an atom on all sides leads to the absurd consequence that an aggregate would be merely atom-sized. But if partial, then there would be the absurd consequence that a moment has parts. Nor do things arise from themselves, because this position is subsumed under the causeless position, and because self-causation is contradictory. Nor from both, because the absurd consequence follows of incurring the faults of both positions.

body.text: tasmāt paramārthato 'nutpannā evāmī bhāvāḥ / saṃvṛtyā tūtpādasya vidyamānatvānnāgamādivirodhaḥ / tathā coktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: Therefore, in the ultimate sense, these entities are entirely unarisen. But since arising exists conventionally, there is no contradiction with scripture and the rest. And thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said:

body.text:
bhāvā vidyanti saṃvṛtyā paramārthe na bhāvakāḥ /
niḥsvabhāveṣu yā bhrāntistatsatyaṃ saṃvṛtirbhavet // iti /
body.translated_text:
Entities exist conventionally; in the ultimate sense they are not entities.
That delusion which occurs regarding things without own-nature — that is what is called conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛti</s>).

body.text: iyaṃ ca yuktirbhagavato 'bhipretā śālistambādau / svataḥ parata ubhābhyām ahetośca janmaniṣedhāt /
body.translated_text: This reasoning is intended by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the <s>Śālistamba</s> and other texts, through the negation of arising from self, from other, from both, and from no cause.

body.text: athavā evaṃ yuktyā vicārayet / dvividhā bhāvā rūpiṇo 'rūpiṇaśca / tatrāpi tāvad rūpiṇo ghatādayaste 'ṇuśo vibhinnarūpatvād naikasvabhāvāḥ / aṇūnāṃ pūrvāparasthitānāṃ pūrvādidigbhāgatvena vibhidyamānānām asiddhāvapyaṇusaṃcayātmakatve nānekasvabhāvo yuktaḥ, na caikānekasvabhāvavyatirekeṇāparaḥ kaścid bhāvasvabhāvo 'stīti niḥsvabhāvā evāmī paramārthataḥ svapnādyupalabdharūpādivad rūpiṇo bhavāḥ / etacca bhagavataiva coktam āryalaṅkāvatāre- "goviṣāṇāṃ punarmahāmate, aṇuśo 'pi vibhidyamānaṃ nāvatiṣṭhate / punarapyaṇavo 'pi bhidyamānā aṇutvalakṣaṇena nāvatiṣṭhante" iti /
body.translated_text: Alternatively, one may investigate by reasoning in this way. Entities are of two kinds: those having form (<s>rūpin</s>) and those without form (<s>arūpin</s>). Among these, first, material entities such as pots and the like — since when divided into atoms they have distinct forms — do not have a unitary own-nature. And when atoms, positioned successively, are divided by their directional parts such as east and so forth, even if their atomic aggregate nature is unestablished, a manifold own-nature is not reasonable. And since there is no other nature of an entity apart from being either unitary or manifold, these material entities are without own-nature in the ultimate sense, like form and so forth apprehended in dreams. And this has been stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself in the <s>Ārya-laṅkāvatāra</s>: "A cow's horn, <s>Mahāmati</s>, when divided into atoms does not stand as anything; and the atoms too, when further divided, do not stand as having the characteristic of atomicity."

body.text: ye cārupiṇaste 'pi tathaiva vicāryumāṇā niḥsvabhāvā eva / tathā hi, bāhyasya nīlāderarthasyābhāvāt sāmarthyata eva vijñānādayo 'rūpiṇaḥ skandhā nilādirūpeṇa pratibhāsanta ityabhyupeyam / uktaṃ ca bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: And those that are formless (<s>arūpin</s>), when examined in the same way, are likewise without own-nature. For since external objects such as blue and the like do not exist, it must be accepted that the formless aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) such as consciousness and so forth appear in the form of blue and the like merely through their own power. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said:

body.text: "bahirdhā nāsti vairūpaṃ svacittaṃ dṛśyate bahiḥ /" iti /
body.translated_text: "External form does not exist; one's own mind is seen as external."

body.text: tataśca nīlādicitrākāranirbhāsatayā grāhyagrāhakākāranirbhāsatayā naikasvabhāvā
body.translated_text: And therefore, inasmuch as they appear with variegated forms such as blue and the like, and inasmuch as they appear with the forms of apprehended and apprehender (<s>grāhya-grāhaka</s>), they do not have a unitary own-nature

body.text: amī yuktāḥ / na caikasyānekarūpatā yuktimatī, ekānekavirodhāt / ekasya kasyacit svabhāvasyāsiddhāvanekarūpatāpyayuktimatī, ekasamūharūpatvād anekasya /
body.translated_text: — this is reasonable. For it is not reasonable that a single entity should have manifold forms, because unity and multiplicity are contradictory. And if no single own-nature is established, manifold form is also not reasonable, since multiplicity has the nature of a collection of unities.

body.text: athavā tatrālīkā evāmī rūpādaya ākārāḥ pratibhāsanta ityubyupagamyate, tadā vijñānam apyalīkaṃ prāpnoti / vijñānasya tatsvarūpāvyatirekāt / na hi svayaṃ prakāśamānarūpatāvyatirekeṇānyad vijñānasya rūpamasti / svayaṃ ca na nirbhāsante rūpādayaḥ / teṣāṃ ca vijñānasvarūpāpannānām alīkatve sarvameva vijñānam alīkam abhyupetaṃ syāt / tasmād "māyopamaṃ ca vijñānam" ityuktaṃ bhagavatā /
body.translated_text: Alternatively, if it is accepted that these forms such as blue and the like that appear are entirely unreal, then consciousness too becomes unreal, because consciousness is not different from those very forms. For there is no other form of consciousness apart from the nature of being self-luminous. And forms and the like are not self-luminous. And since those forms, having the nature of consciousness, are unreal, all consciousness whatsoever would be accepted as unreal. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: "Consciousness too is like an illusion (<s>māyopama</s>)."

body.text: tasmād ekānekasvabhāvaśūnyatvena paramārthato 'līkā evāmī sarvabhāvā iti niścitametat / ayaṃ cārtha ukto bhagavatā laṅkāvatāre-
body.translated_text: Therefore, since they are empty of both unitary and manifold own-nature, all these entities are in the ultimate sense entirely unreal — this is established. And this meaning has been stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>:

body.text:
yathaiva darpaṇe rūpam ekatvānyatvavarjitam /
dṛśyate na ca tatrāsti tathā bhāveṣu bhavatā // iti /
body.translated_text:
Just as a reflection in a mirror, devoid of both unity and otherness,
is seen but does not exist therein — so it is with entities, O <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: ekatvānyatvavarjitam iti, ekatvānyatvarahitam ityarthaḥ / punaścoktam-
body.translated_text: "Devoid of unity and otherness" means: free from unity and otherness — that is the meaning. And again it is said:

body.text:
buddhayā vivicyamānānāṃ svabhāvo nāvadhāryate /
ato nirabhilāpyaste niḥsvabhāvāśca darśitāḥ // iti /
body.translated_text:
When analyzed by the intellect, the own-nature of things cannot be ascertained;
therefore they are declared to be inexpressible and without own-nature.

body.text: tadevaṃ cintāmayyā prajñayā niścitya bhūtamartha tasya pratyakṣīkaraṇāya bhāvanāmayīṃ prajñām utpādayet / "bahuśrutādimātrakeṇā nārthaḥ pratyakṣo bhavatīti niveditam āryaratnameghādiṣu / anubhavaśca pratipattṛṇām, na cāpi sphuṭatarajñānālokodayam antareṇa samyagāvaraṇatamo 'pahīyate / bhāvanābahulīkārataścābhūte
body.translated_text: Thus, having ascertained the true nature of reality through analytical wisdom (<s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>), one should generate meditative wisdom (<s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>) in order to realize it directly. "Through mere learning and the like alone, the truth does not become directly perceived" — this has been taught in the <s>Ārya-ratnamegha</s> and other texts. And this is the experience of practitioners: without the arising of the light of clearer and clearer knowledge, the darkness of obscurations is not properly removed. And through the intensification of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), even regarding what is not

body.text: 'pyarthe sphuṭarajñānam utpadyate / yathā aśubhādipṛthvīkṛtsnādisamāpannānāṃ [jñānodbhavatve] kimpunarbhūte / tathā ca bhāvanāyāḥ parisphuṭajñānaphalatvena sāphalyamuktam āryasamādhirāje-
body.translated_text: evident, clearer knowledge arises — just as for those who have attained the meditations on the impure (<s>aśubha</s>), the <s>pṛthvī-kṛtsna</s>, and so forth, knowledge arises — how much more so regarding what is real! And thus the fruitfulness of meditation, in that its result is perfectly clear knowledge, has been stated in the <s>Ārya-samādhirāja</s>:

body.text:
ārocayāmi prativedayāmi vo yathā yathā bahu ca vitarkayennaraḥ /
tathā tathā bhavati tannimittacittastehi vitarkehi tanniśritehi // iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text:
I declare and make known to you: in whatever way and however extensively a person reflects,
in that way and to that extent does their mind become disposed to that object, through those reflections and through reliance upon them. Thus it is explained at length.

body.text: tasmāt tattvaṃ sākṣātkartukāmo bhāvanāyāṃ pravartate /
body.translated_text: Therefore, one who wishes to realize the truth directly engages in meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>).

body.text: tatra prathamataraṃ tāvad yoginā śamatho niṣpādanīyaścittasthirīkaraṇāya / salilavaccañcalatvāccittasya, na śamathamādhāramanteraṇa sthitirasti / na cāsamāhitena cetasā yathābhutaṃ śakyate jñātum / uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- "samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti" iti / śamatho lābhādikāmanānirapekṣasya samyakpravṛttau sthirasya duḥkhādyadhivāsanaśilasyārabdhavīryasya śīghrataraṃ sampadyate / ata eva āryasaṃdhinirvocanādau dānādaya uttarottaratvena varṇitāḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the yogin should first accomplish <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) in order to stabilize the mind. Because the mind is restless like water, there is no stability without the support of <s>śamatha</s>. And with a mind that is not concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>), one cannot know things as they truly are. For the Blessed One has said: 'One who is concentrated knows things as they truly are.' <s>Śamatha</s> is accomplished most swiftly by one who is indifferent to gain and the like, who is steadfast in right conduct, who has the disposition to endure suffering and the rest, and who has aroused vigor. For this very reason, in the <s>Āryasaṃdhinirmocana</s> and elsewhere, giving (<s>dāna</s>) and the other [perfections] are described in ascending order.

body.text: tadevaṃ śīlādiśamathasambhāreṣu sthito mano 'nukūladeśe sarvabuddhabodhisattveṣu praṇāmādikaṃ kṛtvā pāpadeśanāṃ puṇyānumodanāṃ vidhāya sakalajagadabhyuddharaṇāśayo mahākaruṇām evābhimukhīkṛtya kāyam ṛjuṃ praṇidhāya sukhāsanopaviṣṭaḥ paryaṅkamābhujya samādhimabhiniṣpādayet /
body.translated_text: Thus established in the prerequisites of <s>śamatha</s> such as moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) and the rest, in a place agreeable to the mind, having made prostrations and so forth to all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having performed the confession of sins and the rejoicing in merit, with the intention of rescuing all the world, facing great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), holding the body erect, seated comfortably in the cross-legged posture, one should accomplish <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration).

body.text: tatra prathamaṃ tāvad yad vastu vicārayitavyaṃ yāvatā prakāreṇa saṅkṣepataḥ sakalavastusaṅgraho bhavati tatra cittaṃ badhnīyat / saṅkṣiptaṃ
body.translated_text: Therein, first, one should fix the mind on the object that is to be investigated — in whatever manner there is, in brief, a comprehensive gathering of all objects. In brief,

body.text: punarvastu rūpyarūpibhedena dvidha bhavati / etaccādikarmikasya vikṣepadoṣaparihārārtha saṃkṣiptaṃ tāvad yuktam ālambayitum / yadā tu jitamanaskāro bhavati tadā skandhadhātvādibhedena viśodhya vistaraśo 'pyālambata eva / tathā sandhinirmocanādau yoginām aṣṭādaśaprakāraśūnyatālambanādibhedena nānāprakāram ālambanam uktam /
body.translated_text: objects are of two kinds: those with form (<s>rūpin</s>) and those without form (<s>arūpin</s>). For a beginner (<s>ādikarmika</s>), it is appropriate to take as object a condensed [object], in order to avoid the fault of distraction. But when one has gained mastery over the mind, one may take as object even a detailed [analysis] by purifying [objects] into the divisions of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and so forth. Likewise, in the <s>Saṃdhinirmocana</s> and elsewhere, various kinds of objects are taught for yogins, including the division into the eighteen kinds of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) as objects, and so forth.

body.text: atraiva bhagavatā sattvānugrahād rūpyarūpyādibhedena saṃkṣepamadhyavistāraiḥ vastubhedo 'bhidharmādau nirdiṣṭaḥ / tacca vastu adhyāropāpavādaparihārāya skandhadhātvādisaṅgrahato gaṇayet / tato niścitya sarvaṃ vastusaṅgrahaṃ tatraiva punaścittaṃ prabandhena prerayet /
body.translated_text: In this very context, the Blessed One, out of compassion for beings, has indicated in the <s>Abhidharma</s> and elsewhere the classification of objects in brief, middle, and extensive [forms], divided into those with form, without form, and so forth. One should enumerate those objects through the comprehensive gathering of <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and the rest, in order to avoid superimposition (<s>adhyāropa</s>) and deprecation (<s>apavāda</s>). Then, having ascertained the entire comprehensive gathering of objects, one should direct the mind continuously to that very [object].

body.text: yada tvantarā rāgādinā cittaṃ bahirvikṣipet tadāvagamya vikṣepatām aśubhādibhāvanayā vikṣepam upaśāmya punastatraivoparyupari cittaṃ prerayet / aśubhadibhāvanākramastu granthavistarabhayānna likhitaḥ / yadā tu cittaṃ tatrānabhirataṃ paśyet, tada samādherguṇadarśanato 'bhiratiṃ tatra bhāvayet / vikṣepadoṣadarśanād aratiṃ praśamayet / atha yadā styānamiddhābhibhavād āalambanagrahaṇāprakaṭatayālīnaṃ cittaṃ bhavati tadā lokasaṃjñābhāvanayā prāmodyavastubuddhādiguṇamanasikārāt [vā] layaṃ upaśāmya punastadevālambanaṃ dṛḍhataraṃ gṛṇhīyāt /
body.translated_text: But when in the meanwhile the mind is distracted outward by desire (<s>rāga</s>) and so forth, having recognized the distraction, one should pacify the distraction through the meditation on the impure (<s>aśubha-bhāvanā</s>) and the like, and then direct the mind again and again to that very [object]. The method of the meditation on the impure and so forth has not been written [here] out of fear of excessive length. When one observes that the mind is disinclined toward that [object], one should cultivate delight in it through seeing the virtues of <s>samādhi</s>; one should pacify disinclination through seeing the faults of distraction. Now, when the mind becomes sunken (<s>alīna</s>) due to being overcome by dullness and drowsiness (<s>styāna-middha</s>), so that the apprehension of the object is unclear, one should pacify the sinking through the meditation on the perception of the world (<s>loka-saṃjñā</s>) or through attending to joyful subjects such as the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> and the rest, and then grasp that very object more firmly.

body.text: atha yadā pūrvahasitaramitādyanusmarato 'ntarā cittam uddhataṃ paśyet, tadānityatādisaṃvegamanasikārād auddhatyaṃ praśamayet, tataḥ punastatraivālambane cittasyānabhisaṃskāravāhitāyaṃ yatnaṃ kurvīta / atha yadā layauddhatyabhyāṃ viviktatayā samapravṛttaṃ svarasavāhicittaṃ paśyet tadābhogaśithīlīkaraṇād
body.translated_text: Now, when one observes that in the meanwhile the mind has become agitated through recollecting previous laughter, amusement, and the like, one should pacify the agitation (<s>auddhatya</s>) through attending to [thoughts of] disenchantment such as impermanence and the rest. Then, one should make effort [to bring] the mind to effortless flow (<s>anabhisaṃskāra-vāhitā</s>) upon that very object. Now, when one observes that the mind, free from sinking and agitation, is flowing evenly of its own accord,

body.text: upekṣate / yadā tu samapravṛtte satyābhogaḥ kriyate, tadā cittaṃ vikṣipet /
body.translated_text: one should relax the effort and [apply] equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). But when, while the [mind] is flowing evenly, effort is applied, then the mind would be distracted.

body.text: yadā tu tatrālambane 'nabhisaṃskāravāhi yāvadicchaṃ cittaṃ pravṛttaṃ bhavati, tadā śamatho niṣpanno veditavyaḥ / etacca sarvaśamathānāṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇam, cittaikagratāmātrasvabhāvatvāt / śamathasya / ālambanaṃ tu tasyāniyatameva / ayaṃ ca śamathamārgo bhagavatā āryaprajñāpāramitādau nirdiṣṭaḥ / yad āha- "tatra cittaṃ sthāpayati, saṃsthāpayati, avasthāpayati, upasthāpayati, damayati, śamayati, vyupaśamayati, ekotīkaroti, samādadhāti" iti navapadaiḥ /
body.translated_text: When the mind flows upon that object effortlessly for as long as one wishes, then <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) should be understood as accomplished. And this is the general characteristic of all forms of <s>śamatha</s>, since <s>śamatha</s> is of the nature of mere one-pointedness of mind (<s>cittaikāgratā</s>). The object of <s>śamatha</s>, however, is not fixed. And this path of <s>śamatha</s> has been taught by the Blessed One in the <s>Āryaprajñāpāramitā</s> and elsewhere, where he says — in nine terms: 'Therein, one places the mind, settles it, establishes it, applies it closely, tames it, calms it, thoroughly calms it, unifies it, and concentrates it.'

body.text: tatra sthāpayati, ālambanena badhnāti / saṃsthāpayati, tatraivālambane prabandhena pravartayati / avasthāpayati, vikṣepam avagamya taṃ pariharati / upasthāpayati, vikṣepaṃ parihṛtya uparyupari punastatraivālambane sthāpayati / damayati, ratimutpādayati / śamayati, aratiṃ vyupaśāmayati vikṣepadoṣadarśanāt / vyupaśamayati, styānamiddhādīn vyutthitān vyupaśamayati / ekotīkaroti, ālambane 'nabhisaṃskāravāhitāyaṃ yatnaṃ karoti / samādadhāti, samaprāptaṃ cittam upekṣate samanvāharatītyarthaḥ / eṣa caiṣāṃ padānām arthaḥ pūrvācāryaiḥ maitreyeṇa ca vyākhyātaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein: 'places' — one binds [the mind] with the object. 'Settles' — one directs [the mind] continuously upon that very object. 'Establishes' — having recognized distraction, one removes it. 'Applies closely' — having removed distraction, one places [the mind] again and again upon that very object, moving upward. 'Tames' — one generates delight. 'Calms' — one pacifies disinclination through seeing the faults of distraction. 'Thoroughly calms' — one pacifies dullness, drowsiness, and the like when they arise. 'Unifies' — one makes effort toward the effortless flow [of the mind] upon the object. 'Concentrates' — one applies equanimity to the mind that has attained evenness; the meaning is: one maintains [the mind in balance]. And this meaning of these terms has been explained by the earlier masters and by <s>Maitreya</s>.

body.text: saṃkṣepeṇa sarvasaiva samādheḥ ṣaḍ doṣā bhavanti / kauṣidyam ālambanasaṃpramoṣaḥ, layauddhatyam, anābhogaḥ, ābhogateti / teṣāṃ pratipakṣeṇāṣṭau prahāṇasaṃskārā bhavanīyāḥ / tad yathā- śraddhā, chandaḥ, vyāyāmaḥ praśrabdhiḥ, smṛtiḥ, samprajanyam, cetanā, upekṣā ceti / tatrādyāścatvāraḥ kausīdyasya pratipakṣāḥ / tathā hi- samādherguṇeṣvabhisampratyayalakṣaṇayā śraddhayā tatra yogino 'bhilāṣa utpadyate / tato 'bhilāṣād vīryamarabheta / tadvīryabalena kāyacittakarmaṇyatām
body.translated_text: In brief, there are six faults in all forms of <s>samādhi</s>: laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), forgetting the object (<s>ālambana-saṃpramoṣa</s>), sinking and agitation (<s>laya-auddhatya</s>), non-application (<s>anābhoga</s>), and [over-]application (<s>ābhoga</s>). As their antidotes, eight abandonment-formations (<s>prahāṇa-saṃskāra</s>) should be cultivated: namely, faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), aspiration (<s>chanda</s>), exertion (<s>vyāyāma</s>), pliancy (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), clear comprehension (<s>samprajanya</s>), volition (<s>cetanā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). Therein, the first four are the antidotes to laziness. For through faith — characterized by confidence in the virtues of <s>samādhi</s> — aspiration arises in the yogin. From that aspiration, one begins vigor. Through the power of that vigor, one achieves pliancy of body and mind.

body.text: āsādayati / tataḥ praśrabdhakāyacetasaḥ kausīdyam āvartate / ataḥ śraddhādayaḥ kausīdyaprahāṇāya bhāvanīyāḥ / smṛtirālambanasampramoṣasya pratipakṣaḥ / samprajanyaṃ layauddhatyayoḥ pratipakṣaḥ / tena layauddhatyayoḥ samyagupaṃlakṣaṇāt / layauddhatyāpraśamanakāle tvanābhogadoṣaḥ tatpratipakṣeṇa ca cetanā bhāvanīyā / layauddhatyapraśame sati yadā cittaṃ praśamavāhi tadābhogadoṣaḥ, tatpratipakṣastadānīmupekṣā bhāvanīyā /
body.translated_text: Then, when body and mind are pliant, laziness is turned back. Therefore, faith and the rest should be cultivated for the abandonment of laziness. Mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) is the antidote to forgetting the object. Clear comprehension (<s>samprajanya</s>) is the antidote to sinking and agitation, since through it one correctly observes sinking and agitation. When sinking and agitation have not [yet] been pacified, there is the fault of non-application; as its antidote, volition (<s>cetanā</s>) should be cultivated. When sinking and agitation have been pacified, when the mind is flowing calmly, there is the fault of [over-]application; as its antidote at that time, equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) should be cultivated.

body.text: ebhiraṣṭābhiḥ prahāṇasaṃskāraiḥ samanvāgataḥ samādhiḥ paramakarmaṇyo bhavati / ṛddhayādīn guṇān niṣpādayati / ata evoktaṃ sūtra- "[aṣṭa]prahāṇa [saṃskāra]samanvāgataḥ ṛddhipādaṃ bhāvayati" iti / eṣā ca cittaikāgratā uttarottarakarmaṇyatāsamprayogād ālambanādiguṇaviśeṣayogācca dhyānārūpisamāpattiḥ vimokṣādivyapadeśaṃ labhate /
body.translated_text: A <s>samādhi</s> endowed with these eight abandonment-formations becomes supremely workable. It produces qualities such as supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>) and the like. For this reason it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Endowed with the [eight] abandonment-[formations], one cultivates the basis of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>).' And this one-pointedness of mind, through the progressive conjunction with [increasing] workability and through the special connection with qualities such as the object and so forth, receives the designations of the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), formless attainments (<s>ārūpya-samāpatti</s>), liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), and so forth.

body.text: tathā hi yadopekṣāvedanāsamprayuktā savitarkasavicārā sā bhavati, tadānāgamyā ucyate [prathamadhyānaprayogacittatvāt] / yadā ca kāmatṛṣṇayā pāpadharmaiśca] viviktā bhavati [vitarkavicāra]prītisukhādhyātmasamprasādaiḥ samprayuktā bhavati, tadā prathamaṃ dhyānam ucyate / ata eva prathamadhyānaṃ vitarkamātrarahitaṃ dhyānāntaramucyate / yadā vitarkavicārarahitā prathamadhyānabhūmitṛṣṇayā viviktā ca bhavati / prītisukhādhyātmasamprasādaiḥ samprayuktā bhavati, tadā dvitīyaṃ dhyānamucyate / yadā tu dvitīyadhyānabhūmitṛṣṇayā viviktā bhavati, sukhopekṣāsmṛtisamprajanyasamprayuktā bhavati, tadā tṛtīyaṃ dhyānam ucyate / yadā tṛtīyadhyānabhūmitṛṣṇayā viviktā bhavati / aduḥkhāsukhā upekṣāsmṛtyabhisamprayuktā bhavati, tadā caturthaṃ dhyānamucyate / evam arūpyasamāpattivimokṣābhibhavāyatanādiṣvālambanākārādibhedena yojyam /
body.translated_text: For when [the concentration] is conjoined with equanimous feeling (<s>upekṣā-vedanā</s>) and possesses thought-application (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>), it is called the preliminary [stage] [being the preparatory mental state of the first <s>dhyāna</s>]. When it is separated from the craving of the desire-realm and from unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and is conjoined with thought-application, sustained thought, joy (<s>prīti</s>), bliss (<s>sukha</s>), and inner clarity, it is called the first <s>dhyāna</s>. For this very reason, the first <s>dhyāna</s> devoid of thought-application alone is called the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>. When it is free from thought-application and sustained thought, separated from the craving of the first-<s>dhyāna</s> level, and conjoined with joy, bliss, and inner clarity, it is called the second <s>dhyāna</s>. When it is separated from the craving of the second-<s>dhyāna</s> level and conjoined with bliss, equanimity, mindfulness, and clear comprehension, it is called the third <s>dhyāna</s>. When it is separated from the craving of the third-<s>dhyāna</s> level and conjoined with neither-painful-nor-pleasant [feeling], equanimity, and mindfulness, it is called the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. In the same way, [this pattern] should be applied to the formless attainments, liberations, bases of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>), and so forth, by the distinctions of object, aspect, and the rest.

body.text: tadevamālambane cittaṃ sthirīkṛtya prajñayā vivecayet / yato jñānālokotpādāt sammohabījasyātyantaprahāṇaṃ bhavati / anyathā hi tīrthikānāmiva samādhimātreṇa kleśaprahāṇaṃ na syāt / yathoktaṃ sutre-
body.translated_text: Having thus stabilized the mind on the object, one should discriminate with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). For from the arising of the light of knowledge (<s>jñānāloka</s>), the complete abandonment of the seed of delusion (<s>saṃmoha</s>) takes place. Otherwise, as with the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist practitioners), the abandonment of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) would not occur through <s>samādhi</s> alone. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text:
kiñcāpi bhāvayet samādhimetaṃ na co bibhāveyya sā ātmasaṃjñām /
punaḥ prakupyati kileṣu tasya yathodrakasyeha samādhibhāvanā // iti /
body.translated_text: Even though one may cultivate this <s>samādhi</s>, if one does not meditate on the perception of self, the afflictions will arise again for that one — just as was the meditation of <s>Udraka</s> here.

body.text: tatrāyam āryalaṅkāvatāre saṃkṣepāt prajñābhāvanākramo nirdiṣṭaḥ-
body.translated_text: Therein, the following method of cultivating <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is taught in brief in the <s>Āryalaṅkāvatāra</s>:

children.translated_text: Having ascended to mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>), one should not conceptually construct external objects;
abiding in the object of suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), one should transcend mind-only.
Having transcended mind-only, one should transcend even the absence of appearances (<s>nirābhāsa</s>).
The <s>yogin</s> established in the state without appearances sees <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

body.text:
anābhogagatiḥ śāntā praṇidhānairviśodhitā /
jñānaṃ nirātmakaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ nirābhāse na paśyati // iti /
body.translated_text:
The effortless course is peaceful, purified by aspirations;
the supreme knowledge without self does not see [anything] in the state without appearances.
