body.text: tatrāyamarthaḥ- prathamaṃ yogī ye rūpiṇo dharmā bāhyārthatayā paraiḥ parikalpitāsteṣu tāvad vicārayet / kimete vijñānād anye, āhosvid vijñānamevaitat tathā pratibhāsate, yathā svapnāvasthāyāmiti / tatra vijñānād bahiḥ paramāṇuśo vicārayet / paramāṇūṃśca bhāgaśaḥ pratyavekṣa- māṇo yogī tān arthānna samanupaśyati / tasyāsamanupaśyata evaṃ bhavati cittamātramevaitat sarvaṃ na punarbāhyo 'rthā vipadyate / tadevam-
body.translated_text: Therein, the meaning is as follows: First, the <s>yogin</s> should examine those <s>dharmas</s> with form that are imagined by others as having the nature of external objects. Are these different from consciousness, or does consciousness itself merely appear thus, as in the dream state? Therein, one should analyze the external [objects] atom by atom. The <s>yogin</s>, examining the atoms part by part, does not perceive those objects. Not perceiving them, this [realization] arises in him: 'All this is mere mind; external objects do not [truly] exist.' In this manner—

body.text: "cittamātraṃ samāruhya bāhyamarthaṃ na kalpayet / "
body.translated_text: "Having ascended to mind-only, one should not conceptualize external objects."

body.text: rūpidharmavikalpāṃstyajed ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: The meaning is: one should abandon the conceptual constructions of form <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: teṣām upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptānāṃ vicārayed anupalabdheḥ / evaṃ rūpiṇo dharmān vibhāvyārupiṇo vibhāvayet / tatra yaccittamātraṃ tadapyasati grāhye grāhako na yukto grāhakasya grāhyapekṣatvad tataścittaṃ grāhyagrāhakaviviktam advayameva cittamiti vicārayed advayalakṣaṇe-
body.translated_text: Since those [dharmas] have come to be characterized by apprehension, one should examine [them further], since they are not [ultimately] apprehended. Having thus analyzed the <s>dharmas</s> with form, one should analyze the formless [<s>dharmas</s>]. Therein, that which is mind-only—even that, in the absence of a graspable object, a grasper is not logically tenable, since the grasper depends on the graspable. Therefore, one should examine the mind as devoid of the duality of grasper and grasped—it is non-dual mind. In the characteristic of non-duality—

body.text: "tathatālambane sthitvā tadapi cittamātram atikramet / "
body.translated_text: "Having abided in the support of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), one should transcend even mind-only."

body.text: grahakamākāramatikrameta / dvayanirābhāsa eva advayajñāne tiṣṭhedityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: One should transcend the aspect of the grasper. The meaning is: one should abide in non-dual <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) where duality does not appear.

body.text: evaṃ cittamātramatikramya tadapi dvayanirābhasaṃ yajjñānaṃ tadatikrameta / svataḥ parato bhāvānāṃ janmānupapatteḥ grāhyagrāhakayoścālīkatve tadavyatirekāt tasyāpi satyatvamayuktamiti vicārayet / tatrāpyadvayajñāne vastutvābhiniveśaṃ tyajet, advayajñānanirābhāsa eva jñāne tiṣṭhedityarthaḥ / evaṃ sati sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatāpratipattau sthito bhavati / tatra sthitasya paramatattvapraveśāt nirvikalpasamādhipraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, having transcended mind-only, one should also transcend that knowledge in which duality does not appear. Since the arising of entities from self or from other is untenable, and since both the graspable and grasper are false, and since [that knowledge] is not different from them, one should examine that its reality too is untenable. Therein also, in non-dual knowledge, one should abandon the attachment to substantiality; the meaning is: one should abide in knowledge that is the non-appearance of non-dual knowledge. This being so, one is established in the realization of the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. For one established therein, entry into the ultimate reality is entry into <s>nirvikalpasamādhi</s> (non-conceptual concentration).

body.text: tathā cādvayajñānanirābhāse jñāne yadā sthito yogī tadā paramatattve sthitatvāt, mahāyānaṃ sa paśyati / etadeva tat mahāyānam ucyate yat paramatattvadarśanam / etadeva tat paramatattvadarśanaṃ yat sarvadharmān prajñācakṣuṣā nirūpayataḥ samyagjñānāvaloke satyadarśanam / tathā coktaṃ sutre- "katamaṃ paramārthadarśanam? sarvadharmāṇām adarśanam /" iti /
body.translated_text: And thus, when the <s>yogin</s> is established in knowledge that is the non-appearance of non-dual knowledge, then, being established in ultimate reality, he sees <s>Mahāyāna</s>. That very seeing of ultimate reality is called <s>Mahāyāna</s>. That very seeing of ultimate reality is the seeing of truth in the light of right knowledge by one who examines all <s>dharmas</s> with the eye of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). And thus it is stated in a <s>sūtra</s>: "What is the seeing of ultimate reality? The non-seeing of all <s>dharmas</s>."

body.text: atredṛśamevādarśanamabhipretaṃ na tu nimīlitākṣajātyandhānāmiva pratyayavaikalyād amanasikārato vā yadadarśanam /
body.translated_text: Here, this very non-seeing is intended—not the non-seeing that is like that of one with closed eyes or the congenitally blind, due to deficiency of conditions, or from non-attention.

body.text: tato bhāvābhiniveśadiviparyāsavāsanāyā aprahīṇatvād asaṃjñisamāpattyādivyutthitasyeva punarapi bhāvābhiniveśamūlasya rāgādikleśagaṇasyotpatteramukta eva yogī bhavet / bhāvābhiniveśamūlo rāgādiḥ āryasatyadvayanirdeśādau varṇitaḥ / yatpunaruktam avikalpapraveśadhāraṇyām- "amanasikārato rūpādinimittaṃ varjayati" iti / tatrāpi prajñayā nirūpayato yo 'nupalambhaḥ sa tatrāmanasikāro 'bhipreto na manasikārābhāvamātram / na hyasaṃjñisamāpattyādiriva anādikāliko rūpādyabhiniveśo manasikāraparivarjanamātrāt prahīyate /
body.translated_text: Then, since the <s>vāsanā</s> (habitual tendency) of the distorted view of clinging to existence has not been abandoned, like one who has risen from the attainment of non-perception and so forth, the assemblage of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) such as <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and others, whose root is the clinging to existence, would arise again, and the <s>yogin</s> would not be liberated at all. The root of <s>rāga</s> and other [afflictions] in the clinging to existence is described in the <s>Āryasatyadvayanirdeśa</s> and elsewhere. As for what is stated in the <s>Avikalpapraveśadhāraṇī</s>: "Through non-attention, one avoids the signs of form and so forth"—even there, the non-apprehension that occurs when examining with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is intended as the 'non-attention,' not the mere absence of mental engagement. For the clinging to form and so forth, which is beginningless, is not abandoned merely by the avoidance of mental engagement, as in the attainment of non-perception and the like.

body.text: saṃśayā prahāṇe tu na pūrvopalabdheṣu ca rūpādiṣvabhiniveśamanasikāraparivarjanaṃ śakyaṃ kartum agnyaparivarjane dāhāparivarjanavat / tathāmī rūpādimithyāvikalpāḥ kaṇṭakādivadutkīlya na hastena cetaso 'panetavyāḥ / kiṃ tarhi saṃśayabījāpagamāt / tacca saṃśayabījaṃ yoginaḥ samādhyāloke sati prajñācakṣuṣā nirūpayatastesāṃ rūpādīnāṃ pūrvopalabdhānām upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptānām anupalambhād, rajjoḥ sarpajñānavad, apagacchati nānyathā / tathā saṃśayabījāpagamād rūpādinimittamanasikāraḥ śakyate varjayituṃ nānyathā / anyathā hyasati samādhyāloke prajñācakṣuṣāpyanavaloke yathā andhakūpāvasthitapuruṣasyāvacarakagataghāṭādiṣviva yogino rūpādiṣvastitvasaṃśayo naiva nivarteta / tadanivṛttyā cā prahīṇatimiradoṣasyeva yo 'yukto 'līkarūpādyabhiniveśaḥ pravarteta na kenāpi nivartyeta /
body.translated_text: For the abandonment of doubt, it is not possible to avoid the mental engagement of clinging to form and so forth that were previously apprehended—just as, without avoiding fire, burning cannot be avoided. Likewise, these false conceptualizations regarding form and so forth are not to be removed from the mind by hand, as it were, like pulling out thorns. Rather, [they are removed] through the elimination of the seed of doubt. And that seed of doubt, when the <s>yogin</s>'s light of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is present and he examines with the eye of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), is eliminated through the non-apprehension of those forms and so forth that were previously apprehended and characterized by apprehension—like the knowledge of a snake [projected upon] a rope—and not otherwise. Likewise, through the elimination of the seed of doubt, the mental engagement toward the signs of form and so forth can be avoided, and not otherwise. For otherwise, in the absence of the light of <s>samādhi</s>, and without the examination by the eye of <s>prajñā</s>, the doubt regarding the existence of form and so forth would never cease for the <s>yogin</s>—like a person situated in a dark well regarding movement and objects within it. And from the non-cessation of that [doubt], the illogical clinging to false forms and so forth—like one whose eye disease has not been cured—would continue and could not be averted by anything.

body.text: tasmāt samādhihastena manaḥ sandhāya sūkṣmataraprajñāśastreṇa tatra cetasi rūpādimithyāvikalpabījam uddharet / evam satyutkhātamūlā iva
body.translated_text: Therefore, with the hand of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), having steadied the mind, one should uproot the seed of false conceptualization regarding form and so forth in that mind with the extremely subtle sword of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). In this way, with roots uprooted like

body.text: taravo bhūmernirmūlatayā mithyāvikalpāḥ punaścetasi na virohanti / ata evāvaraṇaprahāṇāya śamathavipaśyanāyuganaddhavāhī mārgo bhagavatā nirdiṣṭaḥ, tayoḥ avikalpasamyagjñāne hetutvāt / tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: trees from the earth, the false conceptualizations, being rootless, do not sprout again in the mind. For this very reason, the path that yokes <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) together was taught by the Blessed One for the abandonment of the obscurations, since both are causes of non-conceptual right knowledge. And thus it is stated:

body.text:
śīlaṃ pratiṣṭhāya samādhilābhāḥ samādhilābhācca hi prajñābhāvanā /
prajñayā jñānaṃ bhavati viśuddhaṃ viśuddhajñānasya hi śīlasampat // iti /
body.translated_text:
Based on <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) comes the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>; from the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>, the cultivation of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom);
through <s>prajñā</s>, purified <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) arises; and from purified knowledge, the perfection of <s>śīla</s>.

body.text: tathā hi yadā śamathenālambane cittaṃ sthirīkṛtaṃ bhavati tadā prajñayā vicārayataḥ samyagjñānāloka utpadyate, tadāndhakāramivāloke prakāśayati āvaraṇam apahīyate / ata evānayoścakṣurālokayoriva samyagjñānotpādaṃ pratyanyo 'nyānuguṇyenāvasthitatvānnālokāndhakāravat parasparavirodhaḥ / na hi samādhirandhakārasvabhāvaḥ / kiṃ tarhi cittaikāgratālakṣaṇaḥ / sa ca samāhito yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti vacanādekāntena prajñānukūla eva bhavati, na tu viruddhastasmāt syāt samāhitasya prajñayā nirūpayataḥ sarvadharmāṇāmanupalambhaḥ / sa eva paramo 'nupalambhaḥ / sā ca tādṛśī yogināmavasthānalakṣaṇā gatiranābhogā, tataḥ paraṃ dṛṣṭavyasyābhāvāt / śānteti bhāvābhāvādivikalpalakṣaṇasya prapañcasyopaśamāt /
body.translated_text: For when the mind has been stabilized on the object through <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), then, as one examines with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), the light of right knowledge arises; then, as light illuminates darkness, the obscurations are removed. For this very reason, since these two—like the eye and light—are established in mutual correspondence with respect to the arising of right knowledge, there is no mutual opposition like that between light and darkness. For <s>samādhi</s> is not of the nature of darkness; rather, its defining characteristic is one-pointedness of mind. And since it is stated 'one who is concentrated knows things as they truly are,' it is exclusively favorable to <s>prajñā</s>, not opposed to it. Therefore, for one who is concentrated and examines with <s>prajñā</s>, there would be the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. That is the supreme non-apprehension. And that kind of state—the defining characteristic of the <s>yogins'</s> abiding—is an effortless course, since beyond that there is nothing to be seen. It is 'peaceful' because of the subsiding of the proliferation characterized by conceptual constructions of existence, non-existence, and so forth.

body.text: tathā hi yadā prajñayā nirūpayan na kiñcid bhāvasvabhāvam upalabhate yogī, tadāsya naiva bhāvavikalpo bhavat / abhāvavikalpo 'pi tasya nāstyeva / yadi bhāvaḥ kadācid dṛṣṭo bhavati, evaṃ sati tanniṣedhenābhāvavikalpaḥ pravartate / yadā tu kālatraye 'pi bhāvo yoginā prajñācakṣuṣā nirūpayatā nopalabdhaḥ, tadā kathaṃ tasya pratiṣedhenābhāvavikalpaṃ kurvīta / evamanye 'pi vikalpāstadā tasya na samutpadyanta eva bhāvābhāvavikalpābhyāṃ
body.translated_text: For when the <s>yogin</s>, examining with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), does not apprehend any nature of existence, then he has no conceptual construction of existence whatsoever. He has no conceptual construction of non-existence either. If existence had at some time been seen, then through its negation, the conceptual construction of non-existence would arise. But when existence is not apprehended by the <s>yogin</s> examining with the eye of <s>prajñā</s> in all three times, then how could he, through its negation, produce a conceptual construction of non-existence? In this way, other conceptual constructions also do not arise in him at that time, since [they depend on] the conceptual constructions of existence and non-existence.

body.text:
sarvavikalpasya vyāptatvāt / vyāpakābhāve ca vyāpyasyāsambhavāt / ayamasau paramanirvikalpo yogaḥ / tatra sthitasya yoginaḥ sarvavikalpānām astaṃgamāt samyak kleśāvaraṇaṃ jñeyāvaraṇaṃ ca prahīyate / tathā hi kleśāvaraṇasyānutpannāniruddhabhāveṣu bhāvādiviparyāso mūlaṃ kāraṇam āryasatyadvayanirdeśādau varṇitaṃ bhagavatā /
anena ca yogābhyāsena sarvabhāvādivikalpānāṃ prahāṇāt sakalabhāvādiviparyāsasyāvidyāsvabhāvasya kleśāvaraṇamūlasya prahāṇam / tato mūlocchedāt kleśavaraṇaṃ samyak prahīyate / tathā coktaṃ satyadvayanirdeśe- "kathaṃ mañjuśrīḥ, kleśā vinayaṃ gacchanti, kathaṃ kleśāḥ parijñātā bhavanti? mañjuśrīrāha- paramārthato 'tyantājātānutpannābhāveṣu sarvadharmeṣu saṃvṛtyāsadviparyāsaḥ / tasmād asadviparyāsāt saṅkalpavikalpaḥ / tasmāt saṃkalpavikalpād ayoniśo manasikāraḥ / tasmād ayoniśo manasikārād ātmasamāropaḥ / tasmād ātmasamāropād dṛṣṭiparyutthānam / tasmād dṛṣṭiparyutthānāt kleśāḥ pravartante / yaḥ punaḥ devaputra! paramārthato 'tyantājātānutpannābhāvān sarvadharmān prajānāti, sa paramārthato 'viparyastaḥ / yaśca paramārthato 'viparyastaḥ so 'vikalpaḥ / yaścāvikalpaḥ sa yoniśaḥ prayuktaḥ / yaśca yoniśaḥ prayuktaḥ tasyātmasamāropo na bhavati / yasyātmasamāropo na bhavati tasya dṛṣṭiparyutthānaṃ na bhavati / yāvat paramārthato nirvāṇadṛṣṭisarva dṛṣṭiparyutthānam api na bhavati / tasyaivam anutpādavihāriṇaḥ kleśā atyantaṃ vinītā draṣṭavyāḥ / ayam ucyate kleśavinayaḥ / yadā, devaputra! kleśān nirābhāsena jñānena paramārthato 'tyantaśūnyān atyantābhāvān atyantanirnimittāt prajānāti, tadā devaputra! kleśāḥ parijñātā bhavanti / tatra
body.translated_text: because all conceptual construction is pervaded [by the error of positing existence and so forth]. And in the absence of the pervader, the pervaded cannot exist. This is the supreme non-conceptual yoga (<s>paramanirvikalpa yoga</s>). For the yogin established therein, through the cessation of all conceptual constructions, the obscuration of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) are properly abandoned. For the Blessed One has described, in the <s>Āryasatyadvayanirdeśa</s> and elsewhere, that the error of [positing] existence and so forth (<s>bhāvādi-viparyāsa</s>) in [things that are in ultimate reality] unarisen and unceased is the root cause of the obscuration of afflictions. Through the practice of this yoga, from the abandonment of all conceptual constructions of existence and so forth, there is the abandonment of all errors of existence and so forth — which are of the nature of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and the root of the obscuration of afflictions. Then, from the cutting of the root, the obscuration of afflictions is properly abandoned. As stated in the <s>Satyadvayanirdeśa</s>: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, how are the afflictions disciplined? How are the afflictions fully known?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'In the ultimate sense, in all <s>dharmas</s> that are utterly unborn, unarisen, and non-existent, there is conventionally the error of [positing what is] non-existent. From that error of the non-existent, [there arises] volition and conceptual construction. From volition and conceptual construction, improper mental engagement (<s>ayoniśo manasikāra</s>). From improper mental engagement, the superimposition of a self (<s>ātma-samāropa</s>). From the superimposition of a self, the arising of [wrong] views. From the arising of [wrong] views, the afflictions operate. But, O son of the gods, whoever knows in the ultimate sense all <s>dharmas</s> as utterly unborn, unarisen, and non-existent — he is, in the ultimate sense, free from error. And one who is free from error is non-conceptual. And one who is non-conceptual is properly engaged. And for one who is properly engaged, the superimposition of a self does not occur. For one for whom the superimposition of a self does not occur, the arising of [wrong] views does not occur — even the arising of all views including the view of <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the ultimate sense does not occur. The afflictions of one who thus abides in non-arising should be seen as utterly disciplined. This is called the disciplining of afflictions. When, O son of the gods, one knows the afflictions through signless (<s>nirābhāsa</s>) knowledge as ultimately utterly empty, utterly non-existent, utterly signless — then, O son of the gods, the afflictions are fully known. Therein,

body.text: yathāpi nāma, devaputra! ya āśīviṣasya gotraṃ prajānāti / sa tasyāśīviṣasya viṣaṃ śamayati / evameva devaputra! ya kleśānāṃ gotraṃ prajānāti tasya kleśāḥ praśāmyanti / devaputra āha- kataman mañjuśrīḥ! kleśānāṃ gotram / āha- yāvad eṣā paramārthato 'tyantājātānutpannābhāveṣu sarvadharmeṣu kalpanā idaṃ kleśānāṃ gotram" iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: just as, O son of the gods, one who knows the lineage of a poisonous snake pacifies the venom of that snake — in the same way, O son of the gods, for one who knows the lineage of the afflictions, the afflictions are pacified. The son of the gods asked: What, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the lineage of the afflictions? He replied: Whatever conceptual construction there is regarding all <s>dharmas</s> that are in the ultimate sense utterly unborn, unarisen, and non-existent — this is the lineage of the afflictions.' And so forth in detail.

body.text: bhāvādiviparyāsena ca sakalaviparyāsasya vyāptatvāt / tatprahāṇe sakalaviparyāsaprahāṇād jñeyāvaraṇam apyanena samyak prahīyate, viparyāsalakṣaṇatvād āvaraṇasya / jñeyāvaraṇe ca prahīṇe pratibandhābhāvād ravikiraṇavad apagatameghādyāvaraṇe nabhasi sarvatrāvyāhato yogi pratyakṣo jñānālokaḥ pravartate / tathā hi vastusvabhāvaprakāśarūpaṃ vijñānam / tacca saṃnihitam api vastu pratibandhasadbhāvānna prakāśayati / pratibandhābhāve tu sati, acintyaśaktiviśeṣalābhāt kimiti sakalam eva vastu yathāvad na prakāśayet / ataḥ saṃvṛtiparamārtharūpeṇa sakalasya vastuno yathāvat parijñānāt sarvajñatvam avāpyate / ato 'yam evāvaraṇaprahāṇo sarvajñatvādhigame ca paramo mārgaḥ /
body.translated_text: And since all errors are pervaded by the error of [positing] existence and so forth, by the abandonment of that, through the abandonment of all errors, the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) too is properly abandoned by this [yoga], since the obscuration has the characteristic of error. And when the obscuration of the knowable is abandoned, in the absence of obstruction — like the rays of the sun in the sky when clouds and other coverings have been removed — the unobstructed perceptual light of knowledge of the yogin operates everywhere. For consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is of the nature of illuminating the own-nature of things. Yet even when things are present, it does not illuminate them due to the existence of obstruction. But when obstruction is absent, through the attainment of inconceivable special powers, why would it not illuminate all things exactly as they are? Therefore, through the complete knowledge of all things exactly as they are — in their conventional and ultimate aspects — omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>) is attained. Hence, this is the supreme path for the abandonment of the [two] obscurations and for the attainment of omniscience.

body.text: yastu śrāvakādīnāṃ mārgastena viparyāsāprahāṇān na samyag āvaraṇadvayaṃ prahīyate / tathā coktam āryalaṅkāvatāre- "anye tu kāraṇādhīnān sarvadharmān dṛṣṭvānirvāṇe 'pi nirvāṇam iti buddhayo bhavanti / dharmanairātmyādarśanād nāsti mahāmate! mokṣa eṣām / mahāmate, śrāvakayānikābhisamayagotrasyāniryāṇe niryāṇabuddhiḥ / atra mahāmate,
body.translated_text: But by the path of the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and the rest, because the errors are not [fully] abandoned, the twofold obscuration is not properly abandoned. As stated in the <s>Āryalaṅkāvatāra</s>: 'Others, having seen all <s>dharmas</s> as dependent on causes, have the understanding that even in non-<s>nirvāṇa</s> there is <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Through not seeing the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharma-nairātmya</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, liberation does not belong to them. O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for those of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle lineage who have the understanding of exit in non-exit — therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>,

body.text: kudṛṣṭivyāvartanā yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ" iti / ata eva cānyena mārgeṇa mokṣābhāvād ekam eva yānam uktaṃ bhagavatā /
body.translated_text: the yoga of turning back from wrong views is to be practiced.' For this very reason, since there is no liberation by any other path, one single vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>) alone has been taught by the Blessed One.

body.text: kevalam [bālena bālasya] avatāraṇābhisandhinā śrāvakādimārgo deśitaḥ / tathā hi sakandha mātramevaitat, na tvātmāstīti bhāvayan śrāvakaḥ pudgalanairātmyam avatarati, vijñaptimātraṃ traidhātukamiti bhāvayan vijñānavādibāhyārthanairātmyamavatarati / anena tvasyadvayajñānasya nairātmyapraveśāt paramatattvapraviṣṭo bhavati / na tu vijñaptimātratāpraveśa eva tattvapraveśaḥ / yathoktaṃ prāk / uktaṃ ca āryalokottaraparivarte "punaraparaṃ bho jinaputra! cittamātraṃ traidhātukam avatarati, tacca cittam anantamadhyatayāvatarati" iti / antayorutpādabhaṅgalakṣaṇayoḥ sthitilakṣaṇasya ca madhyasyābhāvād anantamadhyacittam / tasmād advayajñānapraveśa eva tattvapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Śrāvaka</s> path and the rest were taught merely with the intention of introducing [beginners] step by step. For the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, meditating 'This is merely the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>); there is no self,' enters the selflessness of the person (<s>pudgala-nairātmya</s>); the <s>Vijñānavādin</s> (idealist), meditating 'The three realms are mere representation (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>),' enters the selflessness of external objects. But by this [non-conceptual yoga], through entering the selflessness of non-dual knowledge (<s>advaya-jñāna</s>), one enters the supreme reality — but entry into mere representation alone is not entry into reality, as stated before. And it is said in the <s>Āryalokottaraparivarta</s>: 'Furthermore, O son of the Conqueror, one enters [the understanding that] the three realms are mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>), and that mind is entered as being without end or middle.' Because the two extremes — characterized by arising and cessation — and the middle — characterized by abiding — are absent, the mind is without end or middle. Therefore, entry into non-dual knowledge alone is entry into reality.

body.text: sā ceyaṃ yoginām avasthā kuto viśodhitā? ityāha-
body.translated_text: But from where has this state of the yogins been purified? To this he says:

body.text: "praṇidhānairviśodhitā" iti / mahākaruṇayā yat sarvasattvārthakaraṇāya bodhisattvena praṇihitam, tataḥ praṇidhānabalād uttarottaradānādikuśalābhyāsāt sā tathā viśuddhā jāta, yena sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatājñāne 'pi sakalasattvāpekṣā na vyāvartate yāvat saṃsāra eva ananuliptāḥ saṃsāradoṣairavatiṣṭhanta iti / kathaṃ punaranābhogā śāntetyatra kāraṇamāha-
body.translated_text: 'It has been purified through aspirations (<s>praṇidhāna</s>).' Through great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has aspired to accomplish the welfare of all beings. Through the power of those aspirations, through the progressive practice of wholesome [deeds] such as giving and the rest, [this state] has been so purified that even while [abiding in] the knowledge of the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, concern for all beings is not abandoned — [the bodhisattvas] remain even in <s>saṃsāra</s> itself, untainted by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>. But how [is it that] they are effortless and quiescent? To this, the reason is stated:

body.text: jñānaṃ nirātmakaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ nirābhāsena paśyati / iti /
body.translated_text: 'The supreme knowledge, which is selfless, sees through signless (<s>nirābhāsa</s>) [cognition].'

body.text: yasmād yad advayalakṣaṇaṃ jñānam advayavādināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ paramārthenābhimataṃ tadapi nirātmakaṃ niḥsvabhāvam advayanirābhāsena jñānena paśyati yogī / ato 'parasya draṣṭavyasyābhāvād anābhogā, sarvavikalpābhāvat śānteti /
body.translated_text: Since whatever knowledge has the characteristic of non-duality — which the proponents of non-duality hold to be supreme in the ultimate sense — that too is selfless (<s>nirātmaka</s>), devoid of own-nature, and the yogin sees [it] through non-dual, signless knowledge. Therefore, since there is nothing else remaining to be seen, [they are] effortless; since all conceptual constructions are absent, [they are] quiescent.

body.text: atredānīṃ ko 'sau yogī vidyate, yaḥ paśyatīti cet? na paramārthataḥ kaścid ātmādiḥ svatantro 'sti, yogī nāpi kaścit paśyati / kintu saṃvṛtyā yathā rūpādīviṣayākārajñānotpādamātreṇa vijñānameva loke tathā tathā vyavahriyate devadatto yajñadattaṃ jñānena paśyatīti na tu kaścid ātmādirasti / tathātrāpi jñānamevādvayajñānanirābhāsam utpadyamānaṃ tathā vyapadiśyate nirābhāsena jñānena paśyatiti / na hi sarvadharmāṇāṃ paramārthato niḥsvabhāvatve 'pi saṃvṛtyā yogijñānam anyad vā pṛthagjñānaṃ neṣṭam / tathā coktam āryasatyadvayanirdeśe- "paramārthato 'tyantābhāvaśca saṃvṛttyā ca mārga bhāvayati" iti /
body.translated_text: Now, if [one asks:] 'What yogin exists who sees?' — In the ultimate sense, no self or the like exists independently; there is no yogin who sees anything. But conventionally, just as in the world, by the mere arising of consciousness in the form of objects such as form and the rest, consciousness itself is conventionally designated in various ways — '<s>Devadatta</s> sees <s>Yajñadatta</s> with knowledge' — yet no self or the like exists. So too here, knowledge itself, arising as the signless [cognition of] non-dual knowledge, is so designated: 'One sees through signless knowledge.' For even though all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately devoid of own-nature, the yogin's knowledge — and also the ordinary person's knowledge — is accepted conventionally. As stated in the <s>Āryasatyadvayanirdeśa</s>: 'Even though [there is] utter non-existence in the ultimate sense, one cultivates the path conventionally.'

body.text: anyathā śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattva [buddha]pṛthagjanādivyavasthā kathaṃ bhavet, kintu yasya saṃvṛtyāpi kāraṇaṃ nāsti sa saṃvṛtyāpi notpadyate / yathā śaśaviṣāṇādi / yasya tu [kāraṇaṃ] vidyate sa paramārthato 'līko 'pi samutpadyata eva / yathā- māyāpratibimba [pratidhvani]ādī / na ca māyādeḥ saṃvṛtyā pratītyasamutpāde paramārthato vastutvaprasaṅgaḥ, tasya vicārākṣamatvāt / ataḥ sarvameva māyopamaṃ jagat / tatra yathā kleśakarmamāyāvaśāt sattvānāṃ janmamāyā pravarteta, tathā yogināmapi puṇyajñānasambhāramāyāvaśād yogijñānamāyā pravartata eva / tathā coktam āryaprajñāpāramitāyām- "kaścit śrāvakanirmitaḥ, kaścit pratyekabuddhanirmitaḥ, kaścid bodhisattvanirmitaḥ, kaścit tathāgatanirmitaḥ, kaścit kleśanirmitaḥ kaścit karmanirmitaḥ / anena subhūte, paryāyeṇa sarvadharmā nirmitotpannāḥ" iti / ayaṃ tu viśeṣo yogināṃ pṛthagjanebhyaḥ, te hi māyākāravat tāṃ māyāṃ yathāvat parijñānāt satyato nābhiniviśante,
body.translated_text: Otherwise, how would the distinctions of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, [<s>Buddhas</s>], ordinary beings, and so forth be possible? Yet that which has no cause even conventionally does not arise even conventionally — like a hare's horn and the like. But that which has a cause, even though unreal in the ultimate sense, does arise — like an illusion, a reflection, [an echo,] and the like. Nor does the dependent arising of illusion and the like conventionally entail their being real things in the ultimate sense, since they do not withstand analysis. Therefore, the entire world is like an illusion (<s>māyā</s>). Just as, through the magical power of afflictions and actions [which are like] illusion, the illusory birth of beings proceeds — so too, through the magical power of the accumulations of merit and knowledge, the illusory knowledge of yogins proceeds. As stated in the <s>Āryaprajñāpāramitā</s>: 'Some [beings] are magically produced by <s>Śrāvakas</s>, some by <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, some by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, some by <s>Tathāgatas</s>, some by afflictions, some by actions. By this method, <s>Subhūti</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are produced as magical creations.' But this is the distinction of yogins from ordinary beings: like a magician, through their complete knowledge of that illusion exactly as it is, they do not become attached to it as real.

body.text: tena te yogina ucyante / ye tāṃ bālapṛthagjanavat kautūhalaṃ styatvenābhiniviṣṭāste viparītābhiniveśad bāla ucyante iti sarvamaviruddham / tathā coktam āryadharmasaṅgītau-
body.translated_text: Therefore they are called <s>yogins</s>. Those who, like childish ordinary people, are attached to that [emptiness] with curious fascination as something real—they are called 'childish' because of their distorted attachment. Thus everything is consistent. And thus it is stated in the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṅgīti</s>:

children.translated_text: Just as a certain magician strives for the liberation of his creation,

children.text: na cāsya nirmite saṅgo jñātapūrvo yato 'sya saḥ //
children.translated_text: yet he has no attachment to his creation, since he has known it from the beginning;

body.text:
tribhavaṃ nirmitaprakhyaṃ jñātvā sambodhipāragaḥ /
saṃnahyate jagaddhetorjñātapūrvaṃ jagat tathā // iti /
body.translated_text:
knowing the three realms to be like a creation, one who has reached the shore of awakening
girds himself for the sake of the world, having known the world likewise from the beginning.

body.text: evamanena krameṇa tattvaṃ bhāvayet /
body.translated_text: In this manner, by this method, one should meditate on reality.

body.text: tatra ca layauddhatyādīn vyutthitān pūrvavat praśamayet / yadā tu sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatālambane ca layauddhatyādirahitam anabhisaṃskāreṇa pravṛttaṃ jñānaṃ bhavati, tadā śamathavipaśyanāyuganaddhavāhī mārgo niṣpanno bhavati / tathā yāvat śaknoti tāvad adhimuktibalena adhimukticaryābhūmau sthito bhāvayet /
body.translated_text: Therein, one should pacify dullness, excitement, and the like when they arise, as before. But when the knowledge that operates effortlessly, free from dullness, excitement, and so forth, with the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> as its object, arises—then the path that yokes <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) together is accomplished. Thus, as long as one is able, one should meditate while established on the stage of devoted conduct by the power of aspiration.

body.text: tato yathecchaṃ paryaṅkamābhujya vyutthāya punarevaṃ cintayet / yadi nāmāmī dharmāḥ paramārthata eva niḥsvabhāvā apyete saṃvṛtyā sthitā eva / tathā coktam āryaratnameghe- "kathaṃ bodhisattvo nairātmyakuśalo bhavati? iha kulaputra, bodhisattvaḥ samyakprajñayā rūpaṃ pratyevakṣate, vedanāṃ saṃjñāṃ saṃskārān vijñānaṃ pratyavekṣate / sa rūpaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇo rūpasyotpādaṃ nopalabhate, virodhaṃ nopalabhate, samudayaṃ nopalabhate / evaṃ vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ vijñānasyotpādaṃ nopalabhate, nirodhaṃ nopalabhate, samudayaṃ nopalabhate / ayaṃ ca paramārthato 'nutpādavihāriṇyāḥ prajñāyā na punarvyāvahārikeṇa svabhāvena" iti vistaraḥ / ete ca bālabuddhaya evaṃ niḥsvabhāveṣu bhāveṣu
body.translated_text: Then, having risen from the cross-legged position as one wishes, one should again reflect thus: although these <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately without own-nature, they are established in conventional [truth]. And thus it is stated in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s>: "How does a <s>bodhisattva</s> become skilled in <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness)? Here, son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> examines <s>rūpa</s> (form) with correct <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), examines <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). Examining form, he does not apprehend the arising of form, does not apprehend its cessation, does not apprehend its origination. Likewise, he does not apprehend the arising of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, does not apprehend their cessation, does not apprehend their origination. And this is the <s>prajñā</s> that abides in <s>anutpāda</s> (non-arising) in the ultimate sense, not by its conventional nature." Thus in detail. And these beings of childish intelligence, in entities that are thus without own-nature,

body.text: viparītābhiniveśāt saṃsāre paribhramanto vividhāni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavanti / mahākaruṇām eva āmukhīkṛtya evamanuvicintayet- tathāhaṃ kariṣyāmi yathā sarvajñatvaṃ prāpya eteṣāṃ dharmatāmavabodhayeyamiti /
body.translated_text: due to distorted clinging, wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> and experience manifold sufferings. Having placed <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) at the forefront, one should reflect thus: 'I shall act in such a way that, having attained omniscience, I may awaken them to the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of dharmas).'

body.text: tataḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ pūjāstotropahāraṃ kṛtvā āryabhadracaryāpraṇidhānamabhinirharet / tataḥ śūnyatākaruṇāgarbha eva sakaladānādipuṇyajñānasambhāropārjane pravartate / tathā coktam āryadharmasaṃgītau- "yathābhūtadarśino bodhisattvasya sattveṣu mahākaruṇā pravartate / evaṃ cāsya bhavati- idaṃ mayā samādhimukhaṃ sarvadharmayathābhūtadarśaṃ ca sarvasattvānāṃ nispādayitavyam / sa tayā mahākaruṇayā saṃcodyamāno 'dhiśīlam adhicittam adhiprajñaṃ ca śikṣātrayaṃ paripūryānuttaraṃ samyaksambodhim abhisambudhyate" iti /
body.translated_text: Then, having made offerings, hymns of praise, and presentations to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, one should bring forth the aspiration of the <s>Ārya-Bhadracaryā</s> (Noble Good Conduct). Then, with <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) at its core, one engages in the accumulation of the stores of merit and knowledge through giving and the rest. And thus it is stated in the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṅgīti</s>: "For the <s>bodhisattva</s> who sees things as they truly are, <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) arises toward beings. And thus this thought arises in him: 'I must accomplish for all beings this gateway of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and the seeing of all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are.' Urged by that great compassion, by fulfilling the threefold training—higher moral conduct, higher mind, and higher wisdom—he fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening."

body.text: ayameva prajñopāyayuganaddhabāhī bodhisattvānāṃ mārgo yat paramārthadarśane 'pi saṃvṛtiṃ nocchedayanti / saṃvṛtiṃ cānucchedayanto mahākaruṇāpūrvaṅgamā aviparyastā eva sattvārthakriyāsu pravartante / uktam āryaratnameghe- "kathaṃ bodhisattvo mahāyānakuśalo bhavati / iha bodhisattvaḥ sarvāsu śikṣāsu śikṣate, śikṣāmārgaṃ ca nopalabhate / yacca śikṣate tadapi nopalabhate / yaśca śikṣyate tamapi nopalabhate / na ca taddhetukaṃ tannidānaṃ tatpratyayam ucchedadṛṣṭau patati" iti / āryadharmasaṃgītau coktam- "katamā bodhisattvānāṃ pratipattiḥ? yat kiñcid bodhisattvānāṃ kāyakarma, yat kiñcid vākkarma, yat kiñcin manaḥkarma, tat sarvasattvāpekṣakaṃ pravartate, mahākaruṇāpūrvaṅgamatvāt / mahākaruṇādhipatyaṃ sarvasattvāhitasukhādhyāśayasamutthitam" iti / ayamevaṃ hitāśayaḥ saṃjñībhavati / sā mayā
body.translated_text: This is the very path of <s>bodhisattvas</s> that yokes <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) together: that even in the seeing of ultimate reality, they do not annihilate conventional truth. And not annihilating conventional truth, preceded by <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion), without distortion, they engage in actions for the welfare of beings. As stated in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s>: "How does a <s>bodhisattva</s> become skilled in <s>Mahāyāna</s>? Here, the <s>bodhisattva</s> trains in all trainings, yet does not apprehend the path of training. And what he trains in, that too he does not apprehend. And the one who is being trained, him too he does not apprehend. Yet he does not fall into the annihilationist view that this is caused by that, conditioned by that, dependent on that." And in the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṅgīti</s> it is stated: "What is the practice of <s>bodhisattvas</s>? Whatever bodily action, whatever verbal action, whatever mental action of <s>bodhisattvas</s>—all of that proceeds with regard to all beings, since it is preceded by <s>mahākaruṇā</s>. It arises under the dominion of great compassion, from the intention for the welfare and happiness of all beings." One who has such an intention for welfare becomes conscious [of this]: 'That by me

body.text: pratipattiḥ pratipattavyā sarvasattvānāṃ hitāvahā sukhāvahā / tasya skandheṣu māyāvat pratyavekṣaṇā pratipattirna ca skandhaparityāgaṃ spṛhayatīti / dhātuṣvāśīviṣavat pratyavekṣaṇā pratipattirna ca dhātuparityāgaṃ spṛhayatīti / āyataneṣu śūnyagrāmavat pratyavekṣaṇāpratipattirna cāyatanaparityāgaṃ spṛhayatīti / rūpasya phenapiṇḍavat pratyavekṣaṇā pratipattirna ca tathāgatarūpakāyaviṭhapanāṃ jahāti / vedanāyā budbudvat pratyavekṣaṇā pratipattirna ca tathāgatadhyānasamādhisamāpattisukhaniṣpadanaprayogaṃ nārabhate / saṃjñāyāṃ marīcivat pratyavekṣaṇā pratipattirna ca tathāgatajñānaniṣpādana apratipattiḥ / saṃskārāṇāṃ kadalīvat pratyavekṣaṇā pratipattirna ca buddhadharmasaṃskārāṇām apratipattiḥ / vijñānasya māyāvat pratyavekṣaṇā pratipattirna ca jñānapūrvaṅgamakāyavāṅmanaskarmaniṣpādanā pratipattiḥ" iti vistaraḥ / evam aparyanteṣu sūtrānteṣu prajñopāyarūpā pratipattiranugantavyā /
body.translated_text: practice must be practiced—that which brings welfare and happiness to all beings. His practice is to examine the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) as if illusions, yet he does not aspire to abandon the aggregates. His practice is to examine the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) as if venomous snakes, yet he does not aspire to abandon the elements. His practice is to examine the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) as if an empty village, yet he does not aspire to abandon the sense bases. His practice is to examine <s>rūpa</s> (form) as if a lump of foam, yet he does not abandon the establishment of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> form body. His practice is to examine <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) as if a bubble, yet he does not fail to apply himself to the accomplishment of the happiness of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment). His practice is to examine <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception) as if a mirage, yet there is no failure to practice for the accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge. His practice is to examine <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) as if a plantain tree, yet there is no failure to practice the formations of <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. His practice is to examine <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) as if an illusion, yet his practice is the accomplishment of body, speech, and mental actions preceded by knowledge." Thus in detail. In this way, from the countless <s>sūtras</s>, the practice in the form of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) should be understood.

body.text: tatra yadi nāma lokottaraprajñāvasthāyām upāyasevanā na sambhavati, upāyasevanākāle tu bodhisattvasya māyākāravad aviparyastatvāt lokottarajñānāt prayogapṛṣṭhabhāvani yathāvad vastuparamārthatattvābhiniveśanī prajñāsambhavatyeveti, bhavatyeva prajñopāyayuganaddhavāhī mārgaḥ / āryakṣayamatinirdeśe ca dhyānākṣayatayā prajñopāyayuganaddhavāhī mārgo 'nugantavyaḥ / evamanena krameṇa bodhisattvasya prajñām upāyaṃ ca satataṃ satkṛtya dīrghakālābhyāsena bhāvayato dvādaśāvasthāviśeṣā bhavanti / tā evāvasthā uttarottaraguṇapratiṣṭhārthena bhūmayo vyavasthāpyante / adhimukticaryābhūmeryāvad buddhabhūmiriti /
body.translated_text: Therein, although cultivation of <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) does not occur in the state of supramundane <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), yet when the <s>bodhisattva</s> is cultivating skillful means, since he is undistorted like a magician, from supramundane <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) in its post-attainment aspect, the <s>prajñā</s> that correctly realizes the ultimate truth of things arises—therefore the path that yokes <s>prajñā</s> and <s>upāya</s> together indeed exists. And in the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamatinirdeśa</s>, the path that yokes wisdom and skillful means together should be understood through the inexhaustibility of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). In this manner, by this method, for the <s>bodhisattva</s> who continually and respectfully cultivates <s>prajñā</s> and <s>upāya</s> through long practice, twelve stages of distinction arise. These very stages are established as <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) for the purpose of grounding successively higher qualities—from the stage of devoted conduct up to the <s>Buddha</s> stage.

body.text: tatra yāvat pudgaladharmanairātmyatvaṃ na sākṣātkaroti, kevalaṃ dṛḍhatarādhimuktiḥ / mārādibhirapyabhedyo yadādhimuktibalena tattvaṃ bhavayati, tadā
body.translated_text: Therein, so long as one has not directly realized the <s>pudgala-dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of persons and dharmas), there is merely very firm aspiration. When, by the power of aspiration, one meditates on reality, unbreakable even by <s>Māra</s> and others, then

body.text: dṛḍhādhimuktito 'dhimukticaryābhūmirvyavasthāpyate / asyāmapi bhūmau vartamāno bodhisattva pṛthagjano 'pi sarvabālavipattisamatikrānto 'saṃkhyeyasamādhidhāraṇīvimokṣābhijñādiguṇānvita āryaratnameghe paṭhyate /
body.translated_text: from that firm aspiration, the <s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s> (stage of devoted conduct) is established. Even a <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding on this stage, though still an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), has surpassed all the misfortunes of the childish and is described in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s> as endowed with the qualities of innumerable <s>samādhis</s>, <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, liberations, <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and so forth.

body.text: asyā eva ca mṛdumadhyādhimātrādhimātratarāvasthācatuṣṭayena catvāri nirvedhabhāgīyāni vyavasthāpyante / tathā hi yadā [bāhyārtha vibhāvayatā] īṣatspaṣṭo jñānāloko bhavati tadā uṣmagatanāmakaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyaṃ bhavati / sa cātra mahāyāna ālokalabdhasamādhirucyate / yadā tu sa eva jñānaloko madhyamaspaṣṭo bhavati, tadā mūrdhanāmakanirvedhabhāgīyaṃ bhavati, vṛddhālokaśca samādhirucyate / yadā tu spaṣṭataro bāhyārthānābhāsajñānāloko jāyate, tadā vijñaptimātrāvasthānāt kṣāntināmakaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyaṃ bhavati / ekadeśapraviṣṭaśca samādhirucyate / grāhyakārānupalambhapraveśāt / yadā tu grāhyagrāhakākārarahitam advayaṃ jñānaṃ vibhāvayet tadāgradharmākhyaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyaṃ bhavati / ānantaryaśca sa samādhirucyate, tadanantarameva tattvapraveśāt / atra tāvad adhimukticaryābhūmi /
body.translated_text: And by the fourfold [divisions] of this very [stage]—mild, moderate, intense, and most intense—the four <s>nirvedhabhāgīyas</s> (penetrative factors) are established. For when, [while analyzing external objects], the light of knowledge becomes slightly clear, then the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> called <s>uṣmagata</s> (heat) arises. And here in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> it is called the <s>samādhi</s> of 'obtained light.' When that very light of knowledge becomes moderately clear, then the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> called <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit) arises, and it is called the <s>samādhi</s> of 'increased light.' When a clearer light of knowledge arises in which external objects do not appear, then, because one abides in the <s>vijñaptimātra</s> (mere representation) state, the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> called <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) arises. And it is called the <s>samādhi</s> of 'partial entry'—because of entering the non-apprehension of the aspect of the graspable. When one discriminates the non-dual <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) free from the aspects of both graspable and grasper, then the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> called <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma) arises. And that <s>samādhi</s> is called <s>ānantarya</s> (immediate)—because immediately after it there is entry into reality. Thus far is the <s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s> (stage of devoted conduct).

body.text: itarāstu bhūmayaḥ saṃkṣepata ekādaśāṅgaparipūritā vyavasthāpyante / tatra prathamā bhūmiḥ prathamaṃ pudgaladharmanairātmyatattvādhigamāṅgaparipūritā vyavasthāpyate / tathā hi yadāgradharmānantaraṃ prathamataraṃ lokottaraṃ sarvaprapañcarahitaṃ sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatāsākṣātkāri sphuṭataraṃ jñānam utpadyate, tadā bodhisattvaḥ samyaktvanyayābhāvakrāntito darśanamārgotpādāt prathamāṃ bhūmiṃ praviṣṭo bhavati / ata evāsyāṃ bhūmau prathamato 'nadhigatatattvādhigamād bodhisattvaḥ pramudito bhavati / tata eṣā bhūmiḥ pramuditetyucyate / atra ca dvādaśottaraṃ darśanaheyaṃ kleśaśataṃ prahīyate /
body.translated_text: The other <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) are established as fulfilled by eleven aspects in brief. Among these, the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) is established as fulfilled by the aspect of the initial realization of the truth of <s>pudgala-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of persons) and <s>dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of phenomena). For when, immediately after the <s>agradharmāḥ</s> (supreme dharmas), the very first supramundane knowledge arises — free from all conceptual elaboration, directly realizing the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), utterly clear — then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having entered the certainty of the correct path through the arising of the <s>darśanamārga</s> (path of seeing), has entered the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). For this very reason, on this <s>bhūmi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes joyful because of attaining for the first time the truth not previously attained. Therefore this <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Pramuditā</s> (the Joyful). Here, one hundred and twelve <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) to be abandoned by seeing are relinquished.

body.text: śeṣāstu bhūmayo bhāvanāmārgasvabhāvāḥ / tāsu bhāvanāheyāstraidhātukāḥ ṣoḍaśa kleśāḥ prahīyante / asyāṃ ca bhūmau bodhisattvasya dharmadhātusamudāgamatāprabodhāt svārtha iva parāthe pravartanād dānapāramitātiriktatarā bhavati / sa ca bodhisattvaḥ samadhigatatattvo 'pi vā yāvann śaknoti sūkṣmāpattiskhaliteṣu samprajanyavihāri bhavituṃ tāvat prathamā bhūmiḥ / yadā tu śaknoti, tadāsyāṅgasya paripūrito dvitīyā bhūmirvyavasthāpyate / ata evāsyāṃ bhūmau sūkṣmāpattiskhalitasamudācārāt śīlapāramitātiriktatarā bhavati / sarvadauśśīlyamalāpagamād iyaṃ bhūmirvimaletyucyate /
body.translated_text: The remaining <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) are of the nature of the <s>bhāvanāmārga</s> (path of cultivation). On them, sixteen <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of the three realms to be abandoned by cultivation are relinquished. On this <s>bhūmi</s>, because the <s>Bodhisattva</s> awakens to the full realization of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), and because he engages in benefiting others just as in his own benefit, the <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity) becomes predominant. And that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even though he has realized the truth, as long as he is unable to dwell in full awareness regarding subtle transgressions and lapses, that is the first <s>bhūmi</s>. But when he is able, then, with the fulfillment of that aspect, the second <s>bhūmi</s> is established. For this very reason, on this <s>bhūmi</s>, because of the arising of subtle transgressions and lapses, the <s>śīla-pāramitā</s> (perfection of moral discipline) becomes predominant. Because all stains of immorality are removed, this <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Vimalā</s> (the Stainless).

body.text: sa sūkṣmāpattiskhaliteṣu samprajanyavihārī bhavati / yāvanna śaknoti sakalalaukikaṃ samādhiṃ samāpattuṃ yathāśrutaṃ cārtham ādharttuṃ tāvad dvitīyaiva bhūmiḥ / yadā śaknoti, tadā tasyāṅgasya paripūritastṛtīyā bhūmirvyavasthāpyate / asyāṃ ca bhūmau bodhisattvasya śrutadhāraṇyā sarvalaukikasamādhyābhinirhārārthaṃ sarvaduḥkhasahanāt, kṣāntipāramitātiriktatarā bhavati / teṣāṃ samādhīnāṃ lābhād iya bhūmirapramāṇaṃ lokottaraṃ jñānāvabhāsaṃ karotīti prabhākarītyucyate /
body.translated_text: He dwells in full awareness regarding subtle transgressions and lapses. As long as he is unable to attain the complete worldly <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) and to retain the meaning of what has been heard, that is still the second <s>bhūmi</s>. When he is able, then, with the fulfillment of that aspect, the third <s>bhūmi</s> is established. On this <s>bhūmi</s>, because the <s>Bodhisattva</s> endures all suffering for the purpose of accomplishing all worldly <s>samādhis</s> (meditative concentrations) through the retention of what has been learned, the <s>kṣānti-pāramitā</s> (perfection of patience) becomes predominant. Because of the attainment of those <s>samādhis</s>, this <s>bhūmi</s> produces an immeasurable radiance of supramundane knowledge, and therefore it is called <s>Prabhākarī</s> (the Luminous).

body.text: sa pratilabdhalaukikasakalasamādhirapi yāvann śaknoti yathāpratilabdhairbodhipakṣairdharmairbahulaṃ vihartuṃ sarvasamāpattīnāṃ ca cittam upekṣituṃ tāvat tṛtīyā bhūmiḥ / yadā tu śaknoti tadā tasyāṅgasya paripūritaścaturthī bhūmirvyavasthāpyate / asyāṃ bhūmau bodhisattvasyābhīkṣṇaṃ kāyavāṅmanojalpasamatikramaṇāaya bodhipakṣairdharmairviharaṇāt, viryaparamitātiriktatarābhavati / iyaṃ ca sakalakleśendhanadāhasamarthasya bodhipakṣadharmārciṣa udgatatvād arciṣmatītyucyate /
body.translated_text: He has attained all worldly <s>samādhis</s> (meditative concentrations), yet as long as he is unable to dwell extensively in the <s>bodhipakṣa-dharmāḥ</s> (factors of awakening) as attained, and to maintain equanimity of mind toward all meditative attainments, that is the third <s>bhūmi</s>. When he is able, then, with the fulfillment of that aspect, the fourth <s>bhūmi</s> is established. On this <s>bhūmi</s>, because the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwells in the <s>bodhipakṣa-dharmāḥ</s> (factors of awakening) for the purpose of constantly transcending the mental chatter of body, speech, and mind, the <s>vīrya-pāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor) becomes predominant. And this <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (the Blazing), because the flame of the <s>bodhipakṣa-dharmāḥ</s> (factors of awakening), capable of burning the fuel of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), blazes forth.

body.text: so 'bhīkṣṇaṃ bodhipakṣadharmavihārī bhavati / yāvanna śaknoti satyāni bhāvayan saṃsārānabhimukhaṃ nirvāṇābhimukhaṃ ca ceto vyāvartayitum upāyasaṃgṛhītān
body.translated_text: He dwells constantly in the <s>bodhipakṣa-dharmāḥ</s> (factors of awakening). As long as he is unable, while cultivating the truths, to turn away the mind from its orientation toward <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) and toward <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation), and to cultivate the <s>bodhipakṣa-dharmāḥ</s> (factors of awakening) integrated with skillful means

body.text: bodhipakṣān dharmān bhāvayitum, tāvaccaturthī bhūmiḥ / yadā tu śaknoti tadāsyāṅgasya paripūritaḥ pañcamī bhūmirvyavasthāpyate / ata evāsyām iyam upāyasaṃgṛhītā bodhipakṣabhāvanā [paripūritena] suṣṭhu duḥkhena jīyate abhyasyatā iti sudurjayetyujyate /
body.translated_text: , that is the fourth <s>bhūmi</s>. When he is able, then, with the fulfillment of that aspect, the fifth <s>bhūmi</s> is established. For this very reason, on this <s>bhūmi</s>, this cultivation of the <s>bodhipakṣa-dharmāḥ</s> (factors of awakening) integrated with skillful means is extremely difficult to master through practice, hence it is called <s>Sudurjayā</s> (the Extremely Difficult to Conquer).

body.text: asyāṃ cāryasatyākārabhāvanābahulīkārād dhyānapāramitā atiriktatarā bhavati / upayasaṃgṛhītabodhipakṣabahulavihārī ca bhavati / yāvad na śaknoti saṃsārapravṛttipratyavekṣaṇān nirvitsahayā cittasantatyānimittavihāraṃ samāpattuṃ tāvat pañcamī bhūmiḥ / yadā śaknoti tadāsyāṅgasya paripūritaḥ ṣaṣṭhī bhūmirvyavasthāpyate / asyāṃ ca bodhisattvasya pratītyasamutpādabhāvanāvihārāt prajñāpāramitātiriktatarā bhavati / ata eva prajñāpāramitāyā atiriktataratvāt sarvabuddhadharmeṣu abhimukho 'syāṃ bhūmau vartata iti kṛtvā abhimukhītyucyate /
body.translated_text: On this <s>bhūmi</s>, because of the intensive cultivation of the aspects of the <s>āryasatya</s> (noble truths), the <s>dhyāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation) becomes predominant. And he dwells extensively in the <s>bodhipakṣa-dharmāḥ</s> (factors of awakening) integrated with skillful means. As long as he is unable, through the examination of the process of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), to attain the signless abiding of the mental continuum accompanied by disenchantment, that is the fifth <s>bhūmi</s>. When he is able, then, with the fulfillment of that aspect, the sixth <s>bhūmi</s> is established. On this <s>bhūmi</s>, because of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s dwelling in the cultivation of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) becomes predominant. For this very reason, because the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) is predominant, on this <s>bhūmi</s> one is turned toward all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> (qualities of a Buddha), and therefore it is called <s>Abhimukhī</s> (the Manifest).

body.text: so 'nimittavihāralābhī bhavati / yāvanna śaknoti niśchidram animittavihāraṃ samāpattum, tāvat ṣaṣṭhī bhūmiḥ / yadā śaknoti tadāsyāṅgasya paripūritaḥ saptamī bhūmirvyavasthāpyate / asyāmapi bhūmau bodhisattvaḥ sarvanimittaṃ nirnimittena pratividhyati nimittakṛtavyavahāraṃ ca na virodhayati / ato 'syām upāyapāramitātiriktatarā bhavati / iyaṃ ca bhūmiranābhogamārgopaśleṣāt suṣṭhu dūraṅgamād dūraṅgamā /
body.translated_text: He attains the signless abiding. As long as he is unable to attain the signless abiding without interruption, that is the sixth <s>bhūmi</s>. When he is able, then, with the fulfillment of that aspect, the seventh <s>bhūmi</s> is established. On this <s>bhūmi</s> too, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> penetrates all signs through the signless, yet does not oppose conventional activity based on signs. Therefore, on this <s>bhūmi</s>, the <s>upāya-pāramitā</s> (perfection of skillful means) becomes predominant. And this <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Dūraṅgamā</s> (the Far-Going), because it closely approaches the path of effortless activity and thus goes exceedingly far.

body.text: sa niśchidrānimittāvihāri bhavati / yāvanna śaknotyanābhogavāhinam animittavihāraṃ samāpattuṃ tāvat saptamī bhūmiḥ / yadā śaknoti tadāsyāṅgasya paripūrito 'ṣṭamī bhūmirvyavasthāpyate / asyāṃ ca bhūmau anābhogena kuśalapakṣayogāt praṇidhānapāramitātiriktatarā bhavati / animittābhogāprakampyatvād iyam acaletyucyate /
body.translated_text: He dwells in the signless abiding without interruption. As long as he is unable to attain the signless abiding that flows effortlessly, that is the seventh <s>bhūmi</s>. When he is able, then, with the fulfillment of that aspect, the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> is established. On this <s>bhūmi</s>, because of the effortless engagement in the wholesome class, the <s>praṇidhāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of aspiration) becomes predominant. Because it is unshakable by the signless and effortless, this <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Acalā</s> (the Immovable).

body.text: so 'nābhogānimittavihārī ca bhavati / yāvanna śaknoti paryāyaniruktyādiprabhedaiḥ sarvākārasarvadharmadeśanāyāṃ vaśībhavituṃ tāvad aṣṭamī bhūmiḥ / yadā śaknoti tadāsyāṅgasya paripūrito navamī bhūmirvyavasthāpyate / asyāṃ ca bhūmau bodhisattvasya pratisaṃvid- viśeṣalābhāt prajñābalaviśeṣayogād balapāramitātiriktatarā bhavati / sarvākāradharmadeśanākauśalato 'navadyamativiśeṣalābhāt sādhumatī bhūmirucyate /
body.translated_text: He dwells in the effortless signless abiding. As long as he is unable to gain mastery in teaching all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) in all aspects through various approaches such as etymological explanation and other divisions, that is the eighth <s>bhūmi</s>. When he is able, then, with the fulfillment of that aspect, the ninth <s>bhūmi</s> is established. On this <s>bhūmi</s>, because of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s attainment of the distinctive <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge) and the special power of wisdom, the <s>bala-pāramitā</s> (perfection of powers) becomes predominant. Because of the attainment of the distinctive excellence of faultless intellect through skill in teaching all <s>dharmas</s> in all aspects, this <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Sādhumatī</s> (the Good Intelligence).

body.text: asyāṃ ca pratisaṃviccatuṣṭayalabhī bhavati / yāvanna śaknoti buddhakṣetraparṣannirmāṇādi darśayituṃ paripūrṇadharmasambhogaṃ sattvaparipākaṃ ca kartum, tāvad navamī bhūmiḥ / yadā tu śaknoti tadāsyāṅgasya paripūrito daśamī bhūmirvyavasthāpyate / asyāṃ ca nirmāṇādinā sattvaparipācanāya jñānaviśeṣayogād bodhisattvasya jñānapāramitātiriktatarā bhavati / iyaṃ ca dharmadeśanāmeghaiḥ ananteṣu lokadhātuṣu dharmapravarṣaṇād dharmameghetyucyate / aparairapi skandhapariśuddhayādivyavasthāpanaiḥ bhūmīnāṃ vyavasthāpanamasti, granthavistarabhayān na likhitam /
body.translated_text: On this <s>bhūmi</s>, he attains the fourfold <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge). As long as he is unable to display the creation of <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields), assemblies, emanations, and so forth, and to bring about the complete enjoyment of the <s>Dharma</s> and the maturation of sentient beings, that is the ninth <s>bhūmi</s>. When he is able, then, with the fulfillment of that aspect, the tenth <s>bhūmi</s> is established. On this <s>bhūmi</s>, because of the special power of knowledge for maturing sentient beings through emanations and other means, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>jñāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of knowledge) becomes predominant. And this <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Dharmameghā</s> (the Cloud of Dharma), because it rains the <s>Dharma</s> upon countless world-realms through clouds of <s>Dharma</s>-teaching. There are also other ways of establishing the <s>bhūmis</s> through the purification of the aggregates and so forth, but these have not been written out for fear of excessive length.

body.text: sa pratilabdha- nirmāṇādivaśito 'pi yāvan na śaknoti sarvasmin jñeye sarvākāram asaktam / apratihataṃ jñānam utpādayituṃ tāvad daśamī bhūmi / yadā śaknoti tadāsyāṅgasya paripūrito buddhabhūmirvyavasthāpyate / etacca bhūmivyavasthāpanam āryasaṃdhinirmocane nirdiṣṭam / asyāśca buddhabhūmeḥ sarvākārasakalasaṃpatprakarṣḍaparyantagamanānnāparam utkṛṣṭaṃ sthānāntaramasti [tasmāt tataḥ paraṃ nāsti bhūmivyavasthā] iti /
body.translated_text: He has attained mastery over emanations and so forth, yet as long as he is unable to produce knowledge that is unobstructed, unhindered, and in all aspects with regard to everything knowable, that is the tenth <s>bhūmi</s>. When he is able, then, with the fulfillment of that aspect, the <s>Buddha-bhūmi</s> (stage of Buddhahood) is established. This establishment of the <s>bhūmis</s> has been taught in the <s>Ārya-Saṃdhinirmocana</s> (Noble Sūtra of the Explanation of the Profound Secret). And because this <s>Buddha-bhūmi</s> reaches the ultimate culmination of all perfect excellences in every aspect, there is no other state higher than it. Therefore, beyond it there is no further establishment of <s>bhūmis</s>.

body.text: asyāśca buddhamūmerguṇapakṣaprabhedo buddhairapi na śakyate sarvākāraṃ vaktum / tasyā aprameyatvāt, kathaṃ punaḥ asmatsadṛśaiḥ / yathoktam āryagaṇḍavyūhe-
body.translated_text: The division of the qualities of this <s>Buddha-bhūmi</s> (stage of Buddhahood) cannot be fully expressed in all aspects even by the <s>Buddhas</s> themselves, because it is immeasurable. How then could it be expressed by those like us? As stated in the <s>Ārya-Gaṇḍavyūha</s> —

body.text:
guṇaikadeśa-paryanta nādhigacchet svayaṃbhuvaḥ /
nirīkṣyamāṇo buddho 'pi buddhadharmā hyacintiyāḥ // iti /
body.translated_text: "Even a <s>Buddha</s>, examining, would not reach the limit of even a portion of the qualities of the Self-Arisen One; for the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> are inconceivable."

body.text: etāvattu saṃkṣepeṇa vaktuṃ śakyate / [svaparārthasampattiprakarṣaparyantagataḥ, aśeṣadoṣāpagamaniṣṭhāṃ prāpya bhagavān buddho dharmakāye sthitvā sambhoganirmāṇakāyābhyām anābhogarūpeṇa aśeṣajagadartha kurvan yāvat saṃsāraṃ viharati /
body.translated_text: But this much can be said in brief: Having reached the ultimate culmination of the perfection of benefit for self and others, having attained the finality of the removal of all faults, the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, abiding in the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth body), through the <s>Saṃbhogakāya</s> (enjoyment body) and <s>Nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body), effortlessly accomplishing the welfare of all sentient beings without exception, dwells as long as <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) endures.

body.text: tasmāt prekṣavadbhiḥ sarvaguṇākareṣu bhagavatsu śraddhā utpadanīyā, tadguṇaparisādhanārthaṃ sarvaprakāreṇa prayatitavyam / trikāyadivibhāgastu granthavistarabhayānna likhyate /
body.translated_text: Therefore, by the discerning, faith should be generated in the Blessed Ones who are the repositories of all excellent qualities, and every effort should be made in all ways for the purpose of accomplishing those qualities. The division into the three <s>kāyas</s> (bodies) and so forth, however, is not written out for fear of excessive length.

children.text: nayasyānusāreṇa sūtrasya cāṭha saduktyāsya mārgasya jinaputrakāṇām /
children.translated_text: Following the method and the meaning of the <s>sūtras</s>, with good exposition, this path for the sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One) —

children.text: mayānalpapuṇyaṃ yadāptaṃ ca tena parāmetu buddhiṃ jaganmandamāśu //
children.translated_text: whatever merit has been obtained by me through this, may the world, which is dull, swiftly attain the wisdom of the highest.

body.text: bhūpatiśrīdevarājavacanena] kamalaśīlena bhāvanākramasya ayaṃ saṃkṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text: At the command of the sovereign <s>Śrī Devarāja</s>, this abridgment of the <s>Bhāvanākrama</s> was composed by <s>Kamalaśīla</s>.

body.text: bhāvanākramaḥ prathamaḥ samāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: The first <s>Bhāvanākrama</s> (Stages of Meditation) is completed.

body.text: 2. bhāvanākramo dvitīyaḥ
body.translated_text: 2. The Second <s>Bhāvanākrama</s>

body.text: namo mañjuśriye kumārabhūtāya /
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful!

body.text: mahāyānasūtranayānupraviśyamānānāṃ bhāvanākramaḥ saṃkṣepataḥ kathyate / iha atīśighraṃ sarvajñatāprāptukāmena prekṣāvatā tatprāpaka-hetu-pratyayebhyo 'bhiyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The stages of meditation (<s>bhāvanākrama</s>) for those entering into the method of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s> are stated in brief. Here, a discerning person who desires to attain omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) most swiftly should apply effort toward the causes and conditions that bring about its attainment.

body.text: itthamiyaṃ sarvajñatā tu hetuṃ vinā bhavituṃ na yujyate, sarvasyāpi sarvadā sarvajñatābhāvaprasaṅgatvāt / nirapekṣabhāve tu kutrāpi pratigho na syād, yato hi sarve 'pi sarvajñā eva na bhavanti / kiṃ tarhi kasyacit kadācit kiñcinmātraṃmūtatvāt sarvaṃ hi vastu hetusāpekṣameva / sarvajñatāpi kutracit kadācit kiñcit saṃbhāvyate / sarvasminnapi kāle nāsti, sarvasmin sthāne nāsti, sarvamapi nāsti, tasmāt sā tu niyatameva hetupratyayasāpekṣā / taddhetupratyayeṣvapi abhrāntā avikalāśca sevitavyāḥ / bhrantahetvanuṣṭhāne tu atidīrghakālenāpi na iṣṭaphala-prāptiḥ / yathā-śṛṅgāt payodohavat / sakalahetusevanaṃ vināpi na phalotpādaḥ / bījādiṣu kasyacidapi abhāve aṅkurādiphalānutpādāt / tasmāt tatphalakāmenābhrāntasakalaṃ hetupratyayaṃ sevanīyam /
body.translated_text: In this way, omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) cannot arise without a cause, because otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of everyone always being omniscient. If [omniscience] were independent [of causes], there would be no obstruction anywhere — yet all beings are not omniscient. Rather, because it occurs only for someone, at some time, to some extent, everything is indeed dependent on causes. Omniscience too is possible somewhere, at some time, to some extent; it does not exist at all times, it does not exist in all places, it does not exist as everything — therefore it is necessarily dependent on causes and conditions. In pursuing those causes and conditions too, one must follow them without error and completely. If one practices with mistaken causes, even over an extremely long time one will not attain the desired fruit — like trying to milk from a horn. Without cultivating all the causes, no fruit arises — because if even one among the seed and other [factors] is absent, the fruit of a sprout and so forth does not arise. Therefore, one who desires that fruit must cultivate all the causes and conditions without error.

body.text: ke hetupratyayāḥ sarvajñatāphalasya iti? ucyate, mādṛśo jātyandhasadṛśastān darśayituṃ na śaknoti, tathāpi bhagavataivābhisaṃbuddhaya vineyajanebhyo yathoktaṃ tathaiva mayā bhagavadvacanenaiva kathyate / bhagavāṃstan avocat- "guhyādhipate! tat sarvajñajñānaṃ karuṇāmūlaṃ bodhicittahetukam upāyaparyavasānam" iti / tasmāt sarvajñatāmadhigantukāmaiḥ karuṇā-bodhicittopāyeṣu eteṣu triṣu śikṣitavyam /
body.translated_text: What are the causes and conditions for the fruit of omniscience? It is said: one like me, comparable to one born blind, is unable to show them. Nevertheless, just as the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself, upon attaining complete awakening, taught to those to be trained, so too I shall state them in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> own words. The <s>Bhagavān</s> declared: 'O Lord of Secrets (<s>Guhyādhipati</s>)! That knowledge of omniscience has compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) as its root, the awakening mind (<s>bodhicitta</s>) as its cause, and skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) as its culmination.' Therefore, those who wish to realize omniscience must train in these three: compassion, the awakening mind, and skillful means.

body.text: karuṇayā preryamāṇā bodhisattvāḥ sarvasattvābhyuddhāraṇartham avaśyaṃ pratijñāsyanti / ataḥ svātmadṛṣṭiṃ nirākṛtya atiduṣkarāvichinna-dīrghakāla-sādhītapuṇyajñānasambhāreṣu
body.translated_text: Impelled by compassion, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will inevitably make the vow to rescue all sentient beings. Therefore, having rejected the view of self, [they engage] with zeal in the extremely difficult, uninterrupted, long-term cultivation of the accumulations of merit and wisdom —

body.text: ādareṇa pravṛttiḥ / tatra praviśya paripūrṇa puṇyajñānasambhāram avaśyaṃ sādhayati / sambhārāpariniṣpattau sarvajñatā karatalagatavad bhaviṣyati / tarhi sarvajñatāmūlaṃ tu karuṇāyā eva bhūtatvāt sā tu prathamatarameva bhavanīyā / āryadharmasaṃgītisūtre- "na bhagavan bodhisattvena atibahuṣu dharmeṣu śikṣitavyam / eko dharmo bhagavan bodhisattvena svārādhitaḥ supratibiddhaḥ kartavyaḥ / tasya sarvabuddhadharmāḥ karatalagatā bhavanti / katama ekadharmaḥ? yaduta mahākaruṇā /" iti /
body.translated_text: with diligent engagement. Having entered therein, one necessarily accomplishes the complete accumulation of merit and wisdom. When the accumulations are fully completed, omniscience will be as if placed in the palm of one's hand. Since the root of omniscience is compassion itself, that must be cultivated first of all. In the <s>Āryadharmasaṃgīti Sūtra</s>: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> need not train in very many <s>dharmas</s>. One <s>dharma</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should be well mastered and well penetrated by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Through it, all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> come to rest in the palm of one's hand. What is that one <s>dharma</s>? Namely, great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>).'

body.text: mahākaruṇāparigṛhītatvād bhagavanto buddhāḥ sakalasvārthasampattilābhe 'pi sattvadhātuparyavasānaparyantaṃ tiṣṭhanti / śrāvakavad atiśānte 'pi nirvāṇanagare na praviśantiṃ / sattvān avalokya tacchāntanirvāṇanagaraṃ prajvaladayogṛhavad dūraṃ tyaktatvād bhagavatām apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇahetustu sā mahākaruṇā eva /
body.translated_text: Because they are embraced by great compassion, the blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, even upon attaining the complete fulfillment of their own welfare, remain until the end of the realm of sentient beings. They do not enter the exceedingly peaceful city of <s>nirvāṇa</s> as the <s>śrāvakas</s> do. Seeing sentient beings and having abandoned far away that peaceful city of <s>nirvāṇa</s> as if it were a blazing house — the cause of the non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>) of the <s>Bhagavāns</s> is indeed that great compassion.

body.text: atra sa karuṇābhāvanākramaḥ prathamapraveśādārabhya abhidhātavyaḥ / saṃprati upekṣābhāvanayā sarvasattveṣu anurāgaṃ dveṣaṃ ca nirasya samācittatā prathamaṃ niṣpādayitavyā /
body.translated_text: Here, the stages of the cultivation of compassion must be explained starting from the initial entry. Now, through the cultivation of equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), one must first eliminate attachment and aversion toward all sentient beings and accomplish even-mindedness.

body.text: sarve sattvāḥ sukhaṃ kāmayante, duḥkhaṃ tu na kāmayante / anādimati ca saṃsāre na kaścit sattvo yo nābhūt śataśo me bandhuriti paricintaya- taścātra ko viśeṣaḥ syāt? tarhi kasmiṃścid anurāgaḥ kasmiṃścicca dveṣo bhavet, tasmān mayā sarveṣu sattveṣu cittasamataiva kāryā iti / evaṃ manasikāreṇa madhyasthapakṣata ārabhya mitre śatrau cacittasamatāmeva bhāvayet / tataḥ sarvasattveṣu cittasamatāṃ sādhayitvā maitrīṃ bhāvayet / maitrījalena cittasaṃtānaṃ siṃcayitvā vidyamānasuvarṇabhūmivat kṛtvā karuṇābījavapane sukhena atisuvistāro bhaviṣyati / tataścittasaṃtānaṃ maitryā vāsayitvā karuṇāṃ bhāvayet /
body.translated_text: All sentient beings desire happiness and do not desire suffering. In the beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, there is no sentient being who has not been my relative hundreds of times — so reflect. What distinction, then, could there be? If attachment toward some and aversion toward others were to arise, therefore I should produce even-mindedness toward all sentient beings — thus one should attend. With such mental attention, beginning with the neutral party, one should cultivate even-mindedness toward friends and enemies alike. Then, having established even-mindedness toward all sentient beings, one should cultivate loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>). Having sprinkled the mental continuum with the water of loving-kindness, having made it like a gold-bearing ground, the sowing of the seed of compassion will very easily spread abundantly. Then, having saturated the mental continuum with loving-kindness, one should cultivate compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>).

body.text: sā ca karuṇā sarvapīḍitasattvaduḥkhāvagamecchākārāsti / lokatrayasya sarvasattvānāṃ trividhaduḥkhatayā yathāyogam atyantaduḥkhitatvāt tadartha sarvasattveṣu sā bhāvanīyā / tathā ca ye tāvannākārakāste vividhacirantanadīrghakālikadāhādi-dukheḥṣu nimagnā eva bhāvato varṇitāḥ / tathā pretā api prāyo duḥsahatīvrakṣuttṛṣuduḥkhāgnyabhisaṃśoṣitamūrtayo bahuduḥkhamanubhavanti iti varṇitāḥ / tiryañco 'pi parasparabhakṣaṇakrodhavadhahiṃsādibhiranekavidhaṃ duḥkhamanubhavanto dṛśyanta eva / manuṣyā api kāmaparyeṣaṇākārpaṇyād anyo 'nyadrohopadhātakṛtaṃ priyaviprayogāpriyasaṃyogaṃ dāridrayādyutpannam aprameyaṃ duḥkhamanubhavanto dṛśyanto /
body.translated_text: That compassion is of the nature of wishing to understand and remove the suffering of all afflicted sentient beings. Since all sentient beings of the three worlds are extremely afflicted by the three types of suffering as appropriate, compassion should be cultivated toward all sentient beings for that purpose. Thus, those in the hells are immersed in various long-lasting, prolonged sufferings of burning and the like — so it has been described. Likewise, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) mostly experience great suffering, their bodies desiccated by the fire of unbearable, intense hunger and thirst — so it has been described. Animals too are seen experiencing manifold suffering through mutual devouring, anger, killing, and violence. Humans too, from the wretchedness of seeking desires, from harm done to one another, from separation from the beloved and association with the unbeloved, from poverty and other causes, are seen experiencing immeasurable suffering.

body.text:
ye rāgādinānā-saṃkleśaparyaveṣṭitacittāḥ, ye ca vividhakudṛṣṭigahananimagnāste sarve 'pi duḥkhahetutvāt prapatasthā iva atiduḥkhitā eva / devā api sarvavipariṇāmaduḥkhaduḥkhitā eva / devā api ye kāmavacarāste 'pi nityacyavanapatanādibhayaśkopahatāḥ kathaṃ sukhitā nāma? saṃskāradu khaṃ tu karmakleśalakṣaṇaṃ hetuparatantrasvabhāvaṃ pratikṣaṇabhaṅgurasvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ ca sakalajagati vyāptam / tasmāt sakalameva jagad duḥkhāgnijvālāntarapraviṣṭam avetya yathā mama duḥkham apriyam anyeṣāmapi tādṛśam iti cintayatā / aho bata! duḥkhitā mamaite priyasattvāstu kathaṃ tadduḥkhamuktāḥ syuriti svātmaduḥkhavat kṛtvā tannivāraṇecchākārayā karuṇayā samādhyavasthāyāṃ sarvacaryāsu vāpi sarvadā sarvasattvān bhāvayet / prathamaṃ tāvad mitrapakṣeṣu anubhūtapūrvoktavividhaduḥkheṣu anupaśyatā bhāvanīyā /
tataḥ sattvasamatayāviśeṣamapaśyatā 'sarve sattvāstu me bandhubhūtā eva' iti paricintayatā madhyamapakṣeṣu bhavanīyā / yadā tatra mitrapakṣeṣviva sā karuṇā tulyā pravṛttā bhavati tadā daśasu dikṣu sarvasattveṣu bhāvayet / yadā duḥkhitapriyaśiśoḥ mātṛvat svātmano 'tipriyaṃ duḥkhata uddaraṇecchākārā svarasavāhinīṃ sarvasattveṣu samapravṛttā kṛpā bhavati tadā sā niṣpannā bhavati, mahākaruṇāvyapadeśaṃ ca labhate /
body.translated_text:
Those whose minds are enveloped by the various afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) of desire and the rest, and those who are immersed in the thickets of various wrong views — all of them, because they are causes of suffering, are like those standing at the edge of a precipice, extremely afflicted indeed. Even the gods are afflicted by the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkha</s>). Even those gods who are in the desire-realm (<s>kāmavacara</s>) are stricken by the constant fear of falling and decline — how can they be called happy? The suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkha</s>), characterized by <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>, having its nature dependent on causes, and characterized by momentary disintegration — pervades the entire world. Therefore, having understood that the entire world has entered into the flames of the fire of suffering, one should reflect: 'Just as suffering is unpleasant to me, so is it for others.' 'Alas! These dear beings of mine are suffering — how may they be freed from that suffering?' With compassion in the form of wishing to remove [their suffering], making [their suffering] like one's own, one should meditate on all sentient beings at all times, in meditative absorption as well as in all activities. First, one should meditate by observing the various previously experienced sufferings among those in the category of friends.
Then, seeing no distinction through the equality of sentient beings, reflecting 'all sentient beings are indeed my relatives,' one should meditate on those in the neutral category. When that compassion arises equally toward the neutral ones as toward friends, then one should meditate on all sentient beings in the ten directions. When compassion — in the form of wishing to lift up from suffering one's own most dear [being], like a mother toward her suffering dear child — flows spontaneously and arises equally toward all sentient beings, then it is perfected, and it obtains the designation of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>).

body.text: prathamaṃ tāvad mitrapakṣe kṛtā maitrībhāvanā sukhasaṃyogecchākārā bhavati, kramaśaḥ vyasteṣu śatruṣu cāpi bhāvanīyā / tathābhyastā ca sā karuṇā kramaśaḥ sakalasattvābhyuddharaṇecchāṃ svarasena eva utpādayati /
body.translated_text: First, the cultivation of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) performed toward the category of friends takes the form of wishing for their connection with happiness; it should be gradually cultivated also toward neutral ones and enemies. When that compassion is thus practiced, it gradually produces spontaneously the wish to rescue all sentient beings.

body.text: ato mūlakaruṇāṃ bhāvayitvā bodhicittaṃ bhāvayet / tad bodhicittaṃ tu dvividham- saṃvṛtaṃ paramārtha ca / tatra saṃvṛtaṃ tu karuṇayā sakalasattvābhyuddharaṇaṃ pratijñāya 'jagaddhitāya buddho bhaveyam' iti, anuttarasamyaksambodhicchākāraḥ prathamaścittotpādaḥ / tathāpi śīlaparivartapradarśita-vidhivad bodhisattvaḥ saṃvarasthitānyavidvatsu cittamutpādayet /
body.translated_text: Therefore, having cultivated root compassion, one should cultivate the awakening mind (<s>bodhicitta</s>). That <s>bodhicitta</s> is of two kinds: conventional (<s>saṃvṛta</s>) and ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>). Among these, the conventional [<s>bodhicitta</s>] is, having pledged through compassion to rescue all sentient beings, the first generation of the mind in the form of the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s>), [thinking] 'May I become a <s>Buddha</s> for the welfare of the world.' Furthermore, in accordance with the procedure shown in the chapter on moral conduct (<s>śīlaparivarta</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, established in the vow, should generate the mind among those who do not [yet] know.

body.text: tathā saṃvṛtabodhicittamutpādya paramārthabodhicittotpādārthaṃ prayatitavyam / tacca paramārthagocaram, vimalam, acalam, nirvātapradīpapravāhavanniṣkampam / tatsiddhistu satataṃ satkṛtya dīrghakālaṃ śamathavipaśyanāyogabhāvanākaraṇād bhaviṣyati / āryasaṃdhinirmocane yathā "maitreya! śrāvakāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ vā ye 'pi sarve 'pi laukikalokottarakuśaladharmāḥ śamathavipaśyanāphalā veditavyā iti /" taddvayoḥ sarvasamādhisaṃgṛhītatvāt sarvayogibhiḥ sadā avaśyaṃ śamathavipaśyane sevanīye / tatraiva āryasaṃdhinirmocane bhagavatā uktam, tadyathā- "mayā śrāvakāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ vividhasamādhayo darśitāḥ, te sarve śamathavipaśyanāsaṃgṛhītā veditavyāḥ" iti /
body.translated_text: Having thus generated the conventional <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening), one should strive for the arising of ultimate <s>bodhicitta</s>. That ultimate object is pure, immovable, and unwavering like the flow of a lamp shielded from wind. Its accomplishment will come from constantly and respectfully cultivating the practice of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) over a long period. As stated in the <s>Āryasaṃdhinirmocana</s>: "<s>Maitreya</s>! All wholesome qualities, whether worldly or supramundane, of <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, or <s>tathāgatas</s>, should be understood as fruits of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>."
