Since those two encompass all <s>samādhis</s>, all yogins must always cultivate <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>. In that same <s>Āryasaṃdhinirmocana</s>, the Blessed One declared: "The various <s>samādhis</s> I have taught to <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>tathāgatas</s> should all be understood as encompassed by <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>."

body.text: kevalaṃ śamathamātrabhāvanayā na yoginām āvaraṇaprahāṇam, kleśavikrāntimātrameva tāvat / prajñālokābhāve 'nuśayahānyasaṃbhavād anuśayasaṃhāro na bhaviṣyati / tasmāt tatraiva āryasaṃdhinirmocane uktam "dhyānena hi kleśānāṃ vikrāntiḥ / prajñayā tu anuśayaṃ saṃpratihanti iti" /
body.translated_text: By the cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> alone, yogins cannot abandon the obscurations; there is merely the suppression of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Since in the absence of the light of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) there is no possibility of destroying the latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>), the eradication of latent tendencies will not occur. Therefore, in that same <s>Āryasaṃdhinirmocana</s> it is stated: "Through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), the afflictions are suppressed; but through <s>prajñā</s>, one strikes at the latent tendencies."

body.text: āryasamādhirājasūtre 'pi-
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryasamādhirājasūtra</s> as well:

body.text:
kiṃ cāpi bhāveyya samādhiloke na co vibhāveyya sa ātmasaṃjñām /
punaḥ prakupyanti kileśu tasya yathodrakasyeha samādhibhāvanā /
nairātmyadharmān yadi pratyavekṣate tān pratyavekṣya yadi bhāvayet /
sa hetu nirvāṇaphalasya prāptaye yo anyaheturna sa bhoti śāntaye // iti uktam /
body.translated_text: "Even if one were to cultivate <s>samādhi</s> in this world, yet not discern the notion of self, the afflictions would arise again in that person, just as was the case with <s>Udraka</s>'s cultivation of <s>samādhi</s>. If one examines the phenomena of selflessness, and having examined them cultivates that, this is the cause for attaining the fruit of <s>nirvāṇa</s>; no other cause leads to peace." Thus it is stated.

body.text: bodhisattvapiṭake 'pi- "ye bodhisattvapiṭakasya etaddharmaparyāyāśravaṇe, āryavinayadharmaśravaṇaṃ ca vinā samādhimātreṇa saṃtoṣagrahaṇe tu ahaṃkāravaśād abhimāne patitāḥ janmajarārogamaraṇaśokaparidevanāduḥkhadaurmanasyakopāparimuktāḥ / ṣaḍgatisaṃsārāparimuktāḥ duḥkhaskandhato 'pi aparimuktāḥ / tān saṃdhāya tathāgatena evam uktam- parasmād anukūlaśrotā tu jarāmaraṇamukto bhaviṣyati" iti /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s> as well: "Those who, without hearing this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (doctrinal discourse) of the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s> and without hearing the noble <s>Vinaya</s> teaching, become content with mere <s>samādhi</s>, fall into conceit through the power of ego-grasping, and are not liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and agitation; not liberated from the cycle of the six realms of existence; not liberated from the aggregate of suffering. With reference to them, the <s>Tathāgata</s> declared: 'One who listens receptively from another will become free from old age and death.'"

body.text: tasmāt sakalāvaraṇaṃ vihāya viśuddhajñānodbhavakāmena śamathe sthitvā prajñā bhāvanīyā / evam āryaratnakūṭe 'pi bhāṣitam-
body.translated_text: Therefore, one who wishes to abandon all obscurations and generate pure knowledge should, while established in <s>śamatha</s>, cultivate <s>prajñā</s>. Thus it is also stated in the <s>Āryaratnakūṭa</s>:

body.text:
śīlaṃ pratiṣṭhāya samādhilābhaḥ samādhilābhācca hi prajñābhāvanā /
prajñāyā jñānaṃ bhavati viśuddhaṃ viśuddhajñānasya hi śīlasampat // iti /
body.translated_text: "Established in moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>), one attains <s>samādhi</s>; from the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>, one cultivates <s>prajñā</s>; from <s>prajñā</s> arises pure knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>); and from pure knowledge comes the perfection of moral discipline."

body.text: āryamahāyānaśraddhābhāvanāsūtre 'pi uktam- "kulaputra! prajñāyām anupasthitau bodhisattvānāṃ mahāyānaśraddhā mahāyāne kathamapi utpatsyate (iti) ahaṃ na vakṣyāmi / kulaputra! anena paryāyeṇāpi evaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryamahāyānaśraddhābhāvanāsūtra</s> it is also stated: "O son of noble family! I shall not say that without being established in <s>prajñā</s>, faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> will somehow arise in <s>bodhisattvas</s>. O son of noble family! By this method, the <s>bodhisattvas</s>'

body.text: yā kācid mahāyānaśraddhā mahāyāne utpatsyate sā sarvā tu avikṣiptacittena dharmārthasaṃcintanāt samutpannā veditavyā / "
body.translated_text: whatever faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> arises in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, all of that should be understood as having arisen from contemplating the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s> with an undistracted mind."

body.text: śamathaṃ vinā vipaśyanāmātreṇa yogicittaṃ viṣayeṣu vikṣipyate, vāyumadhyasthitapradīpavacca sthiraṃ na bhavati / ato jñānāloko 'tisphuṭo na bhavati / tasmād ubhayaṃ samaṃ sevitavyam / ataḥ āryamahāparinirvāṇasūtre 'pi uktam- "śrāvakaistu tathāgatagotraṃ na dṛśyate / samādheradhikatvāt prajñāyāśca alpatvāt bodhisattvāstu paśyanti, kintu asphuṭam, prajñātirekāt samādheścālpatvāt / tathāgatastu sarvam avalokayati śamathavipaśyanāsamānayuktatvād" iti / śamathabalena ca vāyunā akṣobhyapradīpavad vikalpavāyubhiścittaṃ na kampate / vipaśyanayā tu sakalakudṛṣṭimalaprahāṇatvād anyairabhedyā / candrapradīpasutre yathā-
body.translated_text: Without <s>śamatha</s>, through <s>vipaśyanā</s> alone, the yogin's mind becomes distracted toward objects and does not remain steady, like a lamp placed in the midst of wind. Therefore the light of knowledge does not become fully clear. Hence both should be cultivated equally. Thus in the <s>Āryamahāparinirvāṇasūtra</s> it is also stated: "<s>Śrāvakas</s> do not see the <s>Tathāgata</s> nature, because their <s>samādhi</s> is excessive and their <s>prajñā</s> is deficient. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> see it, but unclearly, because their <s>prajñā</s> is excessive and their <s>samādhi</s> is deficient. The <s>Tathāgata</s> sees everything, because of the equal union of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>." Through the power of <s>śamatha</s>, the mind is not shaken by the winds of conceptual thought, like a lamp undisturbed by wind. Through <s>vipaśyanā</s>, since all the stains of wrong views are abandoned, one becomes impenetrable by others. As stated in the <s>Candrapradīpasūtra</s>:

body.text: akampiyaḥ śamathabalena bhoti śailopamo bhoti vipaśyanāya /
body.translated_text: "Through the power of <s>śamatha</s> one becomes unshakable; through <s>vipaśyanā</s> one becomes like a mountain."

body.text: ityuktam / ataḥ ubhayena yogakaraṇaṃ sthitam /
body.translated_text: Thus it is stated. Therefore, the practice of both is established.

body.text: tatra ādau saṃprati tena yoginā sukhaṃ śīghraṃ ca śamatha-vipaśyanāsiddhaye śamathavipaśyanāsambhāraḥ sevanīyaḥ / tatra śamathasaṃbhāraḥ katamaḥ? anukūladeśavāsaḥ, alpecchatā, santuṣṭiḥ, kriyābāhulyaparihāraḥ, śīlaviśuddhiḥ icchādivikalpaparityāgaśca /
body.translated_text: Now, to begin with, that yogin should cultivate the prerequisites (<s>saṃbhāra</s>) of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> in order to accomplish <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> easily and swiftly. What are the prerequisites of <s>śamatha</s>? Dwelling in a favorable place, having few desires (<s>alpecchatā</s>), contentment (<s>santuṣṭi</s>), avoidance of excessive activity, purity of moral discipline (<s>śīlaviśuddhi</s>), and abandoning conceptual elaborations regarding desires and the like.

body.text: tatra pañcaguṇayukto hi deśo 'nukūlo jñātavyaḥ / vastrabhojanādeḥ akṛcchreṇa prāptitvāt sulabdhaḥ, durjanaśatrvādyanavasthitatvāt susthānam, nīrogabhūmitvāt subhūmiḥ, mitraśīlavatsamadṛṣṭitvāt sanmitram, divā bahujanāpūritatvād rātrau alpaśabdatvācca syuyuktam / alpecchatā katamā? cībarāderautkṛṣṭamasya ādhikyasya vā anadhyavasanam / saṃtuṣṭiḥ katamā?
body.translated_text: Therein, a favorable place should be known as one endowed with five qualities: easily obtainable (<s>sulabdha</s>), because clothing, food, and such are obtained without difficulty; a good location (<s>susthāna</s>), because it is not inhabited by wicked people, enemies, and the like; good ground (<s>subhūmi</s>), because the land is free from disease; good companionship (<s>sanmitra</s>), because one's friends are virtuous and hold right views; and well-suited (<s>suyukta</s>), because during the day it is not crowded with many people and at night there is little noise. What is having few desires (<s>alpecchatā</s>)? Not insisting on the finest or an excess of robes and the like. What is contentment (<s>santuṣṭi</s>)?

body.text: abaramātracivarāḍilābhena yaḥ sadā santoṣaḥ / kriyābāhulyaparihāraḥ katamaḥ? krayavikrayādiduṣkarmaparihāraḥ, gṛhastha-pravrajitānyatamātisaṃstutipariharaḥ, oṣadhinirmāṇanakṣatragaṇānādiparihāraśca /
body.translated_text: Perpetual satisfaction with obtaining merely the lowest quality of robes and such. What is avoidance of excessive activity? Avoidance of unwholesome activities such as buying and selling, avoidance of excessive association with either householders or renunciants, and avoidance of practices such as medicine-making, astrology, and the like.

body.text: śīlaviśuddhiḥ katamā? saṃvaradvaye 'pi prakṛti-pratikṣepasāvadyaśikṣāpadābhaṅgatā, pramādabhaṅge 'pi śīghrātiśīghraṃ paścāttāpena yathādharmācaraṇam / śrāvakasaṃvare pārājikapratividhāne 'yogyaṃ kathanaṃ yadasti tasminnapi paścāttāpaḥ, paścācca akaraṇa-manasikāraḥ / yaccittena yatkarmaṃ kṛtam, taccitte niḥsvabhāvatāpratisaṃkhyānad sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatābhāvanātvāt tatchīlaviśuddhireva vaktavyā / tattu āryājātaśatrukaukṛtyavinodanād avaboddhavyam / tasmāt kaukṛtyābhāvaṃ kṛtvā bhāvanāyām abhiyogaḥ karttavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is purity of moral discipline (<s>śīlaviśuddhi</s>)? Non-transgression of the training rules regarding both natural and proscribed offenses in both sets of vows (<s>saṃvara</s>); and even when there is a transgression through heedlessness, the swiftest possible remedial practice through remorse in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. Regarding the statement that in the <s>śrāvaka</s> discipline one is unfit for remedy of a <s>pārājika</s> offense, even there one should feel remorse, and afterward maintain the mental attention of non-repetition. Whatever action was done by whatever mind, through the analysis of the essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>) of that mind and the cultivation of the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, that itself is to be called purity of moral discipline. This should be understood from the <s>Āryājātaśatrukaukṛtyavinodana</s>. Therefore, having removed remorse, one should engage in meditation.

body.text: kāmeṣvapi iha janmāntare ca bhāvino vividhadoṣān manasikṛtya teṣu vikalpaḥ pariharttavyaḥ / etāvatā saṃsārabhāvaḥ priyo 'priyo vāpi tatsarvaṃ tu vināśadharmi asthiraṃ ca / niścayena tatsarvasmin mayi ca aciraṃ viyoge bhāve sati mama tasmin katham adhyavasitādirbhaved iti bhāvanayā sarve vikalpāḥ pariharttavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: By reflecting on the various faults of desires both in this life and in future lives, one should abandon conceptual elaboration regarding them. In this way, whether the states of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) are pleasant or unpleasant, all of them are subject to destruction and impermanent. Since separation from all of them and from myself will certainly come before long, how could there be attachment and the like toward them? Through such contemplation, all conceptual elaborations should be abandoned.

body.text: vipaśyanā-sambhāraḥ katamaḥ? satpuruṣāśrayaḥ, bahuśrutaparyeṣaṇā, yoniśomanasikāraśca / tatra kīdṛśaṃ satpuruṣam āśrayed iti cet- yo bahuśrutaḥ prasannavāk, kāruṇiko nirvitsahaśca / tatra bahuśrutaparyeṣṭiḥ katamā? yat sādaraṃ bhagavaddvādaśāṅgadharmapravacananeyārthanītārthātiśravaṇam / ittham āryasaṃdhinirmocane- "yatheccham āryākhyānāśravaṇaṃ hi vipaśyanāvighnaḥ" iti uktam / tatraiva "vipaśyanā ca śravaṇamananābhyāmutpannaviśuddhadṛṣṭihetorūtpadyate /" ityuktam / āryānārāyaṇaparipṛcchāyām api- "śrutimati prajñāpradurbhavati / prajñāvataḥ kleśāḥ praśāmyanti /" ityuktam /
body.translated_text: What are the prerequisites of <s>vipaśyanā</s>? Reliance on a good person (<s>satpuruṣa</s>), seeking extensive learning (<s>bahuśruta</s>), and proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśomanasikāra</s>). What kind of good person should one rely upon? One who is learned, speaks clearly, is compassionate, and is patient with hardship. What is the seeking of extensive learning? Respectfully and extensively listening to the definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>) and provisional meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>) of the Blessed One's twelve divisions of scripture. Thus in the <s>Āryasaṃdhinirmocana</s>: "Listening to noble discourses as one pleases is an obstacle to <s>vipaśyanā</s>," it is stated. And there also: "<s>Vipaśyanā</s> arises from the cause of pure view generated through hearing and reflection." In the <s>Āryānārāyaṇaparipṛcchā</s> as well: "In one who possesses learning, <s>prajñā</s> arises. In one who possesses <s>prajñā</s>, the afflictions are pacified."

body.text: yoniśomanasikāraḥ katamaḥ? yasya nītārthasūtraneyārthasūtrādisunirṇayastādṛśe bodhisattve niḥśaṅke sati bhāvanāyām aikāntikaniścayo bhaviṣyati / anyathā saṃśayāndolitayānasthitastu śṛṅgāṭakamadhyagatamanuṣyavat kutrāpi aikāntikaniścayo na bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: What is proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśomanasikāra</s>)? When a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has properly ascertained the definitive-meaning sūtras, provisional-meaning sūtras, and so forth is free from doubt, there will arise a definitive certainty in meditation. Otherwise, one who is tossed about by doubt, like a person standing at a crossroads, will not arrive at definitive certainty in any direction.

body.text: yoginā tu sadā matsyamāṃsādi parihṛtya apratikūlaṃ bhojanaṃ niyatamātrakaṃ bhoktavyam / tathā tena sāñcitasakalaśamathavipaśyanāsambhāreṇabodhisattvena bhāvanāyāṃ praveṣṭavyam /
body.translated_text: The yogin should always abstain from fish, meat, and the like, and should eat a measured amount of food that is agreeable. Then, that <s>bodhisattva</s>, having accumulated all the prerequisites of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>, should enter into meditation.

body.text: tatra prathamaṃ tāvad yogī bhāvanākāle sarvam itikaraṇīyaṃ parisamāpyaṃ kṛtamūtrapurīṣaḥ kaṇṭakasvarādirahite mano 'nūkūle pradeśe sthitvā mayā sarvasattvā bodhimaṇḍe niṣpādayitavyā iti viniścayan, sakalajagadabhyuddharaṇāśayo mahākaruṇām āmukhīkṛtya daśadigavasthitān sarvabuddhabhodhisattvān pañcāṅgena praṇipatyāgrato buddhabodhisattvan paṭādau sthāpayitvā anyatra vā yathāvat tebhyaśca yathāruci pūjāstavanaṃ kṛtvā svapāpaṃ pradeśya, sakalasya jagataḥ puṇyam anumodya, mṛdutarasukhāsane vairocanabhaṭṭārakabaddhaparyaṅkena ardhaparyaṅkena vā niṣpādya nātyunmūīlite nātinimīlite nāsikāgravinyaste cakṣuṣī kṛtvā, nātinamraṃ nātistabdham ṛjukāyaṃ praṇidhāyāntarmukhāvarjitasmṛtirupaviśet / tataḥ skandhau samau sthāpayet / śiro nonnatam nāvanataṃ eka-pārśve niścalaṃ sthāpayitavyam / kiṃ tarhi nābhipraguṇā nāsikā sthāpayitavyā / dantoṣṭhaṃ mṛdu sthāpanīyam / jivhā coparidantamūle sthāpanīyā / āśvāspraśvāsāstu na saśabdā nāpi sthūlā nāpi tvaritāḥ karaṇīyāḥ / kiṃ tvasaṃlakṣyamāṇā mandaṃ mandamanābhogena yathā praviśeyurnirgaccheyurvā tathā karaṇiyam /
body.translated_text: Therein, first, at the time of meditation, the yogin, having completed all that needs to be done, having relieved himself, situated in a place free from thorns, [disturbing] sounds, and the like, and agreeable to the mind, resolving 'I must bring all beings to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>),' with the intention of rescuing the entire world, facing great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), having prostrated with the five limbs to all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> dwelling in the ten directions, having set up [images of] <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in front on a cloth or elsewhere as appropriate, having performed worship and praise to them as one pleases, having confessed one's sins, having rejoiced in the merit of the entire world — one should sit on a soft and comfortable seat, in the cross-legged posture of the Lord <s>Vairocana</s> or in the half-cross-legged posture, with the eyes neither too open nor too closed, directed at the tip of the nose, the body held straight — neither too bent nor too stiff — with mindfulness turned inward. Then one should place the shoulders level. The head should be placed neither raised nor lowered, motionless to one side. Rather, the nose should be aligned straight with the navel. The teeth and lips should be placed gently. The tongue should be placed at the base of the upper teeth. The inhalations and exhalations should be made neither audible, nor coarse, nor hurried — but imperceptibly, slowly, gently, and effortlessly, so that they enter and exit [naturally].

body.text: tatra prathamaṃ tāvat śamatho nispādayitavyaḥ, bāhyaviṣayavikṣepaśānteḥ āntarālambane satataṃ svarasavāhi prītiprasrabdhivaccitta eva sthitistu śamatha iti ucyate / tasyaiva śamathasyālambanakāle yastattva-vicāraḥ sā vipaśyanā / āryaratnameghe yathā- "śamathaścittaikāgratā / vipaśyanā bhūtapratyavekṣeti" uktam /
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) should first be accomplished. The abiding of the mind in an internal object, with external sense-distraction pacified, flowing continuously of its own accord with joy and pliancy — that is called <s>śamatha</s>. The investigation of reality (<s>tattva-vicāra</s>) while [the mind] is engaged with the object of that very <s>śamatha</s> — that is <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). As stated in the <s>Āryaratnamegha</s>: '<s>Śamatha</s> is one-pointedness of mind; <s>vipaśyanā</s> is the examination of reality.'

body.text: āryasaṃdhinirmocane 'pi- "bhagavan kathaṃ śamathaparigaveṣaṇaṃ vipaśyanākauśalaṃ cāsti? ucyate / maitreya! mayā dharmopacāro vyavasthāpitaḥ / tadyathā- ye sūtrageyavyākaraṇa-gāthā-udāna-nidāna-avadāna-itivṛttaka-jātaka-vaipulya-adbhūtadharma-upadeśa-vargāḥ bodhisattvebhya ākhyātāste bodhisattvaiḥ saṃśrutya saṃdhārya, pāṭhamabhyasya, manasā samparīkṣya, dṛṣṭyā supratividdhaya sa ekākī viviktasthaḥ, antaḥ pratisaṃlīnaḥ, yathāsucintitān tāneva dharmān manasikṛtya, yena cittena manasikārastaccitābhyantaraṃ satataṃ manasikāreṇa manasikāraḥ / tathā praviśya tatra bahuśaḥ sthitaḥ tasyāṃ kāyaprasrabdhicittaprasrabdhisambhavaśca yo 'sti sa tu śamatha iti / tarhi bodhisattvaḥ śamathaparigaveṣaṇaṃ karoti / tena kāyaprasrabdhiḥ, cittaprasrabdhiśca / te prāpya tatraiva sthitaḥ, cittavikṣepaṃ vihāya yathā cintitadharmaḥ teṣāmeva abhyantare samādhigocarapratibimbaṃ pratyavekṣate, adhimucyate, tādṛk samādhigocarapratibimbam, tajjñeyarthe vivicyate pravivecanaṃ parikalpanaṃ paryavekṣaṇaṃ kṣāntiḥ, kāmo viśiṣṭaivbhāgo darśanam, adhigamaśca yo 'sti, sā tu vipaśyanā iti, tathā ca bodhisattvavipaśyanā kauśalam ityuktam / "
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryasaṃdhinirmocana</s> also: 'Blessed One, how does the seeking of <s>śamatha</s> and skill in <s>vipaśyanā</s> exist?' It is said: '<s>Maitreya</s>, the designation of the <s>Dharma</s> has been established by me — namely, the categories of <s>sūtras</s>, songs (<s>geya</s>), predictions (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>), verses (<s>gāthā</s>), inspired utterances (<s>udāna</s>), narratives of occasions (<s>nidāna</s>), legends (<s>avadāna</s>), historical accounts (<s>itivṛttaka</s>), birth stories (<s>jātaka</s>), extensive discourses (<s>vaipulya</s>), marvels (<s>adbhutadharma</s>), and instructions (<s>upadeśa</s>) — which have been proclaimed to <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having heard, retained, recited, studied them, having investigated them with the mind, having thoroughly penetrated them with [right] view — [the bodhisattva], alone, in a secluded place, withdrawn within, attends mentally to those very <s>dharmas</s> as well contemplated. The mind with which one attends — one attends continuously with inner mental engagement upon that mind. Having thus entered and abided therein for a long time, whatever arising of bodily pliancy and mental pliancy there is — that is <s>śamatha</s>. Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> undertakes the seeking of <s>śamatha</s>. Having attained bodily pliancy and mental pliancy, abiding right there, abandoning mental distraction, one examines the reflection within the domain of <s>samādhi</s> regarding those very contemplated <s>dharmas</s>, resolves upon it — [examining] that reflection within the domain of <s>samādhi</s>: the discrimination, investigation, examination, patience, desire, superior determination, view, and attainment regarding that knowable object — that is <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Thus is stated the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> skill in <s>vipaśyanā</s>.'

body.text: tatra śamathābhinirhārakāmo yogī prathamaṃ tāvat sūtrageyādisakalapravacanaṃ tu tathatāparāyaṇam, tathatāpragbhāram, tathatāpravaṇama iti sarvaṃ saṃgrāhya tatra cittam upasthāpayet / etāvatā kiyadākāreṇa sarvadharmasaṃgrahabhute skandhādau tatra cittam upasthāpayet / etāvatā yathādṛṣṭa-yathāśrutabuddhapratimāyāṃ cittaṃ sthāpitavyam / āryasamādhirāje yathā-
body.translated_text: Therein, the yogin who wishes to accomplish <s>śamatha</s> should first comprehend that the entire teaching — <s>sūtras</s>, songs, and all the rest — has suchness (<s>tathatā</s>) as its goal, has suchness as its ground, and inclines toward suchness, and should fix the mind thereon. To this extent, one should fix the mind on the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so forth, which encompass all <s>dharmas</s>, in whatever manner. To this extent, one should fix the mind on a <s>Buddha</s>-image as seen or heard. As in the <s>Āryasamādhirāja</s>:

body.text:
suvarṇavarṇena samucchrayeṇa samantaprāsādiku lokanāthaḥ /
yasyātra ālambani cittu vartate samāhitaḥ socyati bodhisattva // iti uktam /
body.translated_text: 'The Lord of the World, golden in color, of supreme stature, magnificent on all sides — whoever's mind is engaged in contemplation of him is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>samādhi</s>.'

body.text: tathā yatra icchālambanaṃ tasmin cittaṃ sthāpayitvā tatraiva uparyupari satataṃ cittaṃ sthāpayet / tatra upasthāpya cittam īdṛśamevaṃ parīkṣeta / 'kim ālambanaṃ sugṛṇhāti līyate vā athavā bāhyaviṣayavyasekād vikṣipyate iti parīkṣitavyam / tatra yadi styānamiddhābhibhavād cittaṃ līnaṃ vā layābhiśaṅkā darśane tatkāle pramodya vastuni buddhapratimādau vā alokasaṃjñāmanasikaraḥ kartavyaḥ / atha layam upaśāmya yathāpi tatraiva ālambane cittālambanam atisphuṭadarśanaṃ bhavati tathā karaṇiyam /
body.translated_text: Likewise, having fixed the mind on whatever desired object, one should place the mind thereon again and again, continuously. Having fixed the mind thereon, one should examine it thus: 'Does the mind grasp the object well? Is it sinking? Or is it distracted due to the scattering toward external sense-objects?' — this should be examined. Therein, if the mind is sinking due to being overcome by dullness and drowsiness, or if there is an apprehension of the appearance of sinking, at that time one should attend to a joyful object, or to a <s>Buddha</s>-image, or to the perception of light. Then, having pacified the sinking, one should [make the mind] see the object clearly in that very [meditation] — this should be done.

body.text: yadā tu jātyandhavad andhakārapraviṣṭapuruṣavad vā vinimīlitākṣavad vā cittam ālambanaṃ atisphuṭaraṃ na paśyati tadā līnaṃ veditavyam / yadā bāhyarūpādau teṣāṃ guṇakalpanayā dhāvanena, anyamanasikāreṇa vā pūrvānubhūtaviṣayecchayā cittauddhatyaṃ vā auddhatyaśaṅkādarśanaṃ vā tadā sarve saṃskārā anityā duḥkhādimanosaṃvegavastu manasi karttavyam / tataḥ vikṣepaśāntiṃ kṛtvā smṛtisamprajanyarajjunā manonāgaḥ tadālambanastambhe eva bandhitavyaḥ / yadā layauddhatye na bhavataḥ tadālambena cittapraśamavahitāṃ paśyet, tadā ābhogaśithilikaraṇād upekṣayā tatkāle yāvadicchaṃ tiṣṭhet / itthaṃ bhāvitaśamathasya taccharīrasya cittasya ca praśrabdhirbhaviṣyati / yathecchālambane cittaṃ svavaśe bhaviṣyati / tadā śamatho niṣpanno veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: When the mind does not see the object clearly — like one born blind, like a person who has entered darkness, or like one with closed eyes — then it should be known as sunken (<s>līna</s>). When, through running after external forms and the like by imagining their qualities, or through other mental engagement, or through desire for previously experienced sense-objects, there is agitation of the mind or an apprehension of the appearance of agitation, then one should attend mentally to subjects that produce disenchantment, such as 'All conditioned things are impermanent, suffering,' and the rest. Then, having pacified the distraction, one should bind the elephant of the mind to the post of that very object with the rope of mindfulness and clear comprehension (<s>smṛti-samprajanya</s>). When sinking and agitation do not occur, when one sees the mind flowing calmly upon the object, then — by relaxing the effort, through equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) — one should at that time abide as long as one wishes. When <s>śamatha</s> has been thus cultivated, pliancy (<s>praśrabdhi</s>) of body and mind will arise. When the mind becomes under one's control regarding whatever desired object, then <s>śamatha</s> should be known as accomplished.

body.text: tataḥ śamathaṃ niṣpādya vipaśyanāṃ bhāvayet / īdṛśaṃ ca mantavyam bhagavataḥ sarvavacanaṃ tu subhaṣitam, sākṣāt paramparayā vā tattvapratyakṣavyañajanaṃ tattvaparāyaṇameva ca / tattvajñāne ālokobhdavāt tamonirāsavat sarvadṛṣṭijālaviyogo bhaviṣyati / śamathamātreṇa jñānaśuddhirna bhaviṣyati, āvaraṇa-tamonirāsaścāpi na bhaviṣyati / prajñayā ca tattvasamyagbhāvanāyāṃ jñānaviśuddhirbhaviṣyati / prajñayā eva tattvamavagamyate prajñayaiva āvaraṇaṃ samyak prahīyate /
body.translated_text: Then, having accomplished <s>śamatha</s>, one should cultivate <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). And one should consider thus: 'All the words of the Blessed One are well-spoken, and they directly or indirectly reveal the perception of reality and have reality as their goal. When the knowledge of reality arises, like the arising of light dispelling darkness, there will be freedom from the entire net of [wrong] views. Through <s>śamatha</s> alone, the purification of knowledge will not occur, nor will the removal of the darkness of obscuration. But through the proper cultivation of reality by means of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), the purification of knowledge will occur. Through <s>prajñā</s> alone is reality comprehended; through <s>prajñā</s> alone is the obscuration properly abandoned.

body.text: tasmānmayā śamathe sthitvā prajñayā tattvaṃ paryeṣitavyam / śamathamātreṇa saṃtoṣo na karaṇīya iti vicāraṇīyam /
body.translated_text: Therefore, established in <s>śamatha</s>, I must seek reality through <s>prajñā</s>. One should not be content with <s>śamatha</s> alone' — thus one should investigate.

body.text: kīdṛśaṃ ca tattvam iti cet? yat paramārthataḥ sarvavastupudgala dharmātmaśūnyam, tatprajñāparimitayā adhigamyate na cānyathā / āryasaṃdhinirmocane yathoktam "bhagavan! kayā pāramitayā bodhisattvaḥ dharmaniḥsvabhāvatāṃ gṛṇhīyāt? avalokiteśvara! prajñāpāramitayā gṛhyate /" iti / tasmāt śamathe sthitvā prajñāṃ bhāvayet /
body.translated_text: And what is that reality? That which, in the ultimate sense, is empty of the self of persons (<s>pudgala</s>) and the self of <s>dharmas</s> with respect to all things — that is comprehended through the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), and not otherwise. As stated in the <s>Āryasaṃdhinirmocana</s>: 'Blessed One, by which perfection (<s>pāramitā</s>) does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> apprehend the essencelessness of <s>dharmas</s>? <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, it is apprehended through the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' Therefore, established in <s>śamatha</s>, one should cultivate <s>prajñā</s>.

body.text: tatraivaṃ yogī vicārayet, 'pudgalaḥ na skandhadhātvāyatanavyatirikta upalabhyate / na cāpi pudgalaḥ skandhādisvabhavaḥ / te skandhādayastu anityāḥ, anekasvabhāvatvāt pudgalasya ca nityaikarūpeṇa parairupakalpitatvāt / nāpi tattvānyatvābhyām anabhilāpyapudgalasya vastutvaṃ yuktam / vastusataḥ prakārāntarābhāvāt / tasmāt tadyathā bhrama eva ayaṃ lokasya yadutāhaṃ memeti vicāritavyam /
body.translated_text: Therein, the yogin should investigate thus: 'The person (<s>pudgala</s>) is not apprehended as distinct from the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). Nor is the person of the nature of the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest. For those <s>skandhas</s> and the rest are impermanent, since they are of multiple natures; and [yet] the person has been imagined by others as permanent and of a single form. Nor is it reasonable for the ineffable person to be a real entity, through either identity or difference — because there is no other mode [of being] for a real thing. Therefore, just as [there is an error in thinking] "I" and "mine" — this is indeed the delusion of the world — thus one should investigate.'

body.text: dharmanairātmyamapi evaṃ bhavanīyam / dharma iti saṃkṣepataḥ pañcaskandho dvādaśāyatanam, aṣṭādaśadhātavaśca / tatra ye ca skandhāyatanadhāturūpiṇaḥ, na te paramārthataḥ cittākāravyatiriktāḥ / tatparamāṇuśo vibhāge paramāṇavo 'pi bhāgaśaḥ svabhāvatāpratyavekṣamāṇāḥ svabhāvaniścayagrahaṇābhāvāt / tasmād anādikālikavitatharūpādyabhiniveśavaśāt svapnopalabhyamānarūpādipratibhāsavad bālānāṃ cittameva bahiḥ vicchinnamiva rūpādipratibhāsaṃ khyāti / paramārthatastatra rūpādistu na cittākāravyatirikta iti vicārayet / tad evaṃ traidhātukamidaṃ tu cittamātramiti cintayet / sa evaṃ cittameva sakaladharmaprajñaptiṃ niścitya tatra pratyavekṣya ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvaḥ pratyavekṣito bhavatīti cittasvabhāvamapi pratyavekṣate / sa evaṃ vicārayati /
body.translated_text: <s>Dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of dharmas) should also be meditated upon in this way. '<s>Dharmas</s>' in brief means the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), the twelve <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), and the eighteen <s>dhātus</s> (elements). Therein, those <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s> that have form are not, ultimately, different from the aspects of mind. For when they are divided atom by atom, and the atoms too are examined part by part for their own-nature, there is no ascertainment of any own-nature to grasp. Therefore, due to the power of beginningless clinging to false forms and so forth—like the appearance of forms and so forth apprehended in a dream—the minds of the childish appear as if forms and so forth are externally separate. Ultimately, however, one should examine that form and so forth are not different from the aspects of mind. Thus one should think: 'This triple world is mind-only.' Having thus determined that mind alone is the designation of all <s>dharmas</s> and having examined therein, since the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s> has been examined, one also examines the own-nature of mind itself. One examines thus:

body.text: cittamapi paramārthaḥ satyaṃ bhavitum na yujyate / yadā hi alīkasvabhāvarūpādyākaropagrahaṇe cittameva citrākāraṃ pratibhāsate, tadā satyatvaṃ kutra bhavet / yathā rūpādī
body.translated_text: Even mind is not fit to be ultimately real. For when mind itself appears in variegated aspects while apprehending the aspects of form and so forth that are of false nature, where would its reality be? Just as form and so forth are

body.text: alīkaṃ tathā cittamapi tadavyatiriktatvād alīkameva / yathā citrākāratayā rūpādayo naikānekasvabhāvāḥ tathā cittamapi tadavyatirekeṇa anikānekasvabhāvam / tasmāt māyādisvabhāvopamameva cittam /
body.translated_text: false, so too mind, being not different from them, is false alone. Just as, by having variegated aspects, form and so forth have neither a single nor a manifold own-nature, so too mind, being not different from them, has neither a single nor a manifold own-nature. Therefore, mind is comparable in nature to an illusion and the like.

body.text: yathā cittamevaṃ sarvadharmā api māyāsvabhāvasadṛśā eva iti vicārayet / tena tathā prajñayā cittasvabhāve pratyevekṣamāṇe paramārthataḥ cittam abhyantare 'pi nopalabhate, bāhye 'pi nopalabhate, anubhayo 'pi nopalabhate, atītacittamapi nopalabhate, anāgatamapi nopalabhate, pratyutpannamapi nopalabhate / nāpi cittamutpādyamānaṃ kuto 'pyāgacchati, nāpi nirudhyamānaṃ kvacidapi gacchati / cittaṃ tu agrāhyam anirdeśyam, arūpam ca / anirdeśyam agrahyam arūpam ca yadasti tasya svabhāvaḥ kīdṛśaḥ? tathā āryaratnakūṭe yathoktam- "kāśyapa! cittaṃ tu parigaveṣyamāṇaṃ na labhyate / yanna labdhaṃ tanna ālambyate yacca nālambyate / tannātītam, nānāgatam, na ca pratyutpannam /" iti vistaraḥ / tad evaṃ parīkṣyamāṇe cittasya ādiṃ na samanupasyati, antaṃ na samanupaśyati madhyaṃ na samanupaśyati /
body.translated_text: Just as mind [is thus], so too all <s>dharmas</s> are similar to illusion in nature—one should examine in this way. Then, when one thus examines the own-nature of mind with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), one does not ultimately apprehend mind internally, nor externally, nor in both. One does not apprehend the past mind, nor the future mind, nor the present mind. Nor does mind, when arising, come from anywhere; nor, when ceasing, does it go anywhere. Mind is ungraspable, inexpressible, and formless. What is inexpressible, ungraspable, and formless—what kind of own-nature does that have? Thus, as stated in the <s>Ārya-Ratnakūṭa</s>: "<s>Kāśyapa</s>! Mind, when sought, is not found. What is not found is not apprehended. And what is not apprehended is neither past, nor future, nor present." Thus in detail. When thus examined, one does not perceive the beginning of mind, does not perceive the end, does not perceive the middle.

body.text: yathā ca cittam anantamadhyaṃ tathā sarvadharmānapi anantamadhyam avagacchet / tena tadevaṃ cittam anantamadhyam avagamya kimapi cittasvabhāvaṃ nopalabhate / yadapi cittaṃ parīkṣyate tadapi śūnyaṃ pratividhyati / tatpratividhyamāne cittaviṭhapanāsvabhāvaṃ rūpādisvabhāvamapi na samanupaśyati / tena tathā prajñayā sarvadharmasvabhāvasya asamanudarśanatvād rūpaṃ nityam anityaṃ vā, śūnyam aśūnyaṃ vā, sāsravam anāsravaṃ vā, utpannam anutpannaṃ vā, bhāvo 'bhāvo vetī na vikalpayati / yathā rūpaṃ na vikalpayati tathā vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñāneṣvapi na vikalpayati / asiddhe dharmiṇi tasya viśeṣaṇānāmapi asiddhatvāt, tatra kathaṃ vikalpayet / tad evaṃ prajñayā parīkṣyamāṇo
body.translated_text: And just as mind is without end or middle, so too one should understand all <s>dharmas</s> as without end or middle. Then, having thus understood mind as without end or middle, one does not apprehend any own-nature of mind whatsoever. Even the mind that examines—one penetrates that too as empty. When penetrating that, one also does not perceive the own-nature of form and so forth, which is of the nature of the establishment of mind. Then, through that <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), not perceiving the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, one does not conceptualize whether form is permanent or impermanent, empty or non-empty, with outflows or without outflows, arisen or unarisen, existent or non-existent. Just as one does not conceptualize form, so too one does not conceptualize regarding <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). Since the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) is unestablished, its qualifications are also unestablished—how could one conceptualize about them? Thus, when examined by <s>prajñā</s>,

body.text: yadā yoginā kasyacid vastunaḥ svabhāvaparamārthaniścayo na gṛhyate, tadā nirvikalpasamādhau praviśati / sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatā api avagamyate /
body.translated_text: when the <s>yogin</s> does not grasp any ultimate determination of the own-nature of any entity whatsoever, then one enters <s>nirvikalpasamādhi</s> (non-conceptual concentration). The essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> is also understood.

body.text: yaḥ prajñayā vastusvabhāvaṃ pratyavekṣya na bhāvayan, manasikāraparihāramātraṃ bhāvayati, tasya vikalpaḥ kadāpi na nivartate, na ca niḥsvabhāvatāvabodho 'pi bhaviṣyati, prajñālokābhāvāt / evaṃ samyakpratyavekṣaṇāt samyagyathāvajjñānāgnibhāve 'raṇimanthanāgnivat kalpanāvṛkṣo dahyate iti bhagavatā uktam /
body.translated_text: One who, having examined the own-nature of entities with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), does not meditate [on that understanding] but merely cultivates the avoidance of mental engagement—his conceptualization will never cease, nor will the understanding of essencelessness ever arise, due to the absence of the light of <s>prajñā</s>. Thus the Blessed One said that through correct examination, the tree of conceptualization is burned by the fire of correct knowledge of things as they are—like fire [produced] from the friction of fire-sticks.

body.text: tathā uktam āryaratnameghe- "sa evam apakṣālakuśalaḥ sarvaprapañcavigamāya śūnyatābhāvanāya yogamāpadyate / sa śūnyatābhāvanabahulo yeṣu yeṣu sthāneṣu cittaṃ prasarati, cittamabhiramate, tāni tāni sthānāni svabhāvataḥ parigaveṣamāṇaḥ śūnyaṃ pratividhyati / yat cittaṃ tadapi parīkṣamāṇaḥ śūnyaṃ pratividhyati, yenāpi cittena parīkṣate tad api svabhāvataḥ śūnyaṃ parigaveṣyamāṇaṃ pratividhyati / sa evam upaparīkṣamāṇo nirnimittatāyāṃ yogamāpadyate /" iti bhavati / anena tu paryavekṣaṇapūrvagāmitāyāḥ nirnimittatāpraveśaṃ darśayati / manasikāraparihāramātram, prajñayā vastusvabhāvatāṃ ca avicārya, avikalpatāpraveśam asaṃbhāvya, atisphuṭataraṃ darśayati / tathā tayā prajñayā rūpādivastusvabhāvaṃ samyag yathāvat parīkṣya dhyāyati, rūpādau sthitvā dhyānaṃ na karoti / ihalokaparalokayormadhye sthitvā dhyānaṃ na karoti, tadrūpādyanupalambhāt / tasmād apratiṣṭhitadhyāna iti ucyate /
body.translated_text: Thus it is stated in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s>: "Being skilled in purification, he applies himself to the meditation on <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) for the cessation of all proliferation. He, being much engaged in the meditation on emptiness, whatever objects the mind extends to, whatever objects the mind delights in—searching for those objects from the standpoint of own-nature, he penetrates them as empty. The mind that [does this]—examining that too, he penetrates it as empty. Even the mind with which he examines—searching for that too from the standpoint of own-nature, he penetrates it as empty. Examining in this way, he applies himself to the signless." And so it is. By this, [the sūtra] shows that entry into the signless is preceded by examination. It shows most clearly that entry into the non-conceptual is not possible by mere avoidance of mental engagement, without examining the own-nature of entities with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Thus, having correctly and properly examined with that <s>prajñā</s> the own-nature of entities such as form and so forth, one meditates; one does not meditate by abiding in form and so forth. One does not meditate by abiding between this world and the next world, due to the non-apprehension of form and so forth. Therefore it is called <s>apratiṣṭhitadhyāna</s> (non-abiding meditation).

body.text: prajñayā skalavastusvabhāvatāṃ prativīkṣya yasmād anupalambhaṃ dhyāyati- tasmāt prajñottaradhyāyī iti ucyate / āryagaganagañja-āryaratnacūḍādiṣu yathā nirdiṣṭam /
body.translated_text: Since one meditates on non-apprehension, having examined with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) the own-nature of all entities—therefore one is called <s>prajñottaradhyāyin</s> (one who meditates with wisdom as foremost). As taught in the <s>Ārya-Gaganagañja</s>, <s>Ārya-Ratnacūḍā</s>, and others.

body.text: sa evaṃ pudgaladharmanairātmyamayaṃ tattvamavatīrṇaḥ, aparasya parīkṣaṇīyasya darśanīyasya ca abhāvād uparatam, vitarka-vicāra-anabhilāpyaikarasena manasā svarasavāhinā anabhisaṃskāratastattvameva
body.translated_text: Having thus descended into the reality consisting of <s>pudgala-dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of persons and dharmas), since there is nothing further to be examined or seen, with a mind that has ceased [conceptualization], of a single taste that is beyond deliberation, investigation, and verbal expression, flowing spontaneously and effortlessly, [one should abide] meditating on reality itself

body.text: sphuṭataraṃ bhāvayan tiṣṭhet / tatra ca sthitaścittasaṃtānaṃ na vikṣipet / yadāntarā rāgādīnāṃ cittaṃ bahirdhā vikṣapet tadā vikṣepaṃ viditvā śighram aśubhabhāvanādivikṣepam upaśamya śīghraṃ tathatāyāṃ cittam uparyupari praveśayet / yadā tu tatrānabhirataṃ cittaṃ paśyet, tadā samādherguṇadarśanād abhiratiṃ tatra bhāvayet / vikṣepe ca doṣadarśanād aratiṃ praśamayet / atha styānamiddhābhibhavād yadā sphuṭapracāratayā līnaṃ cittaṃ paśyet, layābhiśaṅkitaṃ vā tadā pūrvavat pramodyavastu manasikāreṇa śīghraṃ layamupaśamayet / punaḥ tad eva tattvālambanam atidṛḍhataraṃ gṛṇhīyāt / yadi tadā pūrvahasitaramitānyanusmṛtya cittamantarā samṛddhataṃ paśyed auddhatyābhiśaṅkitaṃ vā tadā anityatādisaṃvegavastumanasikārād vikṣepaṃ śamayet / tataḥ punastatraiva tattve cittānabhisaṃskāravāhitāyāṃ yatnaṃ kurvīta /
body.translated_text: most clearly. And while abiding therein, one should not scatter the stream of mind. If at intervals <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and other [afflictions] scatter the mind outward, then, having recognized the distraction, one should quickly pacify the distraction through meditation on the unattractive and the like, and swiftly re-enter the mind into <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) again and again. But when one sees the mind to be undelighted therein, one should cultivate delight in it by seeing the qualities of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). And one should pacify displeasure by seeing the faults of distraction. Then, when, due to being overpowered by <s>styāna</s> (torpor) and <s>middha</s> (drowsiness), one sees the mind as sinking without clear functioning, or suspects dullness, one should quickly pacify the dullness through mental engagement with joyful objects, as before. Then one should again grasp that very object of reality most firmly. If at that time, having recalled previously [experienced] laughter and play, one sees the mind as having become overactive, or suspects excitement, one should pacify the distraction through mental engagement with sobering objects such as impermanence. Then again, one should strive for the effortless flow of mind in that very reality.

body.text: atha yadā layauddhatyābhyāṃ viviktatayā samapravṛttaṃ svarasavāhisphuṭataraṃ tatraiva tattve cittaṃ utpādayate, tadā bhogaśithilīkaraṇād upekṣaṇiyam / yadi samapravṛtte citte sati ābhogaḥ kriyate, tadā cittaṃ vikṣepyate / līne 'pi citte sati, yadyābhogo na kriyate, tadā atilīnatvād vipaśyanārahitaṃ, cittaṃ ca jātyandhavad bhaviṣyati / tasmāccitte līne sati bhogaṃ kuvīta / samapravṛtte sati bhogaṃ na kurvīta / yadā ca vipaśyanāṃ bhāveyat prajñātiriktatarā bhavet, tadā śamathasyālpatvāt pravātasthita-pradīpavat pracalatvāccittasya na sphuṭaraṃ tattvadarśanaṃ bhavet / atastadā śamathau bhāvayitavyaḥ / śamathasyābhyadhikye 'pi prajñā bhāvayitavyā /
body.translated_text: Then, when the mind, free from dullness and excitement, arises evenly and clearly, flowing spontaneously in that very reality, one should apply equanimity by relaxing effort. For if effort is applied when the mind is proceeding evenly, then the mind becomes distracted. And if effort is not applied when the mind is sinking, then the mind, being excessively sunk and devoid of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), will become like one born blind. Therefore, when the mind is sinking, effort should be applied; when it is proceeding evenly, effort should not be applied. And when one cultivates <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) becomes excessive, then, due to the weakness of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), since the mind wavers like a lamp placed in the wind, there will be no clear seeing of reality. Therefore, at that time, <s>śamatha</s> should be cultivated. When <s>śamatha</s> is excessive, <s>prajñā</s> should be cultivated.

body.text: yadā ubhayaṃ samapravṛttaṃ tadā anabhisaṃskāreṇaiva tāvat sthātavyaṃ yāvat kāyacittapīḍā na bhavet / satyāṃ kāyādipīḍāyāṃ tadantarā sakalameva lokaṃ māyāmarīcisvapnajalacandropamapratibhāsavad dṛṣṭvā īdṛśaṃ cintanīyam / amī sattvāstu evaṃ vidhadharmagāmbhiryānavabodhatayā saṃsāre saṃkliṣṭāḥ / tato 'haṃ kariṣyāmi tāṃstāṃ dharmatām avabodhayeyuḥ, tathā kariṣyāmi' iti cintayan mahākaruṇāṃ bodhicittābhimukhīṃ kurvita / tato viśramya punarapi tathaiva sarvadharmanirābhāsaṃ samādhimavataret / citte 'tikhede sati, tathaiva viśramet / ayaṃ tu śamathavipaśyanāyuganaddhapravṛttimārgaḥ savikalpanirvikalpapratibimbam ālambate /
body.translated_text: When both [śamatha and vipaśyanā] are flowing evenly, then one should abide just with effortlessness, so long as no affliction of body or mind arises. When there is affliction of the body and the rest, in the interval [of rest], having seen the entire world as appearing like an illusion, a mirage, a dream, a moon [reflected] in water, one should think thus: 'These beings, through not comprehending the profundity of <s>dharmas</s> of this kind, are afflicted in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore I shall act so that they may comprehend the nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>); thus shall I act' — thinking thus, one should direct great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward <s>bodhicitta</s>. Then, having rested, one should again enter the <s>samādhi</s> that is free from all appearances of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharma-nirābhāsa</s>). When there is excessive weariness of mind, one should likewise rest. This is the path of the unified practice of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (<s>yuganaddha</s>); it takes as its object the reflection [of reality that is both] conceptual and non-conceptual.

body.text: evaṃ yogī anena krameṇa ghaṭikām ardhapraharam ekapraharaṃ vā yāvatkālecchāparyantaṃ tattvaṃ bhāvayan tiṣṭhet / idaṃ tvarthapravicayadhyānam āryalaṅkāvatāre
body.translated_text: Thus the yogin, by this method, should abide meditating on reality for a <s>ghaṭikā</s> (24 minutes), half a <s>prahara</s> (1.5 hours), one <s>prahara</s> (3 hours), or for as long as one wishes. This, however, is the meditation of investigation of meaning (<s>arthapravicaya-dhyāna</s>), [as] in the <s>Āryalaṅkāvatāra</s>

body.text: nirdiṣṭam / tata icchayā samādherutthātuṃ paryaṅkam abhittvaivam anuvicintayet, amī dharmāḥ sarve paramārthataḥ niḥsvabhāvāḥ santo 'pi saṃvṛtau vyavasthitā eva / tathāsati karmaphalasambandhādayaḥ kathaṃ vyavasthitāḥ syuḥ? bhagavatā coktam-
body.translated_text: it is taught. Then, wishing to rise from <s>samādhi</s>, without breaking the cross-legged posture, one should reflect thus: 'All these <s>dharmas</s>, though in the ultimate sense devoid of own-nature, are indeed established in the conventional [world]. This being so, how are the connections of actions and their fruits and the rest established?' And the Blessed One has said:

body.text: "bhāvā vidyanti saṃvṛtyā paramārthe na bhāvakāḥ /" ityuktam /
body.translated_text: 'Entities exist conventionally; in the ultimate sense they are not entities.'

body.text: amī bālabuddhayo niḥsvabhāvavastuṣu bhāvādisamāropeṇa viparyastabuddhayo bhavanti / cirakālaṃ saṃsāracakre paribhramanti, tato 'haṃ kariṣyāmi anuttarapuṇyajñānasambhāraṃ paripūrya, tataḥ sarvajñapadaṃ prāpya tān dharmatām avabodhayeyam / evaṃ vicintayet / atha śanaiḥ paryaṅkaṃ bhittvā daśadigvyavasthitān sarvabuddhobodhisattvān praṇipatya tebhyaśca pūjāstotropahāraṃ kṛtvāryabhadracaryādimahāpraṇidhānaṃ praṇidadhīta / tataḥ śūnyatākaruṇāgarbhasakaladānādipuṇyasaṃbhāropārjane 'bhiyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: These childish minds, through superimposing existence and the rest upon things devoid of own-nature, become minds with inverted [understanding]. For a long time they wander in the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>. 'Therefore I shall act: having fulfilled the unsurpassed accumulations of merit and knowledge, and having thereby attained the rank of omniscience (<s>sarvajñapada</s>), I shall cause them to comprehend the nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>).' Thus one should reflect. Then, slowly breaking the cross-legged posture, having prostrated to all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> dwelling in the ten directions, and having made offerings, praises, and gifts to them, one should make the great aspiration of the <s>Āryabhadracarya</s> (Noble Conduct of <s>Samantabhadra</s>) and the rest. Then one should apply oneself to the accumulation of merit through all [forms of] giving and the rest, whose essence is emptiness and compassion (<s>śūnyatā-karuṇā-garbha</s>).

body.text: tathā ca sati taddhyānasarvākāravaropetaśunyatābhinirhāraḥ syāt / āryaratnacūḍe yathoktam- "sa maitrīvarmasaṃnaddho mahākaruṇāsthāne sthitvā sarvākāravaropetaśūnyatābhinirhāradhyānaṃ karoti / tatra sarvākāravaropetaśūnyatā katamā? yā dānapagati-śīlānapagati-kṣāntyanapagati-vīryānapagati-dhyānānapagati-prajñanāpagati-upāyānapagatītyādivistaroktiriti /" bodhisattvastu sarvasattvaparipākaṃ kurvīta / kṣetrakāyabahuparivārādisaṃpattiprādurbhāvopāyadānādikuśalaṃ cāvaśyaṃ seveta /
body.translated_text: When this is so, there will be the accomplishment of emptiness endowed with all the best aspects (<s>sarvākāravaropeta-śūnyatā</s>) through that meditation. As stated in the <s>Āryaratnacūḍa</s>: 'He, armored with loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and stationed in great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), performs the meditation of accomplishing emptiness endowed with all the best aspects. Therein, what is emptiness endowed with all the best aspects? That which is not separated from giving (<s>dāna</s>), not separated from moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), not separated from patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), not separated from vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), not separated from meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), not separated from wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), not separated from skillful means (<s>upāya</s>)' — and so forth in detail. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> should accomplish the ripening of all beings. And one must also cultivate the wholesome [activities] such as giving and the rest, which are the means for the manifestation of the splendors of [buddha-]fields, bodies, great retinues, and the like.

body.text: asati ca tathā buddhānām kṣetrādisaṃpattiryoktā sā kasya phalaṃ syāt / tasmāt sarvākāravaropetaṃ tatsarvajñajñānaṃ tu dānādyupāyena paripūryamāṇatvād bhagavān tat sarvajñajñānam upāyena paryantagatam ityavocat / tasmād bodhisattvena dānādyupāyo 'pi sevitavyo na tu śūnyatā eva / āryasarvadharmavaipulye
body.translated_text: Otherwise, whose fruit would be the splendors of <s>Buddha</s>-fields and the rest that are described? Therefore, since that omniscient knowledge endowed with all the best aspects is fulfilled through the means of giving and the rest, the Blessed One declared that omniscient knowledge 'has reached its culmination through skillful means.' Therefore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should also cultivate the means of giving and the rest — not emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) alone. In the <s>Āryasarvadharmavaipulya</s>,

body.text: "yo 'yaṃ maitreya! ṣaṭpāramitāsamudāgamo bidhisattvānāṃ sambodhāya taṃ te mohapuruṣā evaṃ vakṣyanti, prajñāpāramitāyām evaṃ bodhisattvena śikṣitavyam, kiṃ śeṣābhiḥ pāramitābhiriti ucyante / te 'nyāḥ pāramitā dūṣayitavyā maṃsyante / tat kiṃ manyase ajita! duṣprajñaḥ sa kāśirājo 'bhūd yena kapotārthena śyenāya svamāṃsāni dattāni? maitreya āha, no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavān āha- yāni mayā maitreya! bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā ṣaṭpāramitā-pratisaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlānyupacitāni, apakṛtaṃ nu taiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ? maitreya āha no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavān āha- tvaṃ tāvad ajita! ṣaṣṭikalpāna dānāpāramitāyāṃ samudāgataḥ, ṣaṣṭikalpān śīlapāramitāyaṃ ṣaṣṭikalpān kṣāntipāramitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭikalpān viryapāramitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭikalpān dhyānapāramitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭikalpān prajñāpāramitāyāṃ samudāgataḥ / tat te mohapuruṣā evaṃ vakṣyanti / ekanayenaiva bodhiryaduta śūnyatānayeneti te caryāpariśuddhā bhavantītyādi / "
body.translated_text: 'That which, <s>Maitreya</s>, is the practice of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) for the awakening of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — those deluded persons will say: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train only in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; what need is there for the remaining perfections?" They will think that the other perfections should be disparaged. What do you think, <s>Ajita</s>? Was that king of <s>Kāśī</s> of poor wisdom, who gave his own flesh to a hawk for the sake of a pigeon?' <s>Maitreya</s> said: 'No indeed, Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: 'The roots of merit connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s> that were accumulated by me, <s>Maitreya</s>, while practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct — were those roots of merit harmful?' <s>Maitreya</s> said: 'No indeed, Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: 'You yourself, <s>Ajita</s>, practiced the <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> for sixty <s>kalpas</s>, the <s>śīla-pāramitā</s> for sixty <s>kalpas</s>, the <s>kṣānti-pāramitā</s> for sixty <s>kalpas</s>, the <s>vīrya-pāramitā</s> for sixty <s>kalpas</s>, the <s>dhyāna-pāramitā</s> for sixty <s>kalpas</s>, and the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> for sixty <s>kalpas</s>. Those deluded persons will say: "There is only one approach to awakening, namely the approach of emptiness" — [and claim that] their conduct is purified' — and so forth.

body.text: upāyarahite sati bodhisattvaḥ prajñayā eva tu śrāvakavat buddhakāryāṇi kartuṃ na śaknoti / upāyasanāthaśca samartho bhavati / āryaratnakūṭe yathoktam- "tadyathā kāśyapa! amātyasaṃgṛhītā rājānaḥ sarvakāryāṇi kurvanti, evameva upāyakauśalyasaṃgṛhītā bodhisattvasya prajñā sarvabuddhakāryāṇi karoti /" iti / bodhisattvānāṃ mārgadṛṣṭerapyanyā tīrthikānāṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ ca mārgadṛṣṭirapyanyā / evaṃ tīrthikamārgadṛṣṭistu ātmādau viparyāsayuktatvāt sarveṇa sarvaḥ prajñārahito mārgaḥ / tasmāt te muktiṃ na prāpnuvanti /
body.translated_text: Without skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through <s>prajñā</s> alone, would be unable to accomplish <s>Buddha</s>-activities, just like a <s>Śrāvaka</s>. But endowed with skillful means, one is capable. As stated in the <s>Āryaratnakūṭa</s>: 'Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, kings supported by ministers accomplish all tasks, so too the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> wisdom, supported by skill in means, accomplishes all <s>Buddha</s>-activities.' The path-view of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is one thing, and the path-view of <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist practitioners) and <s>Śrāvakas</s> is another. The path-view of <s>tīrthikas</s>, being associated with errors regarding the self and the rest, is entirely a path devoid of wisdom. Therefore they do not attain liberation.

body.text: śrāvakāṇāṃ tu mahākaruṇārahitatvād upāyāyukatā / tasmāt te ekāntanirvāṇaparāyaṇāḥ bhavanti / bodhisattvamārgastu prajñopāyayukto manyate / tasmāt te apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇaparāyaṇā bhavanti / bodhisattvānāṃ mārgastu prajñopāyayukto manyate / tasmāt te apratisṭhitanirvāṇaṃ prāpnuvanti / prajñābalena tu saṃsāre na patati, upāyabalena ca nirvāṇe na patati /
body.translated_text: The path of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, being devoid of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), is lacking in skillful means. Therefore they become exclusively devoted to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. But the path of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is considered to be endowed with both wisdom and skillful means. Therefore they attain the non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhita-nirvāṇa</s>). Through the power of wisdom, one does not fall into <s>saṃsāra</s>; through the power of skillful means, one does not fall into <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: tasmād āryagayāśīrṣe- "dvāvimau bodhisattvānāṃ saṃkṣiptau mārgau / katamau dvau- yaduta prajñā copāyaśca /" ityākhyātam / āryaśrīparamādye 'pi uktam-
body.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>Āryagayāśīrṣa</s>: 'These are the two paths of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in brief. What are the two? Namely, wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and skillful means (<s>upāya</s>).' In the <s>Āryaśrīparamādya</s> also it is stated:

body.text: "prajñāpāramitā tu 'mātā' asti, upāyakauśalyaṃ ca 'pitā' asti / "āryavimalakīrtinirdeśasūtre 'pi- "bodhisattvānāṃ kiṃ bandhanam? kā ca muktiḥ? anupāyena bhavagatiparigraho hi bodhisattvasya bandhanam / upāyena bhavagatigamanaṃ muktiḥ / prajñārahitabhāvagatiparigraho bodhisattvasya bandhanam / prajñayā bhavagatigamanaṃ tu muktiḥ / upāyena aparigṛhītā prajñā hi bandhanam / upāyena parigṛhitā prajñā muktiḥ / prajñayāparigṛhītopāyo bandhanam / prajñayā gṛhītopāyaḥ muktiḥ iti" vistarena uktam /
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the "mother"; skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) is the "father."' In the <s>Āryavimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra</s> also: 'What is the bondage of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? And what is their liberation? Grasping at the modes of existence without skillful means — that is the bondage of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Going through the modes of existence with skillful means — that is liberation. Grasping at the modes of existence without wisdom — that is the bondage of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Going through the modes of existence with wisdom — that is liberation. Wisdom not accompanied by skillful means is bondage. Wisdom accompanied by skillful means is liberation. Skillful means not accompanied by wisdom is bondage. Skillful means accompanied by wisdom is liberation' — thus stated in detail.

body.text: bodhisattvasya prajñāmātrasevanaṃ tu śrāvakeṣṭanirvāṇapatitatvād bandhanavad bhaviṣyati / apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇena muktirna bhaviṣyati / tasmādupāyarahitā prajñā tu bodhisattvānāṃ bandhanamityucyate / tasmād vāyupīḍitena agnisevanavad bodhisattvena viparyāsavāyumātraprahāṇatvāt sopyāprajñayā śūnyatā sevitavyā, na tu śrāvakavat sākṣātkaraṇīyā / yathā āryadaśadharmasūtre coktam- "kulaputra! tadyathā yathā kaścinmanuṣyaḥ agniparicaryāṃ karoti, sa tadagnisatkāraṃ karoti, guruṃ karoti, kintu so 'yamiti mayā so 'gniḥ satkṛtya, gurūkṛtya mānitaśca iti kṛte 'pi eṣa dvābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ parigṛhītavya iti na cintayati / tat kasmāditi cet tannidhānne mayi kāyikaduḥkhaṃ cittadaurmanasyaṃ vā sambhāvyate iti cintanāt / tathaiva ca bodhisattve 'pi nirvāṇāśayo 'pyasti, nirvāṇa-pratyakṣaṃ na karoti / tat kasya hetoriti cet? tannidhānād ahaṃ bodhiṃ nirvarteyam iti cintanād" iti /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva's</s> cultivation of wisdom alone would be like bondage, since it results in falling into the <s>nirvāṇa</s> desired by <s>Śrāvakas</s>; liberation through non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhita-nirvāṇa</s>) would not occur. Therefore, wisdom devoid of skillful means is called the bondage of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore, just as one who is afflicted by wind cultivates fire [as a remedy], the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should also cultivate emptiness with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), since it abandons only the wind of error — but should not realize it directly as a <s>Śrāvaka</s> would. As stated in the <s>Āryadaśadharma-sūtra</s>: 'O son of good family, just as a certain person performs the service of fire — he honors that fire, respects it — but even having thought "I have honored, respected, and revered this fire," he does not think "I should grasp it with both hands." Why? Because he thinks "It would bring about bodily suffering and mental distress for me." In the same way, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> too has the aspiration for <s>nirvāṇa</s>, but does not directly realize <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? Because he thinks "From that [premature realization] I would [fail to] accomplish awakening."'

body.text: kevalam upāyamātrasevane 'pi bodhisattvaḥ pṛthagjanabhūmeranuttīrṇatvād atyavabaddha eva bhaviṣyati / tasmāt prajñāsahitamupāyaṃ seveta / evaṃ mantraparigṛhītaviṣavad bodhisattvakleśe 'pi prajñāparigrahabalena bhāvite sati amṛtikatā / punaḥ svabhāvena abhyudayaphalaṃ dānādi yadasti tatra kimuta
body.translated_text: If one cultivates skillful means alone as well, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, not having transcended the stage of ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana-bhūmi</s>), would remain extremely bound. Therefore one should cultivate skillful means accompanied by wisdom. In this way, just as poison grasped by a <s>mantra</s> [is rendered harmless], when even the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> are cultivated with the power of the grasp of wisdom, they become nectar-like. How much more so with giving and the rest, which by their very nature bear the fruit of prosperity? Therein, what then —

body.text: vaktavyam / āryaratnakuṭe coktaṃ yathā- "tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa! mantrauṣadhaparigṛhītaṃ viṣaṃ na vinipātayati evameva bodhisattvānām kleśaḥ prajñāparigṛhitatvād api na śaknoti vinipātayitum iti / "
body.translated_text: should be stated. And in the <s>Ārya-Ratnakūṭa</s> it is said thus: "Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, poison that is protected by <s>mantras</s> and herbs does not cause downfall—even so, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, being protected by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), are unable to cause downfall."

body.text: tasmād yena kāraṇena bodhisattva upāyabalena saṃsāramanutsṛjati tasmād nirvāṇe na patati / yasmāt prajñābalena sakalālambanaṃ prahīyate tasmāt saṃsāre na patati, tasmād apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇabuddhatvaṃ prāpyate / tasmād āryagaganagañje 'pi uktam- "tatprajñānena hi sarvakleśāḥ parivarjyante / upāyajñānena hi sarvasattvā na parityajyante /" iti / āryasaṃdhinirmocane 'pi- "ekāntasattvārthavimukhasya ekāntasaṃskārābhisaṃskāravimukhasya nānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiruktā mayeti /" tasmād buddhatvaprātukāmena prajñopāyau ubhau sevitavyau /
body.translated_text: Therefore, since by the power of <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not abandon <s>saṃsāra</s>, he does not fall into <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Since by the power of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) all objects of clinging are abandoned, he does not fall into <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore <s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa-buddhatva</s> (Buddhahood of non-abiding nirvāṇa) is attained. Therefore in the <s>Ārya-Gaganagañja</s> too it is said: "By <s>prajñā</s>-knowledge, all <s>kleśas</s> are eliminated. By <s>upāya</s>-knowledge, all beings are not abandoned." And in the <s>Ārya-Saṃdhinirmocana</s> too: "I have not declared unsurpassed perfect awakening for one who is entirely averse to the welfare of beings, nor for one who is entirely averse to the conditioning of formations." Therefore, one who desires to attain Buddhahood must cultivate both <s>prajñā</s> and <s>upāya</s>.

body.text: tatra lokottaraprajñābhāvanāvasare, atisamāhitāvasare vā dānādyupāyasevanāsambhāvanāyāmapi tatra prayogatatpṛṣṭhalabdhaprajñayoḥ yo 'pi bhavati, tadā upāyasevanaṃ bhavatyeva / tasmāt prajñāpāyau yugapat pravartete / punaraparaṃ bodhisattvānām ayaṃ hi prajñopāyayuganaddhavāhi mārgaḥ sarvasattvāvalokitamahākaruṇayā parigṛhītatvāt lokottaramārgaḥ sevyate, utthānopāyakāle 'pi māyākāravad aviparyastameva dānādi sevyate / āryākṣayamatinirdeśe 'pi yathoktam- "tatra ko hi bodhisattvopāyaḥ? kaśca prajñābhinirhāra iti? yataḥ samādhāne sattvāvalokitamahākaruṇāvalambane cittopasthāpanā sa eva upāyaḥ / yataḥ śāntipraśāntisamāpattiḥ sā tu tatprajñā"iti vistaraḥ / māradamanaparicchede 'pi uktam- "punaraparaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ samutkarṣikaprayogastu prajñājñānena abhiyogaṃ karoti / upayajñānena sarvakuśaladharmasaṃgraho
body.translated_text: Therein, even at the time of cultivating supramundane <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), or at the time of deep concentration, although the cultivation of <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) such as giving and so forth is not possible, yet through the <s>prajñā</s> of the preparatory and post-attainment [stages] that exists at that time, there is cultivation of skillful means. Therefore <s>prajñā</s> and <s>upāya</s> operate simultaneously. Moreover, this path of <s>bodhisattvas</s> that yokes wisdom and skillful means together operates thus: because it is embraced by <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) that looks upon all beings, the supramundane path is cultivated; and at the time of arising and [practicing] skillful means, giving and so forth are cultivated without distortion, like a magician. As stated in the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamatinirdeśa</s>: "What then is the <s>bodhisattva's</s> skillful means? And what is the manifestation of wisdom? That wherein, in concentration, the mind is established in the support of great compassion looking upon beings—that itself is the skillful means. That which is the attainment of peace and quiescence—that is the wisdom." Thus in detail. And in the <s>Māradamanapariccheda</s> too it is stated: "Moreover, the supreme application of <s>bodhisattvas</s> applies itself through <s>prajñā</s>-knowledge. Through <s>upāya</s>-knowledge, the gathering of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>

body.text: 'pi prayujyate / prajñājñānena nairātmya-asattva-ajīva-apoṣa-apudgaleṣu ca prayujyate / upāyajñānena yaḥ sarvasattvaparipāko 'pi prayojyaḥ" iti vistaraḥ / āryadharmasaṃgītisūtre 'pi-
body.translated_text: is also applied. Through <s>prajñā</s>-knowledge, one applies oneself to <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness), non-being, non-soul, non-nourishing, and non-person. Through <s>upāya</s>-knowledge, the ripening of all beings is also to be applied." Thus in detail. In the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṅgīti-sūtra</s> too:

children.translated_text: Just as a certain magician strives for the liberation of his creation,

children.text: na cāsya nirmite saṅgo jñātapūrvo yato 'sya saḥ //
children.translated_text: yet he has no attachment to his creation, since he has known it from the beginning;

body.text:
tribhavaṃ nirmitaprakhyaṃ jñātvā sambodhipāragaḥ /
saṃnahyate jagaddhetorjñātapūrva jagat tathā // iti /
body.translated_text:
knowing the three realms to be like a creation, one who has reached the shore of awakening
girds himself for the sake of the world, having known the world likewise from the beginning.

body.text: bodhisattvanām prajñopāyavidhireva sādhyamadhikṛtya tatprayogasaṃsāre sthito 'pi asti, āśayanirvāṇe sthito 'pi syād ityuktam /
body.translated_text: It is said that the method of <s>prajñā</s> and <s>upāya</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, with regard to what is to be accomplished and its application, is such that one may be established in <s>saṃsāra</s> and one may be established in <s>nirvāṇa</s> by intention.

body.text: tādṛśyāṃ śūnyatāmahākaruṇāgarbhānuttarasamyaksaṃbuddhau pariṇatadānādyupāyabhāvanāṃ kṛtvā, paramārthabodhicittotpādārtha pūrvavat nityaṃ kāle kāle śamathavipaśyanāprayogo yathāśakti bhāvanīyaḥ / āryagocarapariśuddhisūtre- sarvāvasthāsu sattvārthakāribodhisattvānāmanuśaṃsā yathā nirdiṣṭā tathā saṃnihitasmṛtyā sarvadā upāayakauśalaṃ bhāvitavyam /
body.translated_text: Having cultivated the meditation on <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) such as giving and so forth, dedicated to such unsurpassed perfect awakening whose core is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion), the practice of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) should be cultivated at all times to the best of one's ability for the purpose of generating <s>paramārthabodhicitta</s> (ultimate awakening mind), as before. As the benefits are taught in the <s>Ārya-Gocarapariśuddhi-sūtra</s> for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who perform the welfare of beings in all situations, so too, with ever-present mindfulness, skill in <s>upāya</s> should always be cultivated.

body.text: tādṛkkaruṇopāyabodhicittabhāvakaḥ sa iha janmani avaśyaṃ viśiṣṭo bhavati / tasmāt svapne nityaṃ buddhabodhisattvadarśanaṃ bhaviṣyati / susvapnāntarāṇyapi dṛśyante / devā api anumodanād rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti / pratikṣaṇamapi vipulapuṇyajñānasambhārasaṃcayo bhaviṣyati / kleśāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyamapi kṣīṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / sarvadaiva sukhasaumanasyamadhikaṃ bhaviṣyati / bahujanapriyo bhaviṣyati / śarīre 'pi rogagrasto na bhaviṣyati / paramacittakarmaṇyatāpi prāptā bhaviṣyati / tasmād abhijñatādiviśiṣṭaguṇaprāptiḥ /
body.translated_text: One who thus cultivates <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), and <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) will certainly become distinguished in this very life. Therefore, the seeing of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will constantly occur in dreams. Good dreams will also be seen. The gods too, out of rejoicing, will provide protection. At every moment there will be a vast accumulation of the stores of merit and knowledge. The rigidity of the obscuration of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) will be diminished. There will always be abundant happiness and joy. One will be dear to many people. There will be no affliction by disease in the body. The supreme pliancy of mind will also be attained. Therefore, the attainment of distinguished qualities such as <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) and the rest [will follow].

body.text: atha ṛddhibalena anantalokadhātūn gatvā bhagavato buddhān pūjayati / tebhyaḥ dharmo 'pi śrūyate / maraṇasamaye 'pi avaśyameva buddhabodhisattvadarśanaṃ bhaviṣyati / janmāntare 'pi buddhabodhisattvānapagatadeśaviśiṣṭagṛhe cāpi janma bhaviṣyati / tasmād anāyāsapuṇyajñānasambhāraḥ paripūrayiṣyate / mahābhogo bahuparivāraśca bhaviṣyati / tīkṣṇaprajñayā bahujanaparipākamapi kariṣyanti / sarvajātiṣu jātismaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / tādṛśī aparimitānuśaṃsā sūtrāntareṣu saṃbhūtā avagantavyā /
body.translated_text: Then, by the power of <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous ability), having gone to infinite world-realms, one worships the blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. From them, the <s>Dharma</s> is also heard. At the time of death too, the seeing of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will certainly occur. In the next life too, there will be birth in a distinguished household in a land not devoid of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore, the stores of merit and knowledge will be fulfilled effortlessly. One will possess great enjoyment and an extensive retinue. With sharp <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), one will also ripen many beings. In all births, there will be recollection of [past] births. Such immeasurable benefits should be understood as set forth in other <s>sūtras</s>.

body.text: tena tādṛkkaruṇopāyabodhicittāni ca nityam ādareṇa ciraṃbhavitāni kramaśaḥ cittasaṃtāne atipariśuddhakṣaṇotpādena paripākabhūtatvād araṇimanthanāgnivat samyagarthabhāvanāprakarṣaparyantaṃ gamanaṃ bhūtvā lokottarajñānasakalavikalpajālāpagamanaṃ niṣprapañcadharmadhātuprasphuṭāvagati, nirmalaniścalanirvātasthitapradīpavat niścalapramāṇabhūtaḥ, sarvadharmanairātmyasvabhāvaḥ tattvasākṣātkārī, darśanamārgasaṃgṛhītaḥ paramārthabodhicittasvabhāva utpadyate / tadutpādād vastuparyantatālambane praviṣṭaḥ / tathāgatagotre utpadyate, bodhisattvānapakṣālapravṛttiḥ, lokasarvagatinivṛttiḥ, bodhisattvadharmatādharmadhātvavabodhasthitiḥ, prāptabodhisattvaprathamabhūmiḥ ityanuśaṃsā tadvistaraḥ daśabhūmyādiṣu avagantavyaḥ / idaṃ tathatālambanadhyānam āryalaṅkāvatāre nirdiṣṭam / idaṃ tu bodhisattvānām niṣprapañcanirvikalpatāyāmeva praviśati /
body.translated_text: Then, when such <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), and <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) have been cultivated with care for a long time, by the arising of an extremely purified moment in the mental continuum, progressively reaching maturity—like fire from the friction of fire-sticks—reaching the culmination of the supreme cultivation of the true meaning, there arises supramundane knowledge that is free from the entire net of conceptualization, the clear realization of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) free from proliferation, steady and authoritative like a lamp standing still, unflickering, in a windless place, whose nature is the <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) of all <s>dharmas</s>, the direct realization of reality, included in the <s>darśanamārga</s> (path of seeing), of the nature of <s>paramārthabodhicitta</s> (ultimate awakening mind). Upon its arising, one has entered the object that is the ultimate limit of entities. One is born in the <s>Tathāgata</s> lineage; one proceeds without falling away from the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [path]; all worldly destinations cease; one abides in the realization of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, the <s>dharmatā</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>; one has attained the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) of the <s>bodhisattva</s>—thus the benefits. The details should be understood from the <s>Daśabhūmi</s> and other [texts]. This is the meditation on <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) as its object, as taught in the <s>Ārya-Laṅkāvatāra</s>. This enters into the very state of non-conceptuality free from proliferation for <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: adhimuktibhūmau tu adhimuktivaśāt pravṛttirvyavasthāpitā na tu abhisaṃskāreṇa / tajjñānaprādurbhāve tu sākṣāt praveśaḥ / tathā prathamabhūmipraveśaḥ tadanantaraṃ bhāvanāmārge lokottareṇa tatpṛṣṭhalabdhajñānena dvābhyāṃ ca prajñopāyabhāvanākrameṇa bhāvanāpraheyasaṃcitāvaraṇasya sūkṣmasūkṣmataravyavadānād uttarottaraviśiṣṭaguṇaprāptaye adhobhūmipariśodhanena tathāgatajñānaparyantaṃ praviśya, sarvajñatāsāgaram avatīrya, kāryapariniṣpattyālambanamapi prāpnoti / evaṃ krameṇa eva cittasaṃtānapariśuddhiḥ āryalaṅkāvatāre 'pi uktā / āryasaṃdhinirvocane
body.translated_text: On the <s>adhimuktibhūmi</s> (stage of aspiration), however, the operation is established by the power of aspiration, not by [direct] realization. But upon the manifestation of that knowledge, there is direct entry. Thus, upon entering the first <s>bhūmi</s>, thereafter on the <s>bhāvanāmārga</s> (path of meditation), by the two—supramundane and post-attainment knowledge—through the method of cultivating <s>prajñā</s> and <s>upāya</s>, by the progressively subtler purification of the accumulated obscurations to be abandoned by meditation, for the attainment of successively more distinguished qualities, by the purification of the lower <s>bhūmis</s>, one enters up to the extent of <s>Tathāgata</s> knowledge, descending into the ocean of omniscience, and also attains the object of the completion of [all] purposes. In this way, progressively, the purification of the mental continuum is also stated in the <s>Ārya-Laṅkāvatāra</s>. In the <s>Ārya-Saṃdhinirmocana</s>

body.text: 'pi yathoktam- "krameṇottarottarabhūmisu suvarṇavat cittaṃ vyavadāya, anuttarasaṃyaksaṃbodhiparyantam abhisaṃbudhyati" iti /
body.translated_text: too, as stated: "Progressively purifying the mind on the successively higher <s>bhūmis</s>, like gold, one fully awakens up to the extent of unsurpassed perfect awakening."

body.text: sarvajñatāsāgarapraveśe sati cintamaṇivat sakalasattvopajīviguṇaskandhayuktaḥ pūrvapraṇīdhānaphalasatkṛtaḥ, mahākaruṇāsvabhāvabhūtaḥ, anābhoganānopayayuktaḥ, aparimitanirmāṇairaśeṣajagatsarvārthākaraḥ kṛtaḥ / aśeṣaguṇasaṃpattiprakarṣaparyantabhutaḥ, savāsanādoṣaṃ sakalamalaṃ nirākṛtya, sattvadhātvantaparyantavihārī, iti prekṣāvān bhagavati buddhe sakalaguṇākare śraddhām utpādya tadguṇapariniṣpattyarthaṃ svayaṃ sarvān prayatnān kuryāt / tasmād bhagavatā evamuktam- "tadetat sarvajñajñānaṃ karuṇāmūlaṃ bodhicittahetukam upāyaparyavasānam" iti /
body.translated_text: Upon entering the ocean of omniscience, endowed with the aggregate of qualities that sustain all beings like a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel), honored by the fruit of former aspirations, whose nature is <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion), endowed with effortless and manifold <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), accomplishing all purposes of the entire world through unlimited emanations. Being the culmination of the excellence of the complete perfection of all qualities, having removed all defilement together with its <s>vāsanās</s> (habitual tendencies), abiding throughout the realm of beings to its very end—thus the discerning one, having generated faith in the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, the treasury of all qualities, should make all efforts for the perfection of those qualities. Therefore the Blessed One said thus: "That all-knowing knowledge has compassion as its root, <s>bodhicitta</s> as its cause, and <s>upāya</s> as its culmination."

children.translated_text: The virtuous, having removed the impurity of envy and the rest, are insatiable for qualities, like the ocean for waters;

children.text: vivecya gṛṇhanti subhāṣitāni haṃsāḥ payo yatpayāṃsi prahṛṣṭāḥ //
children.translated_text: they discerningly take up what is well-spoken, like joyful <s>haṃsas</s> (swans) [who separate] milk from water.
Therefore, the mind confused by bias has been cast away by the wise;
everything well-spoken should be accepted, even from a child.

children.text: prakāśya yat prāpi mayā śubham asamapaddhitam /
children.translated_text: Whatever good [merit] I have obtained by composing [this], by the incomparable path,
by that merit, may all people attain the middle path.

body.text: ācāryakamalaśīlena madhye nibaddho bhāvanākramaḥ samāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: The middle <s>Bhāvanākrama</s>, composed by <s>Ācārya Kamalaśīla</s>, is completed.

body.text: bharatīyopādhyāyena prajñāvarmaṇā mahālokacakṣuṣā vandyajñānasenena cānūdya sunirṇitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Translated and finalized by the Indian preceptor <s>Prajñāvarman</s> and the great world-illuminating <s>Vandyajñānasena</s>.

body.text: bhāvanākramaḥ dvītīyaḥ samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: The Second <s>Bhāvanākrama</s> is completed.

body.text: : blank
3. bhāvanākramastṛtīyaḥ
body.translated_text: 3. Third <s>Bhāvanākrama</s>

body.text: mahāyānasūtrāntanayapravṛttānāṃ saṃkṣepato bhāvanākramaḥ kathyate / tatra yadyapi bodhisattvānāmaparimito 'pramāṇādibhedene bhagavatā samadhirupadiṣṭaḥ, tathāpi śamathavipaśyanābhyāṃ sarve samādhayo vyāptā iti / sa eva śamathavipaśyanāyuganaddhavāhī mārgastāvat kathyate / uktaṃ ca bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: The method of meditation (<s>bhāvanākrama</s>) is briefly stated for those who have entered the path of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtras. Therein, although the Blessed One has taught immeasurable <s>samādhis</s> (meditative concentrations) to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> with distinctions such as immeasurable and so forth, nevertheless all <s>samādhis</s> are pervaded by <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). Therefore, the path that bears the union of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> is first stated. And the Blessed One has said —

body.text:
nimittabandhanāj janturatho doṣṭhulabandhanāt /
vipaśyanāṃ bhāvayitvā śamathaṃ ca vimucyate // iti /
body.translated_text:
A being is bound by signs and further bound by the coarse [afflictions];
having cultivated <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) and <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), one is liberated.

body.text: tasmāt sakalāvaraṇa-prahāṇārthina śamathavipaśyane sevanīye / śamathabalena svālambane cittam aprakampyaṃ bhavati nivātasthitapradīpavat / vipaśyanayā yathāvad dharmatattvāvagamāt samyagjñānālokaḥ samutpadyate, tataḥ sakalam āvaraṇaṃ prahīyate, andhakāravad ālokodayāt /
body.translated_text: Therefore, one who desires the abandonment of all obscurations should practice <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). By the power of <s>śamatha</s>, the mind becomes unshakable upon its object, like a lamp placed in a windless spot. By <s>vipaśyanā</s>, through the proper comprehension of the reality of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), the light of correct knowledge arises, and then all obscuration is removed — just as darkness [is dispelled] by the arising of light.

body.text: ata eva bhagavatā catvāryālambanavastūni yogināṃ nirdiṣṭāni / nirvikalpapratibimbakam, savikalpapratibimbakam, vastuparyantatā, kāryapariniṣpattiśca / tatra śamathena yat sarvadharmapratibimbakaṃ buddhādirūpaṃ cādhimucyālambyate tena nirvikalpapratibimbakam ucyate / tatra bhūtārthanirūpaṇāvikalpābhāvān nirvikalpakam ucyate / yathāśrutodgṛhītānāñca dharmāṇāṃ pratibimbakam adhimucyālambyata iti kṛtvā pratibimbakam ucyate / tad eva pratibimbakaṃ yadā vipaśyanayā vicārayati yogī tattvādhigamārthaṃ tadā savikalpapratibimbakam ucyate, tattvanirūpaṇavikalpasya vipaśyanālakṣaṇasya tatra samudbhavāt / tasyaiva ca pratibimbasya svabhāvaṃ nirūpayan
