body.translated_text: For this very reason, four objects of meditation (<s>ālambanavastu</s>) have been taught by the Blessed One for yogins: the non-conceptual reflection (<s>nirvikalpapratibimbaka</s>), the conceptual reflection (<s>savikalpapratibimbaka</s>), the limit of reality (<s>vastuparyantatā</s>), and the accomplishment of the purpose (<s>kāryapariniṣpatti</s>). Therein, that which is apprehended with conviction through <s>śamatha</s> as the reflection of all <s>dharmas</s> in the form of a <s>Buddha</s> and so forth is called the non-conceptual reflection — because therein there is an absence of the conceptualization of examining true meaning, it is called non-conceptual. And because the reflection of <s>dharmas</s> as heard and retained is apprehended with conviction, it is called 'reflection.' When the yogin examines that very reflection through <s>vipaśyanā</s> for the purpose of comprehending reality, then it is called the conceptual reflection, because the conceptualization of examining reality — which has the character of <s>vipaśyanā</s> — arises therein. And when, examining the own-nature of that very reflection

body.text: yogī darpaṇāntargatasvamukha-pratibimbapratyavekṣaṇena svamukhagatavairūpyāṇāṃ viniścayavat, sarvadharmāṇāṃ yathāvat svabhāvāvagamāt / yadā vastu paryantatālakṣaṇāṃ tathatāṃ pratibidhyati, tadā vastuparyantatāvagamāt prathamāyāṃ bhūmau vastuparyantatālambanam ucyate / tato bhāvanāmārgeṇa pariśiṣṭāsu bhūmiṣvoṣadhirasāyanopayogād iva krameṇa viśuddhataratamakṣaṇodayād āśrayaparāvṛttau satyām, āvaraṇa-prahāṇalakṣaṇa-kāryaparisamāptiryadā bhavati tadā buddhabhūmau tad eva jñānaṃ kāryapariniṣpattyālambanam ucyate /
body.translated_text: , the yogin — just as one, by observing the reflection of one's own face within a mirror, ascertains the blemishes on one's own face — comprehends the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are; when one penetrates <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), which has the character of the limit of reality, then, through comprehension of the limit of reality, on the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage), this is called the object of the limit of reality. Then, through the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), on the remaining <s>bhūmis</s> — like the gradual use of medicinal elixirs — through the successive arising of increasingly pure moments, when the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>) has occurred and the accomplishment of the purpose characterized by the abandonment of obscurations is achieved, then on the <s>Buddha-bhūmi</s> (stage of Buddhahood), that very knowledge is called the object of the accomplishment of the purpose.

body.text: tad evam anena kiṃ darśitaṃ bhavati? śamathavipaśyanābhyāṃ samastavastuparyantatādhigamo bhavati / tena cāvaraṇaprahāṇalakṣaṇā kāryapariniṣpattiravāpyate / tad eva ca buddhatvam / ato buddhatvādhigamārthinā śamathavipaśyane sevanīye / yastu te na sevate tasya naiva vastuparyantatādhigamo nāpi kāryapariniṣpattiriti / tatra śamathaścittaikāgratā / vipaśyanā bhūtapratyavekṣeti saṃkṣepād āryaratnameghādau bhagavatā śamathavipaśyanayorlakṣaṇam uktam / tatra yoginā śīlaviśuddhayādau śamathavipaśyanāsaṃbhāre sthitena sarvasattveṣu mahākaruṇām utpādya, samutpādita-bodhicittena śrutacintābhāvanāyāṃ prayoktavyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, what is shown by this? Through <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), there is the complete comprehension of the limit of reality. And through that, the accomplishment of the purpose characterized by the abandonment of obscurations is obtained. And that itself is <s>Buddhahood</s>. Therefore, one who desires the attainment of <s>Buddhahood</s> should practice <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>. For one who does not practice them, there will be neither the comprehension of the limit of reality nor the accomplishment of the purpose. Therein, <s>śamatha</s> is one-pointedness of mind. <s>Vipaśyanā</s> is the examination of reality — thus, in brief, the Blessed One has stated the characteristics of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s> and elsewhere. Therein, the yogin, established in the equipment of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> beginning with the purification of moral conduct, having generated great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward all sentient beings, having aroused the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>), should apply himself to hearing, reflecting, and meditating.

body.text: tatra prathamaṃ tāvad yogī bhāvanā-kāle sarvam itikaraṇiyaṃ parisamāpya kṛtamūtrapurīṣaḥ kaṇṭaka-svarādirahite mano 'nukūle pradeśe sthitvā mayā sarvasattvā bodhimaṇḍe niṣpādayitavyā iti viniścayan, sakalajagadabhyuddharaṇāśayo mahākaruṇām āmukhīkṛtya, daśadigavasthitān sarvabuddhabodhisattvān pañcāṅgena praṇipatyāgrato buddhabodhisattvān pīṭhādau sthāpayitvā anyatra vā yathāvat tebhyaśca yathāruci pūjāstavanaṃ kṛtvā svapāpaṃ pradeśya, sakalasdya jagataḥ puṇyam anumodya, mṛdutarasukhāsane vairocanabhaṭṭārakabaddhaparyaṅkeṇa
body.translated_text: Therein, first, at the time of meditation, the yogin, having completed all that needs to be done, having relieved himself, situated in a place free from thorns, [disturbing] sounds, and the like, and agreeable to the mind, resolving 'I must bring all sentient beings to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>),' with the intention of rescuing the entire world, facing great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), having prostrated with the five limbs to all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> dwelling in the ten directions, having set up [images of] <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in front on a seat or elsewhere as appropriate, having performed worship and praise to them as one pleases, having confessed one's sins, having rejoiced in the merit of the entire world — on a soft and comfortable seat, in the cross-legged posture of the Lord <s>Vairocana</s>

body.text: ardhaparyeṅkeṇa vā niṣadya nātyunmīlite nātinimīlite nāsikāgravinyaste cakṣuṣī kṛtvā, nātinamraṃ nātistabdham ṛjukāyaṃ praṇidhāyāntarmukhāvarjitasmṛtirupaviśet / tataḥ skandhau samau sthāpayet / śiro nonnataṃ nāvanatam ekapārśve niścalaṃ sthāpayitavyam / kiṃ tarhi nābhipraguṇā nāsikā sthāpayitavyā / dantoṣṭhaṃ mṛdu sthāpanīyam / jivhā copari dantamūle sthāpanīyā / āśvāsapraśvāsāstu na saśabdā nāpi śthūlā nāpi tvaritāḥ karaṇīyāḥ / kiṃ tvasaṃlakṣayamāṇāṃ mandaṃ mandamanābhogena yathā praviśeyurnirgaccheyurvā tathā karaṇiyam /
body.translated_text: or in the half-cross-legged posture, one should sit with the eyes neither too open nor too closed, directed at the tip of the nose, the body held straight — neither too bent nor too stiff — with mindfulness turned inward. Then one should place the shoulders level. The head should be placed neither raised nor lowered, motionless to one side. Rather, the nose should be aligned straight with the navel. The teeth and lips should be placed gently. The tongue should be placed at the base of the upper teeth. The inhalations and exhalations should be made neither audible, nor coarse, nor hurried — but imperceptibly, slowly, gently, and effortlessly, so that they enter and exit [naturally].

body.text: tatra prathamaṃ tāvad yogī yathādṛṣṭaśrute tathāgatavigrahe cittaṃ sthāpayitvā śamathaṃ niṣpādayet / tañca tathāgatavigraham uttaptakanakāvadātaṃ lakṣaṇānuvyañjanālaṃkṛtaṃ parṣanmaṇḍalamadhyagataṃ nānāvidhairupāyaiḥ sattvārthaṃ kurvantaṃ prābandhikena manasikāreṇa tadguṇābhilāṣaṃ samupādāya layauddhatyādīn vyupaśamayya tāvad dhyāyed yāvat sphuṭataraṃ puro 'vasthitamiva taṃ paśyet / tataḥ tasya tathāgatavigrahapratibimbakasyāgatigatiṃ nirūpayato vipaśyanāṃ bhāvayati / tataścaivaṃvidhaṃ vicintayet / yathedaṃ tathāgatavigrahapratibimbakaṃ na kutaścid āgataṃ nāpi kvacid gamiṣyati tiṣṭhadapi svabhāvaśūnyam ātmātmīyarahitaṃ tathā eva sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvaśūnyā āgatigatirahitāḥ pratibimbopamāḥ, bhāvādirūparahitā iti vicāryoparatavicāreṇa nirjalpaikarase manasā tattvaṃ bhāvayan yāvadicchaṃ tiṣṭhet / ayaṃ ca samādhiḥ pratyutpannabuddhasaṃmukhāvasthitasamādhirnirdiṣṭaḥ / asya cānuśaṃsā vistaratastatraiva sutre bodhayitavyā /
body.translated_text: Therein, first, the yogin, having fixed the mind on the form of a <s>Tathāgata</s> as seen or heard, should accomplish <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding). And that form of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — radiant like molten gold, adorned with the [major] marks and [minor] signs, situated in the midst of an assembly, accomplishing the welfare of beings through various means — with continuous mental engagement, generating aspiration for his qualities, pacifying dullness, excitement, and the like, one should meditate until one sees him as though clearly present before one. Then, examining the coming and going of the reflection of that <s>Tathāgata</s> form, one cultivates <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). Then one should contemplate thus: just as this reflection of the <s>Tathāgata</s> form has neither come from anywhere nor will go anywhere, and even while appearing is empty of own-nature, devoid of self and what belongs to self, so too all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are empty of own-nature, devoid of coming and going, comparable to reflections, and free from the form of arising and so forth — thus investigating, with the cessation of investigation, with a mind of a single taste, free from verbal elaboration, one should abide in reality as long as one wishes while meditating. And this <s>samādhi</s> has been taught as the <s>Pratyutpannabuddhasaṃmukhāvasthita-samādhi</s> (concentration of standing in the presence of the presently appearing Buddhas). The benefits of this should be understood in detail in that very sūtra.

body.text: etāvatā prakāreṇa sarvadharmasaṃgraho bhavati, tatra cittam upanibadhya layauddhatyādipraśamena śamathaṃ niṣpādayet / rūpyarūpibhedena ca
body.translated_text: By this method, all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are encompassed. Having fixed the mind thereon, pacifying dullness, excitement, and the like, one should accomplish <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding). And by the division of form and formless

body.text: saṃkṣepāt sarvadharmasaṃgrahaḥ / tatra rūpaskandhasaṃgṛhītā rūpiṇaḥ / vedanādiskandhasvabhāvā arūpiṇaḥ / tatra bālā bhāvādigrahābhiniveśād viparyastadhiyaḥ saṃsāre paribhramanti / teṣāṃ viparyāsāpanayanāya, teṣu ca mahākaruṇām āmukhīkṛtya, niṣpannaśamatho yogī tattvādhigamāya tato vipaśyanāṃ bhāvayet / bhūtapratyavekṣaṇā ca vipaśyanocyate / bhutaṃ punaḥ pudgaladharmanairātmyam /
body.translated_text: , all <s>dharmas</s> are encompassed in brief. Therein, those included in the <s>rūpa-skandha</s> (aggregate of form) are material (<s>rūpin</s>). Those whose nature is the aggregate of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and so forth are immaterial (<s>arūpin</s>). Therein, the childish (<s>bāla</s>), with minds perverted due to clinging to existence and so forth with respect to these, wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). For the removal of their perversion, and having faced great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward them, the yogin who has accomplished <s>śamatha</s> should then cultivate <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) for the comprehension of reality. And the examination of reality is called <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Reality, moreover, is the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgala-nairātmya</s>) and the selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharma-nairātmya</s>).

body.text: tatra pudgalanairātmyaṃ yā skandhānāmātmātmīyarahitatā / dharmanairātmyaṃ yā teṣāmeva māyopamatā / tatraivaṃ yogī nirūpayet / na tāvad rūpādivyatiriktaḥ pudgalo 'sti / tasyā pratibhāsanāt / rūpādiṣvevāhamiti pratyayotpattiśca / na cāpi rūpādiskandhasvabhāvaḥ pudgalaḥ / teṣāṃ rūpādīnāmanityānekasvabhāvatvāt / pudgalasya ca nityaikarūpeṇa parairupakalpitatvāt / nāpi tattvānyatvābhyām anabhilāpyapudgalasya vastutvaṃ yuktam / vastusataḥ prakārāntarābhāvāt / tasmād alīkavibhrama evāyaṃ lokasya yadutāhaṃ mameti niścayaṃ pratipannasya / tato rūpiṇo 'pi dharmān dharmanairātmyādhigamāya vicārayet- kim ete cittavyatirekeṇa paramārthasantaḥ sthitāḥ āhosviccittameva rūpādinirbhāsaṃ svapnāvasthāyāṃ pratibhāsavat pratibhāsata iti / sa tān paramāṇuśo nirūpayan, paramāṇūṃśca bhāgaśaḥ pratyavekṣamāṇo nopalabhate / tathā cānupalabhamānasteṣu astināstitvavikalpān nivartayati /
body.translated_text: Therein, the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgala-nairātmya</s>) is the absence of self and what belongs to self in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). The selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharma-nairātmya</s>) is the illusion-like nature of those very [skandhas]. Therein, the yogin should examine thus: First, no person (<s>pudgala</s>) exists distinct from the <s>skandhas</s> of form and so forth, because of [merely] appearing as such. And the arising of the cognition 'I' occurs only with respect to form and so forth. Nor is the person of the nature of the <s>skandhas</s> of form and so forth, because those — form and so forth — are impermanent and of multiple natures, while the person has been imagined by others as permanent and of a single form. Nor is it reasonable for the ineffable person to be a real entity through either identity or difference, because there is no other mode [of being] for a real thing. Therefore, this is indeed the delusion of the world — namely, of one who has adopted the conviction 'I' and 'mine.' Then, for the purpose of comprehending the selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharma-nairātmya</s>), one should also examine material (<s>rūpin</s>) <s>dharmas</s> — are these established as ultimately real apart from mind, or is it mind itself that appears as form and so forth, as in the appearance [of objects] in the dream state? He, examining them atom by atom, and examining the atoms too part by part, does not find [any substance]. And thus, not finding [anything], he ceases the conceptualizations of 'exists' and 'does not exist' regarding them.

body.text: cittamātrañca traidhātukam avatarati nānyathā / atha coktaṃ laṅkāvatāre-
body.translated_text: And one enters [the understanding that] the triple world is mind-only, and not otherwise. As stated in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s> —

body.text:
aṇuśo vibhajati dravyaṃ na caiva rūpaṃ vikalpayet /
cittamātravyavasthānaṃ kudṛṣṭyā na prasīdati // iti /
body.translated_text: One divides substance atom by atom, yet one should not conceptualize form; one who does not accept the position of mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>) is [afflicted by] wrong views.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavati cittamevānādikālikavitatharūpādyabhiniveśavaśāt svapnopalabhyamānarūpādipratibhāsavad bālānāṃ bahiḥ vicchinnamiva rūpādipratibhāsaṃ khyāti / tasmāccittamātrameva traidhātukam / sa evaṃ cittameva sakaladharmaprajñaptiṃ niścitya tatra pratyavekṣya ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvaḥ pratyavekṣito bhavatīti cittasvabhāvamapi pratyavekṣate / sa evaṃ vicārayati, cittamapi paramārthato māyāvad anutpannam / yada hi alīkasvabhāvarūpādyākāropagraheṇa cittameva citrākāraṃ pratibhāsate, tadāsyāpi rūpādivat tadavyatirekāt satyatvaṃ kutra bhavet? yathā citrākāratayā rūpādayo naikānekasvabhāvāstathā cittamapi tadavyatirekeṇa naikānekasvabhāvam / nāpi cittamutpādyamānaṃ kutaścid āgacchati / nāpi nirudhyayānaṃ kvacid gacchati / nāpi svaparobhayataḥ paramārthenāsyotpādo yuktaḥ / tasmān māyopamameva cittam / yathā cittamevaṃ sarvadharmā māyāvat paramārthato 'nutpannāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then he thinks thus: It is mind alone that, under the power of beginningless false attachment to form and the rest, appears to childish beings — like the appearance of form and the rest apprehended in a dream — as if form and the rest are perceived externally as separate. Therefore, the three realms are mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>). Having thus ascertained that mind alone is the designation of all <s>dharmas</s>, and having examined therein [the nature of dharmas] — since the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s> has been examined, he also examines the own-nature of mind itself. He investigates thus: Mind too is, in the ultimate sense, unborn like an illusion (<s>māyā</s>). For when mind itself appears in variegated forms through the apprehension of the aspects of form and the rest — which are of false nature — then how could mind have reality, since it is not different from form and the rest? Just as, through having variegated forms, form and the rest are neither of single nor multiple nature, so too mind, being not different from them, is neither of single nor multiple nature. Mind when arising does not come from anywhere; mind when ceasing does not go anywhere. Nor is its arising from self, other, or both reasonable in the ultimate sense. Therefore mind is just like an illusion. Just as mind [is thus], all <s>dharmas</s> are, like an illusion, ultimately unborn.

body.text: yenāpi cittena pratyavekṣate yogī tasyāpi svabhāvaṃ parīkṣamāṇo nopalabhate / tad evaṃ yatra yatrālambane yoginaścittaṃ prasaret tasya tasya svabhāvaṃ parīkṣamāṇo [tat svabhāvamapi nopalabhate] 'sau yada nopalabhate tadā sarvameva vastu vicārya kadalīskandhavad asāramavagamya, tataścittaṃ vivartayati / tato bhāvādivikalpoparatau sarvaprapañcavigatam ānimittaṃ yogaṃ pratilabhate / tathā coktam āryaratnameghe- "sa evam apakṣālakuśalaḥ sarvaprapañcavigamāya śūnyatābhāvanāyā yogamāpadyate / sa śūnyatābhāvanābahulo yeṣu yeṣu sthāneṣu cittaṃ prasarati cittamabhiramate tāni tāni sthānāni svabhāvataḥ
body.translated_text: Even the mind with which the yogin examines — examining its own-nature, he does not find [it]. Thus, wherever the yogin's mind ranges to an object, examining the own-nature of each — [he does not find its own-nature either]. When he does not find [it], then, having investigated all things and comprehended them as essenceless like a plantain trunk (<s>kadalī-skandha</s>), he turns the mind back. Then, with the cessation of conceptual construction of existence and the rest, he attains the signless (<s>ānimitta</s>) yoga free from all elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>). As stated in the <s>Āryaratnamegha</s>: 'He, being skilled in purification, undertakes the yoga of cultivating emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) for the elimination of all elaboration. He, being immersed in the cultivation of emptiness, wherever the mind ranges, wherever the mind delights — those very places, examining [them] by [their] own-nature,

body.text: parigaveṣamāṇaḥ śūnyaṃ pratividhyati [yat cittaṃ tadapi parīkṣamāṇaṃ śūnyaṃ pratividhyati] yenāpi cittena parīkṣate tad api svabhāvataḥ parigaveṣyamāṇaṃ śūnyaṃ pratividhyati / sa evam upaparīkṣamāṇo nirnimittatāyāṃ yogamāpadyate /" tad eva anenaivaṃ darśitaṃ bhavati / yastu nopaparīkṣate tasya nāsti nirnimittatāyāṃ praveśa iti /
body.translated_text: he penetrates [them as] empty. [The mind that examines, examining that too, he penetrates as empty.] Even the mind with which he examines, seeking [it] by its own-nature, he penetrates as empty. He, thus examining, undertakes the yoga of signlessness.' By this it is shown: For one who does not examine, there is no entry into signlessness.

body.text: sa evaṃ dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvamupaparīkṣamāṇo yada nopalabhate, tadāstīti na vikalpayati nāstīti na vikalpayati / yo 'sau nāstīti kalpyate tasya buddhau sarvadaivāpratibhāsanāt / yadi hi bhāvaḥ kadācid dṛṣṭo bhavet, tadā tasya pratiṣedhān nāstīti kalpayet / yadā kālatraye 'pi yoginā prajñayā nirūpayatā bhāvo nopalabdhaḥ tadā kasya pratiṣedhān nāstīti kalpayet / evamanye vikalpāstasya tadānīṃ na santi eva, bhāvābhāvavikalpābhyāṃ sarvasya vikalpasya vyāptatvāt / evaṃ vyāpakābhāvād byāpyasyāpyabhāvaḥ / evaṃ sati niṣprapañcanirvikalpatāmavatīrṇo bhavati, rūpādiṣu cāniśrito bhavati / prajñayā ca nirūpayataḥ sakalavastusvabhāvānupalambhāt prajñottaradhyāyī bhavati / sa evaṃ pudgaladharmanairātmyamayaṃ tattvamavatīrṇaḥ, aparasya parīkṣaṇīyasya cābhāvād, uparatavicāreṇa nirvikalpaikarasena manasā svarasavāhinā, anabhisaṃskārataḥ tad eva tattvaṃ sphuṭataram avadhārayan yogī tiṣṭheta / tatra ca sthitaścittabandhaṃ na vikṣipet /
body.translated_text: When, thus examining the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, he does not find [it], he does not conceptualize 'It exists,' nor does he conceptualize 'It does not exist.' That which would be conceptualized as 'It does not exist' never appears at all to his awareness. For if an entity had ever been seen, then through its negation one might conceptualize 'It does not exist.' But when the entity has not been found by the yogin examining with wisdom in all three times, then through the negation of what would one conceptualize 'It does not exist'? In this way, other conceptual constructions also do not exist for him at that time, since all conceptual construction is pervaded by the conceptual constructions of existence and non-existence. Thus, from the absence of the pervader, the pervaded too is absent. This being so, he has entered the state of being free from elaboration and non-conceptual, and he becomes unattached to form and the rest. And since, through examining with wisdom, the own-nature of all things is not found, he becomes one whose meditation goes beyond <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). He, having thus entered reality consisting of the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s> (<s>pudgala-dharma-nairātmya</s>), and since there is nothing further to be examined — with investigation ceased, with a mind of one taste that is non-conceptual, flowing of its own accord, effortlessly — the yogin should abide, ascertaining that very reality ever more clearly. And while abiding therein, he should not let the binding of the mind be distracted.

body.text: yadāntarā cittaṃ bahirdhā vikṣiptaṃ paśyet tadā tatsvabhāvapratyevekṣaṇena vikṣepaṃ praśamayya, punastatraiva cittamuparyupari prerayet / yadā tu tatrānabhirataṃ cittaṃ paśyet, tadā samādherguṇadarśanād abhiratiṃ tatra thāvayet / vikṣepe ca doṣadarśanād aratiṃ praśamayet / atha styānamiddhābhibhavād yada pracāratayā līnaṃ cittaṃ paśyet, layābhiśaṅkitaṃ vā tadā pramodyavastu buddharūpādikamālokasaṃjñāṃ vā manasikṛtya layamupaśamayet, tatastad eva tattvaṃ dṛḍhataraṃ
body.translated_text: When in the meanwhile he sees the mind distracted outward, he should pacify the distraction by examining its own-nature, and then direct the mind again and again to that very [reality]. When he sees the mind disinclined toward that [reality], he should cultivate delight in it by seeing the virtues of <s>samādhi</s>. He should pacify disinclination by seeing the faults in distraction. When, due to being overcome by dullness and drowsiness (<s>styāna-middha</s>), he sees the mind sunken through its dullness, or apprehends the appearance of sinking, he should pacify the sinking by attending to a joyful subject such as the form of a <s>Buddha</s>, or to the perception of light. Then he should grasp that very reality more firmly

body.text: gṛṇhīyāt / yadā tu jātyandhavad andhakārapraviṣṭapuruṣavad vinimīlitākṣavat sphuṭataraṃ tattvaṃ nāvadhārayed yogī, tadā tasya līnaṃ cittaṃ veditavyaṃ vipaśyanārahitaṃ ca / atha yathā pūrvānubhūtaviṣayaspṛhayā cittamantarā samuddhataṃ paśyed, auddhatyābhiśaṅkitaṃ vā, tadānityatādi saṃvegavastumanasikārād auddhatyaṃ śamayet / tataḥ punaḥ tatraiva tattve cittānabhisaṃskāravāhitāyāṃ yatnaṃ kurvīta / yadā ca vikṣiptapuruṣavad vānaravad vānavasthitavṛtti cittaṃ bhavet, tad auddhatyaṃ boddhavyaṃ śamatharahitaṃ ca / atha yadā layauddhatyābhyāṃ viviktatayā samapravṛttaṃ svarasavāhi sphuṭataraṃ tatraiva tattve cittam utpādyate tadābhogaśithilīkaraṇād upekṣaṇiyam / tadā ca śamathavipaśyanāyuganaddhavāhī mārgoniṣpanno veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: When the yogin, like one born blind, like a person who has entered darkness, or like one with closed eyes, does not ascertain reality clearly, then his mind should be known as sunken and lacking <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). When he sees the mind agitated in the meanwhile through craving for previously experienced sense-objects, or apprehends the appearance of agitation, he should pacify the agitation by attending to subjects that produce disenchantment, such as impermanence and the rest. Then he should make effort again toward the effortless flow of the mind upon that very reality. When the mind is of unstable behavior, like a distracted person or like a monkey, that should be recognized as agitation, and as lacking <s>śamatha</s>. Now, when — free from sinking and agitation — the mind arises evenly, flowing of its own accord, clearly upon that very reality, then one should relax the effort [and apply] equanimity. At that point, the path of the unified flow of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (<s>yuganaddha</s>) should be known as accomplished.

body.text: yadā ca vipaśyanā bhāvayet prajñātiriktatarā bhāvayet, tadā śamathasyālpatvāt pravātasthitapradipavat pracalatvāccittasya na sphuṭataraṃ tattvadarśanaṃ bhavet / atastadā śamatho bhāvayitavyaḥ / śamathasyābhyādhikye middhāvaṣṭabadhapuruṣasyeva sphuṭataraṃ tattvadarśanaṃ na syāt / tasmāt tadā prajñā bhāvayitavyā / yadā samapravṛtte dve api bhavato yuganaddhavāhibalīvardadvayavat tadānabhisaṃskāreṇaiva tāvat sthātavyaṃ yāvat kāyacittapīḍā na bhavet /
body.translated_text: When one cultivates <s>vipaśyanā</s> with excessive wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), then, due to the weakness of <s>śamatha</s>, the mind wavers like a lamp placed in the wind, and there is no clear seeing of reality. Therefore, at that time, <s>śamatha</s> should be cultivated. When <s>śamatha</s> is in excess, like a person overcome by drowsiness, there would be no clear seeing of reality. Therefore, at that time, <s>prajñā</s> should be cultivated. When both flow evenly — like a pair of yoked oxen flowing in unison — then one should abide with just effortlessness, so long as no affliction of body or mind arises.

body.text: saṃkṣepataḥ sarvasyaiva samādheḥ ṣaḍ doṣā bhavanti / kausīdyam, ālambanasaṃpramoṣaḥ, layaḥ, auddhatyam, anābhogaḥ, ābhogaśceti / eṣāṃ pratipakṣeṇāṣṭau prahāṇasaṃskārā bhāvanīyāḥ / śraddhā, chandaḥ, vyāyāmaḥ, prasrabdhiḥ, smṛtiḥ, saṃprajanyam, cetanā, upekṣā ceti / tatrādyāścatvāraḥ kausīdyapratipakṣāḥ / tathā hi- samādhiguṇeṣvabhisaṃpratyayalakṣaṇayā śraddhayā yogino 'bhilāṣaḥ samutpadyate / tato 'bhilāṣavān vīryamārabhate / tato vīryārambhaṇāt kāyacittayoḥ karmaṇyatāṃ bhāvayati / tataḥ prasrabdhakāyacetasaḥ
body.translated_text: In brief, there are six faults in all forms of <s>samādhi</s>: laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), forgetting the object (<s>ālambana-saṃpramoṣa</s>), sinking (<s>laya</s>), agitation (<s>auddhatya</s>), non-application (<s>anābhoga</s>), and [over-]application (<s>ābhoga</s>). As their antidotes, eight abandonment-formations (<s>prahāṇa-saṃskāra</s>) should be cultivated: faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), aspiration (<s>chanda</s>), exertion (<s>vyāyāma</s>), pliancy (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), clear comprehension (<s>samprajanya</s>), volition (<s>cetanā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). Therein, the first four are the antidotes to laziness. For through faith — characterized by confidence in the virtues of <s>samādhi</s> — aspiration arises in the yogin. From that aspiration, one endowed with aspiration begins vigor. Through the undertaking of vigor, one cultivates pliancy of body and mind. Then, when body and mind are pliant,

body.text: kausīdyaṃ vyāvartate / tataḥ [śraddhādayaḥ kausīdyaprahāṇāya bhavanti] tadartha te bhāvanīyāḥ / smṛtirālambana-saṃpramoṣasya pratipakṣaḥ / saṃprajanyaṃ layauddhatyayoḥ pratipakṣaḥ / tayostena samupekṣya parivarjanāt / layauddhatyāpraśamanakāle tu anābhogadoṣaḥ tatastatpratipakṣeṇa cetanā bhāvanīyā / layauddhatyapraśame sati, yadā praśamabāhi cittaṃ bhavet, tadābhogadoṣaḥ / tasya pratipakṣastadānīm upekṣā bhāvanīyā / yadi samapravṛtte citte ābhogaḥ kriyate, tadā cittaṃ vikṣipyate / līne 'pi citte sati yadyābhogo na kriyate, tadā vipaśyanārahitatvād, andhapuruṣavaccittaṃ līnaṃ syāt / tasmāt līnacittaṃ nigṛṇhīyād, uddhataṃ praśamayet, punaḥ samāprāptam upekṣeta /
body.translated_text: laziness is turned back. Therefore, [faith and the rest are for the abandonment of laziness;] they should be cultivated for that purpose. Mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) is the antidote to forgetting the object. Clear comprehension (<s>samprajanya</s>) is the antidote to sinking and agitation — by observing and avoiding them through that [faculty]. When sinking and agitation have not been pacified, there is the fault of non-application; as its antidote, volition (<s>cetanā</s>) should be cultivated. When sinking and agitation have been pacified, when the mind is flowing calmly, there is the fault of [over-]application; as its antidote at that time, equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) should be cultivated. If effort is applied when the mind is flowing evenly, then the mind would be distracted. Even when the mind is sunken, if effort is not applied, then — being devoid of <s>vipaśyanā</s> — the mind would be sunken like a blind person. Therefore, the sunken mind should be raised up, the agitated [mind] should be pacified, and the evenly attained [mind] should be [treated with] equanimity.

body.text: tato yāvadiccha yogī tāvad anabhisaṃskāreṇaiva tattvaṃ bhāvayaṃstiṣṭhet / satyāṃ tu kāyādipīḍāyāṃ punaḥ punarantarā sakalameva lokaṃ vyavalokyamāyājala candropamapratibhāsaṃ [vata] avataret / tatha coktam avikalpapraveśe- lokottareṇa jñānenākāśasamatalān sarvadharmānpaśyati / pṛṣṭhalabdhena punarmāyāmarīcisvapno dakacandropamān paśyatīti / tad evaṃ māyopamaṃ jagad avagamya, sattveṣu mahākaruṇām āmukhīkṛtyaivam anuvicintayet / evaṃvidhaṃ dharmagāmbhoryam anavagacchanto 'mī bālabuddhaya ādiśānteṣveva dharmeṣu bhāvādisamāropaviparyastā vividhakarmakleśān upacinvanti / tataḥ saṃsāre paribhramanti, tato 'haṃ kariṣyāmi yathaitān evaṃvidhaṃ dharmāgāmbhīryam avabodhayeyam iti, tato viśramya punarapi tathaiva sarvadharmanirābhāsaṃ samādhimavataret / cittakhede sati, tathaiva viśramya punaravataret / evam anena krameṇa ghaṭikām [arthapraharam] ekapraharaṃ vā yāvantaṃ kālaṃ śaknoti tāvantaṃ kālaṃ tiṣṭhet /
body.translated_text: Then, the <s>yogin</s> should remain meditating on reality effortlessly for as long as he wishes. But when there is physical and other distress, he should intermittently arise and, surveying the entire world, descend [again into meditation seeing it] as an appearance like a net of illusions, a moon [reflected in water]. And thus it is stated in the <s>Avikalpapraveśa</s>: 'By supramundane knowledge, one sees all <s>dharmas</s> as equal to space. By post-attainment [knowledge], one sees them as like illusions, mirages, dreams, and the moon [reflected] in water.' Having thus understood the world as illusion-like, with <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) toward beings placed at the forefront, one should reflect thus: 'Not understanding such profundity of the <s>Dharma</s>, these beings of childish intelligence, distorted by the superimposition of existence and so forth upon <s>dharmas</s> that are primordially peaceful, accumulate various <s>karmas</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Thus they wander in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore I shall act so as to awaken them to such profundity of the <s>Dharma</s>.' Then, having rested, one should again enter the <s>samādhi</s> in which all <s>dharmas</s> are without appearance, in the same manner. When there is mental fatigue, one should likewise rest and enter again. In this way, by this method, one should remain for a <s>ghaṭikā</s> (24 minutes), [a half-<s>prahara</s>], or one <s>prahara</s> (3 hours)—for as long a time as one is able.

body.text: tata icchayā samādheḥ utthātuṃ paryaṅkam abhittvaivam anuvicintayet / yadi nāmāmī dharmāḥ sarva eva paramārthato 'nutpannāstathāpi māyavat pratiniyatavividhahetupratyayasāmagrīvaśena vicitrā evāvicāraramaṇīyāḥ pravartante, tena nocchedadṛṣṭiprasaṅgaḥ / nāpyapavādāntasya, yataśca prajñayā vicāryamāṇā nopalabhyante, tena na śāśvatadṛṣṭiprasaṅgo nāpi samāropāntasya / tatra ye prajñācakṣurvikalatayā viparyastamatayā ātmābhiniviṣṭā vividhāni karmāṇi kurvanti te saṃsāre paribhramanti / ye punarekāntena saṃsāravimukhā mahākāruṇyavikalatayā ca na [sattvārthaṃ] dānādipāramitāḥ paripūrayanti ātmānaṃ damayanti te sattvā upāyavikalatayā śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhau patanti /
body.translated_text: Then, wishing to arise from <s>samādhi</s>, without breaking the cross-legged posture, one should reflect thus: Although all these <s>dharmas</s> are indeed ultimately unarisen, yet, like illusions, by the power of the assemblage of their specific and various causes and conditions, they proceed in variety, delightful without analysis. Therefore there is no implication of the annihilationist view, nor of the extreme of denial. And since, when examined with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), they are not apprehended, therefore there is no implication of the eternalist view, nor of the extreme of superimposition. Therein, those who, through the deficiency of the eye of <s>prajñā</s> and with distorted understanding, cling to self and perform various <s>karmas</s>—they wander in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Those again who are one-sidedly averse to <s>saṃsāra</s> and who, through the deficiency of <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion), do not fulfill the <s>pāramitās</s> of giving and so forth [for the welfare of beings] but discipline only themselves—those beings, through the deficiency of <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), fall into the awakening of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>.

body.text: ye tu asvabhāvaṃ jagad avagamya mahākāruṇyabalena sakalajagadabhyuddharaṇakṛtaniścayā māyākāravad aviparyastadhiyo vipulapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāraṃ samupāyanti te tathāgataṃ padaṃ prāpyāsaṃsāramaśeṣasya jagataḥ sarvākāraṃ hitasukhāni saṃpādayantaḥ tiṣṭhanti / te ca jñāna[sambhāra]balena [samasta]kleśaprahāṇān na saṃsāre patanti sarvasattvāpekṣayā ca samupārjitavipulāprameyapuṇyasaṃbhāravaśena na nirvāṇe patanti, sarvasattvopajīvyāśca bhavanti / tasmān mayā sakalasattvahitasukhādhānārthināpratiṣṭhitanirvāṇam adhigantukāmena vipulapuṇyajñāna-saṃbhāropārjane 'bhiyogaḥ [sadā] karaṇiyaḥ / tathā coktam āryatathāgataguhyasutre- "jñānasambhāraḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇāya saṃvartate / puṇyasambhāraḥ sarvasattvopajīvitāyai saṃvartate / tasmāt tarhi bhagavan bodhisattvena mahāsattvena puṇyasambhāre jñānasaṃbhāre ca sarvadābhiyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ" iti / āryatathāgatotpattisaṃbhasūtre coktam- "sa khalu punareṣa tathāgatānāṃ
body.translated_text: But those who, understanding the world as without own-nature, through the power of <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) have determined to uplift the entire world, and who, with undistorted understanding like that of a magician, accumulate the vast stores of merit and knowledge—they, having attained the <s>Tathāgata</s> state, remain accomplishing the welfare and happiness of the entire world in every way throughout <s>saṃsāra</s>. And through the power of the accumulation of knowledge, by the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), they do not fall into <s>saṃsāra</s>. And through the power of the vast, immeasurable store of merit accumulated with regard to all beings, they do not fall into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and they become sustenance for all beings. Therefore, I who desire to attain <s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s> (non-abiding nirvāṇa) for the purpose of bestowing welfare and happiness upon all beings must always apply myself to the accumulation of the vast stores of merit and knowledge. And thus it is stated in the <s>Ārya-Tathāgataguhya-sūtra</s>: "The accumulation of knowledge leads to the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>. The accumulation of merit leads to being sustenance for all beings. Therefore, Blessed One, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> must always apply himself to both the accumulation of merit and the accumulation of knowledge." And in the <s>Ārya-Tathāgatotpattisaṃbhava-sūtra</s> it is stated: "Moreover, this arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s>

body.text: saṃbhavo naikena kāraṇena bhavati / tat kasya hetoḥ? samudāgataistāvad bho jinaputrāprameyaśatasahasradaśakāraṇaistathāgatāḥ samudāgacchanti / katamairdaśabhiryadutāprameyapuṇyajñānasambhārātṛptisamudāgamakāraṇeneti" vistara / āryavimalakīrtinirdeśe coktam- "śatapuṇyanirjātāḥ sarvakuśaladharmanirjātā apramāṇakuśalamūlakarmanirjātāḥ kāyāstathāgatasyeti" vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: does not occur from a single cause. Why is that? For <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise from immeasurable hundreds of thousands of ten causes. What are those ten? Namely, the cause of insatiable accumulation of immeasurable stores of merit and knowledge—" and so forth in detail. And in the <s>Ārya-Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s> it is stated: "The bodies of <s>Tathāgatas</s> are born from a hundred [types of] merit, born from all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, born from the action of immeasurable roots of merit—" and so forth in detail.

body.text: tad evaṃ kṛtvā śanaiḥ paryaṅkaṃ bhittvā daśadigvyavasthitān sarvabuddhabodhisattvān praṇipatya tebhyaśca pūjāstotropahāraṃ kṛtvāryabhadracaryādipraṇidhānaṃ pranidadhīta / tataḥ śūnyatākaruṇāgarbhānuttarasaṃbodhipariṇāmitasakaladānādipuṇyasaṃbhāropārjanābhiyukto bhavet /
body.translated_text: Having done so, one should slowly break the cross-legged posture, bow to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in the ten directions, and having made offerings, hymns of praise, and presentations to them, one should make aspirations such as the <s>Ārya-Bhadracaryā</s> and others. Then one should be engaged in the accumulation of the entire store of merit through giving and the rest, dedicated to unsurpassed perfect awakening, with <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) at its core.

body.text: yastu manyate, cittavikalpasamutthāpitaśubhāśubhakarmavaśena sattvāḥ svargādikarma phalamanubhavantaḥ saṃsāre saṃsaranti / ye punarna kiñciccintayanti nāpi kiñcit karma kurvanti te parimucyante saṃsārāt / tasmānna kiñciccintayitavyam / nāpi dānādikuśalacaryā kartavyā / kevalaṃ mūrkhajanamadhikṛtya dānādikuśalacaryā nirdiṣṭeti / tena sakalamahāyānaṃ pratikṣiptaṃ bhavet / mahāyānamūlatvācca sarvayānānāṃ tatpratikṣepeṇa sarvam eva yānaṃ pratikṣiptaṃ syāt / tathā hi 'na kiñciccintayitavyamiti' bruvata bhutapratyavekṣālakṣaṇā prajñā pratikṣiptā bhavet / bhūtapratyavekṣā-mūlatvāt samyagjñānasya tatpratikṣepā llokottarāpi prajñā pratikṣiptā bhavet / tatpratikṣepāt sarvākārajñatā pratikṣiptā bhavet / nāpi dānādicaryā kartavyeti vadatā copāyo dānādiḥ sphuṭatarameva pratikṣiptaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, one who thinks: 'Through the power of good and bad <s>karma</s> produced by mental conceptualization, beings experience the fruits of <s>karma</s> such as heaven and so forth and transmigrate in <s>saṃsāra</s>. But those who do not think anything at all and do not perform any <s>karma</s> are liberated from <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore nothing should be thought about. Nor should wholesome practice such as giving and so forth be performed. Wholesome practice such as giving and so forth was taught merely for the benefit of fools'—by such [a view] the entire <s>Mahāyāna</s> would be rejected. And since <s>Mahāyāna</s> is the root of all vehicles, by its rejection all vehicles would be rejected. For by saying 'nothing should be thought about,' the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) characterized by the examination of reality would be rejected. Since right knowledge has the examination of reality as its root, by its rejection even supramundane <s>prajñā</s> would be rejected. By its rejection, <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) would be rejected. And by saying 'the practice of giving and so forth should not be performed,' <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) consisting of giving and so forth is most explicitly rejected.

body.text: etāvad eva ca saṃkṣiptaṃ mahāyānaṃ yaduta prajñopāyaśca / yathoktam āryagayāśīrṣe- "dvāvimau bodhisattvānāṃ saṃkṣiptau mārgau / katamau dvau? yaduta
body.translated_text: The entirety of <s>Mahāyāna</s>, in brief, is just this: <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means). As stated in the <s>Ārya-Gayāśīrṣa</s>: 'There are two paths of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in brief. What are the two? Namely,

body.text: prajñā copāyaśca /" āryatathāgataguhyasūtre coktam- "imau ca prajñopāyau bodhisattvānāṃ sarvapāramitāsaṃgrahāya saṃvartete" iti / tataśca mahāyānaṃ pratikṣipatā mahat karmāvaraṇaṃ kṛtaṃ syāt / tasmād [mahāyānaṃ pratikṣipataḥ, alpaśrutasya, ātmadṛṣṭiṃ parāmṛśataḥ,] asyānupāsitavidvajjanasyānavadhārita-tathāgata-pravacananīteḥ svayaṃ vinaṣṭasya parān api nāśayato yuktyāgamadūṣitatvāt, viṣasaṃsṛṣṭavacanaṃ saviṣabhojanamiva ātmakāmena dhīmatā dūrata eva parihartavyam /
body.translated_text: <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means).' And in the <s>Ārya-Tathāgataguhya-sūtra</s> it is stated: 'These <s>prajñā</s> and <s>upāya</s> lead to the gathering of all <s>pāramitās</s> for <s>bodhisattvas</s>.' Therefore, by rejecting <s>Mahāyāna</s>, a great karmic obstruction would be created. Therefore, the words of one who rejects <s>Mahāyāna</s>, who is of little learning, who clings to the view of self, who has not attended upon the learned, who has not properly ascertained the method of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> teaching, who is self-destroyed and destroys others—being corrupted by reasoning and scripture, like speech mixed with poison, like poisoned food—should be avoided from afar by the wise who care for themselves.

body.text: tathā hyanena bhūtapratyavekṣāṃ pratikṣipatā dharmapravicayākhyaṃ pradhānam eva bodhyaṅgaṃ pratikṣiptaṃ syāt / vinā ca mūtapratyavekṣayā yoginaḥ katham anādikālābhyastarūpādibhāvābhiniveśasya cittaṃ nirvikalpatāṃ praviśet? sarvadharmeṣvasmṛtyamanasikāreṇa praviśatīti cet, tad ayuktam / na hi vinā bhūtapratyavekṣayānubhūyamāneṣvapi sarvadharmeṣvasmṛtiramanasikāro vā śakyate kartum / yadi ca nāmāmī dharmā mayāsmartavyā nāpi manasikartavyā ityevaṃ bhāvayannasmṛtimanasikārau teṣu bhāvayet tadā sutarām eva tena te smṛtā manasikṛtāśca syuḥ / atha smṛtimanasikārābhāvamātram asmṛtyamanasikārāvabhipretau, tadā tayorabhāvaḥ kena prakāreṇa bhavatīti etad eva vicāryate / na cābhāvaḥ kāraṇaṃ yuktam, yena tato [nirnimittāmanasikārāt] nirvikalpatā bhavet / [tanmātrato 'vikalpatāyāṃ] saṃmurcchitasyāpi smṛtimanasikārābhāvān nirvikalpatāpraveśaprasaṅgaḥ / na ca bhūtapratyavekṣāṃ vinānya upāyo 'sti yena prakāreṇāsmṛtyamanasikārau kuryāt /
body.translated_text: For by this person who rejects the examination of reality, the very foremost limb of awakening called <s>dharmapravicaya</s> (investigation of dharmas) would be rejected. And without the examination of reality, how could the <s>yogin's</s> mind, which has clung to the existence of form and so forth since beginningless time, enter non-conceptuality? If one says: 'It enters through non-mindfulness and non-attention regarding all <s>dharmas</s>'—that is untenable. For without the examination of reality, non-mindfulness or non-attention cannot be accomplished even regarding <s>dharmas</s> that are being experienced. And if one, thinking 'these <s>dharmas</s> are not to be remembered by me, nor to be attended to,' thus cultivates non-mindfulness and non-attention regarding them—then all the more would those [dharmas] be remembered and attended to by that very [person]. If mere absence of mindfulness and attention is meant by non-mindfulness and non-attention, then the question is: in what manner does their absence come about? Mere absence is not a logically valid cause by which non-conceptuality would arise from [causeless] non-attention. [If it were,] then even one who has fainted would have entry into non-conceptuality, since mindfulness and attention are absent [in that state]. Nor is there any other means apart from the examination of reality by which one could produce non-mindfulness and non-attention.

body.text: satyapi cāsmṛtyamanasikārasambhave, vinā bhūtapratyavekṣayā niḥsvabhāvatā dharmāṇāṃ katham avagatā bhavet? na hi svabhāvata evaṃ dharmāḥ
body.translated_text: And even if non-mindfulness and non-attention were possible, without the examination of reality, how could the essencelessness of <s>dharmas</s> be understood? For <s>dharmas</s> are not by their very nature

body.text:
śūnyāḥ sthitā ityevaṃ vinā tatpratyavekṣayā tacchūnyatāprativedho bhavet / nāpi vinā śūnyatāprativedhena āvaraṇaprahāṇaṃ saṃbhavati sarvatra sarveṣāṃ muktiprasaṅgāt /
kiṃ ca tasya yogino yadi sarvadharmeṣu muṣitasmṛtitayā mūḍhatayā vā smṛtimanasikārau na pravartete, tadātyantamūḍhaḥ katham asau yogī bhavet / vinā ca bhūtapratyavekṣayā tatrāsmṛtim amanasikāraṃ cābhyastatā moha evābhyasto bhavet / tata eva samyagjñānāloko dūrīkṛtaḥ syāt / athāsau na muṣitasmṛtirnāpi mūḍhaḥ, tadā kathaṃ tatrāsmaraṇam amanasikāraṃ kartu śaknuyād vinā bhūtapratyavekṣayā / na hi smaranneva na smarati, paśyan eva na paśyatīti yuktam abhidhātum / asmṛtyamanasikārābhyāsācca kathaṃ pūrvanivāsānusmṛtyādi-buddhadharmodayo bhavet, virodhāt, na hyuṣṇaviruddhaṃ śītam āsevamānasya uṣṇasparśasaṃvedanaṃ bhavet /
body.translated_text:
they abide as empty" — without that examination of it, there would be no realization of that emptiness. Nor is the abandonment of obscurations possible without the realization of emptiness, for otherwise liberation would absurdly follow for everyone everywhere.
Furthermore, if for that <s>yogin</s>, with respect to all <s>dharmas</s>, mindfulness and mental attention (<s>smṛti-manasikāra</s>) do not operate due to loss of mindfulness or due to delusion, then being utterly deluded, how could he be a <s>yogin</s>? And without examination of reality (<s>bhūtapratyavekṣā</s>), if one cultivates non-mindfulness and non-attention toward that, it would be delusion itself that is cultivated. Thereby the light of correct knowledge would be driven far away. But if he is neither one who has lost mindfulness nor deluded, then how could he practice non-remembering and non-attention toward that without examination of reality? For it is not reasonable to assert that one who is remembering does not remember, or that one who is seeing does not see. And through the practice of non-mindfulness and non-attention, how could the arising of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities such as the recollection of former lives (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛti</s>) come about? Because of contradiction — for one who cultivates cold, which is contrary to heat, would not have the experience of a warm sensation.

body.text: kiṃ ca samādhisamāpannasya yogino yadi manovijñānam asti, tadāvaśyaṃ tena kiṃcid ālambayitavyam / na hi pṛthagjanānāṃ sahasā nirālambanaṃ jñānaṃ bhavet / atha nāsti, tadā kathaṃ niḥsvabhāvatā dharmāṇāmavagatā bhavet? kena ca pratipakṣeṇa kleśāvaraṇaṃ prahīyate? na ca caturthadhyānālābhinaḥ pṛthagjanasya cittanirodhaḥ saṃbhavati / tasmāt saddharme yāvasmṛtyamanasikārau paṭhitau tau bhūtapratyavekṣāpūrvākau draṣṭavyau / asmād bhūtapratyavekṣayāsmṛtirmanasikāraśca śakyate kartum, nānyathā / tathā hi yadā nirūpayan samyakprajñayā yogī kālatraye paramārthataḥ samutpannaṃ na kaṃcid dharma paśyati, tadā tatra kathaṃ smṛtimanasikārau kuryāt / yo hi kālatraye 'pyasattvān nānubhūtaḥ paramārthataḥ sa kathaṃ smaryeta, manasi vā kriyeta / tato 'sau sarvaprapañcopaśamaṃ nirvikalpaṃ jñānaṃ praviṣṭo bhavet / tatpraveśācca śūnyatāṃ pratividhyati tatprativedhācca prahīṇasakalakudṛṣṭijālo bhavati /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, if the <s>yogin</s> who has attained <s>samādhi</s> possesses mind-consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>), then he must necessarily apprehend some object. For ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) cannot suddenly have objectless cognition. But if he does not possess it, then how could the essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>) of <s>dharmas</s> be understood? And by what antidote would the obscuration of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) be abandoned? Moreover, the cessation of mind is not possible for an ordinary being who has not attained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. Therefore, wherever non-mindfulness and non-attention are taught in the true <s>Dharma</s>, they should be understood as preceded by examination of reality (<s>bhūtapratyavekṣā</s>). Through this examination of reality, non-mindfulness and non-attention can be accomplished, not otherwise. For when the <s>yogin</s>, investigating with correct <s>prajñā</s>, does not see any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that has ultimately arisen in the three times, then how could he apply mindfulness and attention toward that? For that which, not existing in the three times, has not been ultimately experienced — how could it be remembered or attended to mentally? Thereupon he enters the cognition that is free from conceptual elaboration (<s>nirvikalpa-jñāna</s>), the pacification of all proliferation (<s>prapañcopaśama</s>). And through that entry, he realizes emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), and through that realization, the entire net of wrong views is abandoned.

body.text: upāyayuktaḥ prajñāsevanataśca samyak saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyakuśalo bhavati / ato 'nāvaraṇajñānalābhāt sarvān eva buddhadharmān adhigacchati / tasmānna vinā bhūtapratyavekṣayā samyagjñānodayo nāpi kleśāvaraṇaprahāṇām / tathā coktaṃ mañjuśrīvikurvitasūtre- "kathaṃ dārike bodhisattvo vijitasaṃgrāmo bhavati? āha, yo mañjuśrīḥ vicāya vicāya sarvadharmān nopalabhate" iti / tasmād visphāritajñānacakṣuḥ prajñāśastreṇa kleśārīn nirjitya, nirbhayo viharan yogī, na tu kātarapuruṣa iva vinimīlitākṣaḥ / āryasamādhirāje 'pyuktam-
body.translated_text: Being endowed with skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) and through the cultivation of <s>prajñā</s>, one becomes skilled in both conventional and ultimate truth (<s>saṃvṛti-paramārtha-satya</s>). Therefore, through obtaining unobstructed knowledge (<s>anāvaraṇa-jñāna</s>), one attains all the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>. Therefore, without examination of reality (<s>bhūtapratyavekṣā</s>), neither the arising of correct knowledge nor the abandonment of the obscuration of afflictions is possible. Thus it is stated in the <s>Mañjuśrīvikurvita-sūtra</s>: "How, O maiden, does a <s>bodhisattva</s> become victorious in battle? <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: One who, having investigated and investigated all <s>dharmas</s>, does not apprehend them." Therefore, with the eye of knowledge opened wide, having conquered the enemies of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) with the weapon of <s>prajñā</s>, the <s>yogin</s> dwells fearlessly — not like a timid man with eyes shut tight. In the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s> also it is said:

body.text:
nairātmyadharmān yadi pratyevekṣate tān pratyavekṣya yadi bhāvayet /
sa hetu nirvāṇapahalasya prāptaye yo 'nyaheturna sa bhoti śāntaye // iti /
body.translated_text:
"If one examines the <s>dharmas</s> of non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>), and having examined them, cultivates them,
that is the cause for attaining the fruit of <s>nirvāṇa</s>; no other cause leads to peace."

body.text: sutrasamuccaye coktam- "ātmanā vipaśyanāyogam anuyukto viharati parāṃśca vipaśyanāyāṃ nābhiyojayatīti mārakarmeti /" vipaśyanā ca bhūtapratyavekṣāsvabhāvā āryaratnamegha-sandhinirmocanādau, āryaratnameghe ca- "vipaśyanāṃ nirūpayato niḥsvabhāvatāprativedhad animittapraveśa uktaḥ /" āryalaṅkāvatāre coktam- "yasmāt, mahāmate, buddhayā vicāryamāṇānāṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ bhāvānāṃ nāvadhāryate / tenocyante niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmāḥ" iti / tatra tatra sūtre yā bhagavatā nānāprakārā pratyavekṣā nirdiṣṭā sā virudhyate, yadi bhūtapratyavekṣā na kartavyā / tasmād evaṃ yuktaṃ vaktuṃ vayam alpaprajñā alpavīryāścana śaknumo bāhuśrutyaṃ paryeṣitumiti / na hi tatpratikṣepo yukto bhagavatā
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Sūtrasamuccaya</s> it is stated: "If one dwells devoted to the practice of <s>vipaśyanā</s> by oneself but does not engage others in <s>vipaśyanā</s>, this is the work of <s>Māra</s>." And <s>vipaśyanā</s>, whose nature is the examination of reality (<s>bhūtapratyavekṣā</s>), is taught in the noble <s>Ratnamegha</s>, <s>Sandhinirmocana</s>, and elsewhere. In the noble <s>Ratnamegha</s>: "Through the investigation of <s>vipaśyanā</s>, entry into the signless (<s>animitta</s>) is declared on account of realizing essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>)." And in the noble <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s> it is said: "Because, <s>Mahāmati</s>, when investigated by wisdom (<s>buddhi</s>), neither the particular nor the general characteristics of entities can be ascertained, therefore all <s>dharmas</s> are said to be without own-nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>)." The various kinds of examination taught by the Blessed One in those various <s>sūtras</s> would be contradicted if examination of reality were not to be undertaken. Therefore, it is proper to say: "We are of little wisdom and little energy and are unable to seek extensive learning" — but the rejection of that is not proper, since the Blessed One has praised extensive learning (<s>bāhuśrutya</s>) in many ways

body.text: bahudhā bāhuśrutyasya varṇitatvāt / tat punarbrahmaparipṛcchāyām uktam- "ye tvacintyeṣu dharmeṣu [cintana]viprayuktāḥ teṣām ayoniśa iti / tatrāpi ye paramārthato 'nutpannānāṃ dharmāṇām utpādaṃ parikalpyānityaduḥkhadirūpeṇa śrāvakādivaccintāṃ prakurvanti, teṣāṃ samāropāpavādāntena cintāṃ pravartayatām ayoniśaḥ tad bhavatīti tatpratiṣedhāya yad uktaṃ na bhūtapratyavekṣāyāḥ sa pratiṣedhaḥ tasyāḥ sarvasūtreṣvanujñānāt / tathā ca tatraiva brahmaparipṛcchāyām uktam- "cittaśūro bodhisattva āha-yaścittena sarvadharmāścintayati tatra cākṣato 'nupahataḥ sa tenocyate bodhisattvaḥ" iti / tatraivoktam- "kathaṃ vīryavanto bhavanti, yada sarvajñatācittaṃ vicīyamānānopalabhante" iti / punaḥ tatraivoktam- "matimantaśca te bhaviṣyanti yoniśo dharmān pratyavekṣaṇatayeti" / punaḥ tatraivoktam- "pravicinvanti te dharmān yathā māyāmarīciketi" /
body.translated_text: . This is further stated in the <s>Brahmaparipṛcchā</s>: "Those who are disengaged from contemplation regarding the inconceivable <s>dharmas</s> — for them it is unwise (<s>ayoniśas</s>)." There also, those who, by imputing arising to <s>dharmas</s> that are ultimately unborn, engage in contemplation in the manner of <s>śrāvakas</s> and others — viewing them under the aspect of impermanence, suffering, and so forth — for them, who carry out contemplation falling into the extremes of superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) and denial (<s>apavāda</s>), that becomes unwise. The prohibition stated to counter that is not a prohibition of examination of reality (<s>bhūtapratyavekṣā</s>), since it is sanctioned in all <s>sūtras</s>. Thus in that very <s>Brahmaparipṛcchā</s> it is stated: "The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Cittaśūra</s> said: One who contemplates all <s>dharmas</s> with the mind and therein remains uninjured and unharmed — he is called a <s>bodhisattva</s>." There also it is said: "How do they become energetic? When, investigating the mind of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā-citta</s>), they do not apprehend it." Again there it is said: "And they will be wise, through wisely examining <s>dharmas</s>." Again there it is said: "They investigate <s>dharmas</s> as being like illusions and mirages."

body.text: tad evaṃ yatra yatrācintyādiprapañcaḥ śrūyate, tatra tatra śrutacintāmātreṇaiva tattvādhigamaṃ ye manyante, teṣām abhimānapratiṣedhena pratyātmavedanīyatvaṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratipādayate / ayoniśaśca cittapratiṣedhaḥ kriyata iti boddhavyam, na bhūtapratyavekṣāyāḥ pratiṣedhaḥ / anyathā bahutaraṃ yuktyāgamaviruddhaṃ syāt / yathoktaṃ prāk / kiñca yad eva śrutacintāmayyā prajñayā viditaṃ tad eva bhāvanāmayyā prajñayā bhāvanīyaṃ nānyat / saṃdiṣṭa-dhāvanabhūmyaśvadhāvanavat / tasmāt bhūtapratyavekṣā kartavyā / yadi nāmāsau vikalpasvabhāvātathāpi yoniśo manasikārasvabhāvatvāt tato bhūta nirvikalpajñānodaya iti kṛtvā tajjñānārthinā sā sevanīyā / nirvikalpe ca bhutajñānāgnau
body.translated_text: Thus, wherever the proliferation of the inconceivable and so forth is heard, for those who think that the realization of reality is achieved by mere hearing and reflection (<s>śruta-cintā</s>) alone, the teaching establishes that <s>dharmas</s> are to be personally experienced (<s>pratyātmavedanīya</s>), as a refutation of their pride. And it should be understood that the prohibition pertains to unwise mental engagement, not to the examination of reality (<s>bhūtapratyavekṣā</s>). Otherwise, there would be far too much contradiction with both reasoning and scripture, as was stated previously. Moreover, what is known through the <s>prajñā</s> born of hearing and reflection (<s>śruta-cintā-mayī prajñā</s>) is precisely what should be cultivated through the <s>prajñā</s> born of meditation (<s>bhāvanā-mayī prajñā</s>), and nothing else — like a horse that runs on the very ground that has been shown to it. Therefore, examination of reality must be undertaken. Even though that examination is of the nature of conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>), because it has the nature of wise attention (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>), the arising of true non-conceptual knowledge (<s>nirvikalpa-jñāna</s>) proceeds from it; therefore one who seeks that knowledge should cultivate it. And when the fire of true non-conceptual knowledge

body.text: samutpanne, sati, kāṣṭhadvayanigharṣasaṃjātavanhinā tatkāṣṭhadvayadāhavat sāpi paścāt tenaiva dahyata evetyuktam āryaratnakūṭe /
body.translated_text: has arisen, just as a fire born from the friction of two sticks burns those very two sticks, so too that examination is subsequently consumed by that very knowledge itself — thus it is stated in the noble <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>.

body.text: yaccāpyucyate- na kiṃcit kuśalādikarma kartavyam iti / tatraivaivaṃ vadatā karmakṣayān muktirityājīvaka vādābhyupagamo bhavet / na hi bhagavatpravacane karmakṣayān muktiriṣyate / kiṃ tarhi, kleśakṣayāt / anādikālopacittasya hi karmaṇo na śakyate kṣayaḥ kartu tasyānantatvāt / apāyādiṣu ca tatphalaṃ bhuñjānasyāparasyāpi karmaṇaḥ prasūteḥ kleśeṣu cāvikaleṣu tatkaraṇatayā sthiteṣu karmaṇo niroddhum aśakyatvāt / pradīpānirodhe tatprabhāyā anirodhavat / na cāpi tasya vipaśyanāpavādinaḥ kleśakṣayaḥ saṃbhavatītyukta prāk / atha kleśakṣayārtha vipaśyanā sevanīyeti manyate, tadā kleśakṣayād eva muktiḥ sidhyatīti karmakṣaye tarhi vyarthaḥ śramaḥ / akuśalakarma na kartavyam iti yuktametat, kuśalaṃ tu kimiti pratiṣidhyate / saṃsārāvāhakatvāt pratiṣidhyata iti cet, tadayuktam / yad eva ātmādiviparyāsasamutthāpitam kuśalaṃ tad eva saṃsārāvāhakaṃ bhavati / na tu bodhisattvānāṃ mahākaruṇāsamutthāpitam anuttarasaṃbodhipariṇāmitamapi / tathā āryadaśabhūmake eta eva daśakuśalakarmapathāḥ pariṇāmanādipariśuddhiviśeṣeṇa śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvabuddhatvavāhakā bhavantīti nirdiṣṭam / āryaratnakūṭe ca, sarvamahānadīnāṃ mahāsamudre praviṣṭānāṃ payaḥ skandhavad bodhisattvānāṃ nānāmukhopacitaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ sarvajñatāpariṇāmitaṃ sarvajñataikarasaṃ bhavati iti varṇitam /
body.translated_text: As for the assertion that "no wholesome or other <s>karma</s> should be performed" — by speaking thus, one would adopt the position of the <s>Ājīvikas</s>, that liberation comes from the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>. But in the teaching of the Blessed One, liberation through the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> is not accepted. What then? Through the exhaustion of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). For it is impossible to exhaust <s>karma</s> that has been accumulated since beginningless time, because it is infinite. And because, while one experiences the fruits of that <s>karma</s> in the lower realms and elsewhere, further <s>karma</s> is produced; and because, while the afflictions remain intact and standing as the cause of <s>karma</s>, <s>karma</s> cannot be stopped — just as when a lamp is not extinguished, its light is not extinguished either. Nor is the exhaustion of afflictions possible for one who rejects <s>vipaśyanā</s>, as was stated previously. If one thinks that <s>vipaśyanā</s> should be cultivated for the purpose of exhausting afflictions, then since liberation is established precisely through the exhaustion of afflictions, the effort to exhaust <s>karma</s> would be pointless. That unwholesome <s>karma</s> should not be performed — this is reasonable. But why is wholesome <s>karma</s> prohibited? If one says it is prohibited because it carries one through <s>saṃsāra</s>, that is wrong. Only that wholesome action which is produced by the false conception (<s>viparyāsa</s>) of self and so forth carries one through <s>saṃsāra</s>. But not that which is produced by the great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and dedicated to unsurpassed awakening (<s>anuttara-saṃbodhi</s>). Thus in the noble <s>Daśabhūmika</s> it is taught that these very ten paths of wholesome action (<s>daśa-kuśala-karmapatha</s>), through the distinction of purification by dedication and other means, become vehicles leading to the states of <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and <s>Buddha</s>. And in the noble <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>, it is praised that, just as the waters of all great rivers that have entered the great ocean become one mass, so too the roots of merit (<s>kuśala-mūla</s>) accumulated by <s>bodhisattvas</s> through various means, when dedicated to omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), become of one taste with omniscience.

body.text: yā ca buddhabodhisattvānāṃ rūpakāyakṣetrapariśuddhiḥ prabhāparivāramahābhogatādisaṃpattiḥ dānādipuṇyasambhāraphalasattvena tatra tatra sūtre varṇitā bhagavatā sāpi virudhyate / kuśalacaryāpratiṣedhe ca prātimokṣasaṃvarādirapi pratikṣiptaḥ syāt / tato vyarthameva tasya śiromuṇḍitakāṣāyadhāraṇādi prasajyeta / kuśalakarmābhisaṃskāravaimukhye ca sati saṃsāravaimukhyaṃ sattvārthakriyāvaimukhyaṃ ca sevitaṃ bhavet / tato bodhiḥ tasya dūre bhavet / uktaṃ hyāryaṃsaṃdhinirmocane- "ekāntasattvārthavimukhasya ekāntasaṃskārā bhisaṃskāravimukhasya nānuttarāsamyaksaṃbodhiruktā mayeti / "āryopāliparipṛcchādau ca- "saṃsāre vaimukhyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ paradauḥśīlyamiti varṇitam / saṃsāraparigrahaḥ tu paramaṃ śīlam /" uktam āryavimalakīrtinirdeśe ca- "upāyād bhavati saṃsāragamanaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mokṣaḥ / upāyarahitā ca prajñā bandhaḥ, prajñārahitaścopāyo bandhaḥ / prajñāsahita upāyo mokṣaḥ, upāyasahitā prajñā mokṣaḥ" iti varṇitam / āryagaganagañje uktam- "saṃsāraparikhedo bodhisattvānāṃ mārakarma iti /" sūtrasamuccaye ca- "asaṃskṛtaṃ ca pratyavekṣate saṃskṛtaiśca kuśalaiḥ parikhidyata iti mārakarma iti / bodhimārga prajānāti pāramitāmārga ca na paryeṣata iti mārakarmeti /" yat punaḥ tatraivoktam- "dānacittābhiniveśād yāvat prajñācittābhiniveśāṃ mārakarmeti tatra na dānādināṃ sevāpratiṣedhaḥ kiṃ tvahaṃkāramamakāracittābhiniviṣṭasya grāhyagrāhakacittābhiniviṣṭasya caupalambhikasya yo viparītābhiniveśo dānādau tasya pratiṣedhaḥ / viparītābhiniveśasamuttthāpitā hi dānādayo 'pariśuddhā bhavantīti kṛtvā mārakarmetyuktam / anyathā dhyānam api na sevanīyaṃ syāt / tathā ca kathaṃ muktiḥ bhavet?
body.translated_text: Moreover, the purity of the form-body and the pure land of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and the prosperity of radiance, retinue, and great enjoyments — which the Blessed One has described in various <s>sūtras</s> as being the fruits of the accumulation of merit through generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest — that too would be contradicted. And if wholesome practice is prohibited, even the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> vows and the rest would be rejected. Then his shaving the head and wearing the saffron robe and so forth would be entirely pointless. And if there is aversion toward the conditioning of wholesome actions, then aversion to <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) and aversion to acting for the welfare of beings would be practiced. Then awakening would be far from him. For it is stated in the <s>Ārya-Saṃdhinirmocana</s>: 'For one who is entirely averse to the welfare of beings and entirely averse to conditioning, unsurpassed perfect awakening has not been taught by me.' And in the <s>Ārya-Upāliparipṛcchā</s> and elsewhere: 'Aversion to <s>saṃsāra</s> is described as a transgression of moral discipline for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. But the embrace of <s>saṃsāra</s> is the supreme moral discipline.' And in the <s>Ārya-Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s> it is described: 'The entry of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> into <s>saṃsāra</s> through skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) is liberation. Wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) without skillful means is bondage, and skillful means without wisdom is bondage. Skillful means accompanied by wisdom is liberation, and wisdom accompanied by skillful means is liberation.' In the <s>Ārya-Gaganagañja</s> it is stated: 'Weariness of <s>saṃsāra</s> is the activity of <s>Māra</s> for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.' And in the <s>Sūtrasamuccaya</s>: 'One who contemplates the unconditioned and becomes weary of conditioned wholesome [deeds] — that is the activity of <s>Māra</s>. One who knows the path to awakening but does not seek the path of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) — that is the activity of <s>Māra</s>.' As for what is stated in that very [text]: 'Clinging to the thought of generosity, up to clinging to the thought of wisdom — that is the activity of <s>Māra</s>' — therein it is not a prohibition of the practice of generosity and the rest, but rather a prohibition of the perverted clinging of one whose mind is fixed on ego and possessiveness, whose mind is fixed on the graspable and the grasper, and who is attached to apprehension, with respect to generosity and so forth. For generosity and the rest that are produced from perverted clinging become impure — therefore it is called the activity of <s>Māra</s>. Otherwise, even meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) would not be worth practicing. And then, how would liberation be possible?

body.text: ata evaupalambhikasya sattvanānātvasaṃjñāyā yad dānādi tad apariśuddham iti pratipādanāya āryagaganagañje 'pi- "sattvanānātva [viparītakarma]saṃjñino dānādi mārakarmetyuktam" / yaccāpi [tri]skandhapariṇāmanāyām uktam- "sarvam eva dāna-śīla-kṣānti-vīrya-dhyāna-prajñāsamatām ajānatopalambhayati, tena paryeṣṭitadānena parāmṛṣṭaśīlena śīlaṃ rakṣitam / ātmaparasaṃjñinā kṣāntirbhāvitetyādi tat pratideśayāmīti /" tatrāpyaupalambhikasya nānatvasaṃjñino viparītābhiniveśasamutthāpitā dānādayo 'pi śuddhā bhavantīti etāvanmātraṃ pratipāditam / na tu sarvathā dānādīnāṃ sevanapratiṣedhaḥ / anyathā sarvasyaiva dānāderaviśeṣeṇa pratideśanā kṛtā syāt, nopalambhaviparyāsapatitasyaiva / yaccāpi brahmaparipṛcchāyām uktam- "yāvatī caryā sarvā parikalpyā / niṣparikalpyā ca bodhirityādi /" tatrāpyutpādādivikalpacaryāyāḥ prakṛtatvāt tasyāḥ parikalpatvamuktam / animittavihāre cānabhisaṃskāravāhinaḥ sthitasya bodhisattvasya vyākaraṇaṃ bhavati, nānyasyetyetāvanmātraṃ pratipāditam / sarveṣāṃ ca dānādīnāṃ paramārthato 'nutpannatvaṃ ca paridīpitam, na tu caryā na kartavyetyabhihitam /
body.translated_text: For this very reason, in the <s>Ārya-Gaganagañja</s> too, in order to demonstrate that generosity and the rest of one who is an apprehender (<s>aupalambhika</s>) and has the perception of the multiplicity of beings are impure, it is stated: 'The generosity and so forth of one who has the perception of the multiplicity of beings [and perverted action] is the activity of <s>Māra</s>.' And what is also stated in the <s>Triskandha</s> confession: 'One who does not know the equality of all generosity, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom, who apprehends [them with grasping] — by such sought-out generosity, morality is guarded with clinging; by one who has the perception of self and other, patience is cultivated — and so forth — I confess that.' Therein too, only this much is demonstrated: that generosity and the rest, produced from the perverted clinging of one who is an apprehender and has the perception of multiplicity, become impure. But there is no prohibition of the practice of generosity and the rest in every respect. Otherwise, all generosity and the rest would have been confessed without distinction, not only [that] of one who has fallen into the perversion of apprehension. And what is also stated in the <s>Brahmaparipṛcchā</s>: 'Whatever practice there is, all is conceptualized. But awakening is non-conceptualized' — and so forth. Therein too, since the practice of conceptualization of arising and the like is the topic, its being conceptualized is stated. And the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) is given to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who dwells in the signless abiding with effortless flow, and not to another — only this much is demonstrated. And the non-arising of all generosity and the rest in the ultimate sense is also illuminated, but it is not stated that practice should not be performed.

body.text: anyathā hi dīpaṅkarāvadāne ye buddhā bhagavatā paryupāsitā yeṣāṃ tu kalpamapi bhagavatā bhāṣamāṇena na śakyaṃ nāmaparikīrtnaṃ kathaṃ teṣāṃ bhagavatā bodhisattvāvasthāyāṃ caryāpratiṣedho na kṛtaḥ / dīpaṅkareṇāpi tadānīṃ bhagavataścaryāpratiṣedho na kṛta eva / kiṃ tu yadā śāntānimittavihāre 'ṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau sthito 'sau dṛṣṭastadāsau vyākṛto bhagavatā, tatra tasya caryā
body.translated_text: For otherwise, in the <s>Dīpaṅkara</s> narrative, those <s>Buddhas</s> whom the Blessed One attended — whose names even the Blessed One could not enumerate even if speaking for an entire <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age) — how is it that they did not prohibit practice for the Blessed One when he was in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage? Even <s>Dīpaṅkara</s> did not at that time prohibit the Blessed One's practice. Rather, when [the Blessed One] was seen dwelling on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> in the peaceful signless abiding, then the Blessed One was given the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) by him. Therein, his practice

body.text: apratiṣiddhā / sā cānimittavihāraparamatā bodhisattvānām aṣṭāmyāṃ bhūmau daśabhūmikairbuddhaiḥ pratiṣiddhā 'mā bhūd etad eva teṣāṃ parinirvāṇam' iti kṛtvā yadi tu sarvathā caryā na kartavyā bhavet pūrvoktaṃ sarva virudhyeta /
body.translated_text: was not prohibited. And that supreme devotion to the signless abiding of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> was prohibited by the <s>Buddhas</s> of the ten <s>bhūmis</s>, thinking 'Let this not become their final <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' But if practice were not to be performed in every respect, everything stated above would be contradicted.

body.text: yacca tatraiva brahmaparipṛcchāyām uktam- "dānaṃ ca dadāti taccāvipākābhikāṅkṣī, śīlaṃ ca rakṣati taccāsamāropitaḥ" ityādi / caturbhiḥ brahma! dharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā avaivarttikā bhavanti buddhadharmeṣu / katamaiścaturbhiḥ aparimitasaṃsāraparigraheṇa aparimitabuddhopasthānapūjayetyādi sarvaṃ virudhyeta / nāpi mṛdvindriyeṇaiva caryā kartavyā na tu tīkṣṇendriyeṇeti yuktaṃ vaktum / yataḥ prathamāṃ bhūmimupādāya yāvaddaśamībhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dānādicaryā utpadyate, na ca pariśiṣṭāsu na samudācaratīti vacanāt / nahi bhūmipraviṣṭā api mṛdvindriyāyuktāḥ / āryopaliparipṛcchāyām- "anutpattikadharmakṣāntipratiṣṭhitenaiva tyāgamahātyāgātityāgāḥ kartavyāḥ" iti varṇitam / sūtrasamuccaye ca- "ṣaṭpāramitādipratipattimān bodhisattvastathāgatarddhigatikaḥ" iti varṇitam / na ca tathāgatarddhigateranyā śīghratarā gatirasti / nāpi ṣaṭpāramitādaśabhūmivyatirekeṇānyo bodhisattvānāṃ mārgo 'sti yaḥ śīghrataravāhīsyāt / krameṇaiva ca cittasaṃtateḥ kanakaśuddhivat śuddhirbhavatīti sūtre varṇitam [āryalaṅkāvatāradaśabhūmikādau coktaṃ]- tathatāyāṃ yadā sthito bodhisattvo bhavati, tadā prathamāyāṃ bhūmau praviṣṭo bhavati / tataḥ krameṇaiva pūrvabhūmīḥ pariśodhya tathāgatabhūmiṃ praviśatīti / ato nāsti bhūmipāramitāvyatirekeṇa [yugapat] buddhatvapurapraveśe anyanmukhaṃ nāpi bhagavatā kvacit sūtrādau deśitam /
body.translated_text: And what is also stated in that very <s>Brahmaparipṛcchā</s>: 'One gives generosity and is not desirous of its fruit; one guards morality and is not attached [to it]' — and so forth. '<s>Brahman</s>! <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with four <s>dharmas</s> (qualities) become irreversible in the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> (qualities of Buddhahood). Which four? By the embrace of limitless <s>saṃsāra</s>, by the unlimited attendance upon and worship of <s>Buddhas</s>' — and so forth — all this would be contradicted. Nor is it reasonable to say that practice should be performed only by one of dull faculties but not by one of sharp faculties, because it is stated that the practice of generosity and the rest arises for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established from the first <s>bhūmi</s> up to the tenth <s>bhūmi</s>, and does not cease on the remaining [bhūmis]. For even those who have entered the <s>bhūmis</s> are not aptly described as having dull faculties. In the <s>Ārya-Upāliparipṛcchā</s> it is described: 'By one who is established in <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas), the acts of renunciation, great renunciation, and supreme renunciation should be performed.' And in the <s>Sūtrasamuccaya</s> it is described: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who possesses the practice of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) and so forth attains the destination of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' And there is no swifter destination than the destination of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Nor is there any other path for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> apart from the six <s>pāramitās</s> and the ten <s>bhūmis</s> that would be a swifter vehicle. And it is described in the <s>sūtras</s> that the purification of the mental continuum occurs progressively, like the purification of gold [stated in the <s>Ārya-Laṅkāvatāra</s>, the <s>Daśabhūmika</s>, and elsewhere]: 'When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwells in <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), he has entered the first <s>bhūmi</s>. Then, progressively purifying the lower <s>bhūmis</s>, he enters the <s>Tathāgata-bhūmi</s> (stage of the Tathāgata).' Therefore, there is no other gateway to entry into the city of <s>Buddhahood</s> [suddenly] apart from the <s>bhūmis</s> and <s>pāramitās</s>, nor has the Blessed One taught [such] in any <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text:
dhyāna eva ṣaṭpāramitāntargamāt tatsevanād eva sarvapāramitāḥ sevitā bhavantyato na dānādayaḥ [anyapāramitāḥ] pṛthak sevitavyā iti cet tad ayuktam / evaṃ hi buddhe gomayamaṇḍale 'pi ṣaṭpāramitāntargamān maṇḍalakam eva kartavyaṃ syānna dhyānādyāḥ / śrāvakasyāpi nirodhasamādhisamāpannasya nimittād eva asamudācārāt tadā ṣaṭpāramitāparipūriprasaṅgaḥ / tataśca na śrāvakebhyo bodhisattvānāṃ bhedaḥ pratipādito bhavet / sarvāvasthāyām eva tu bodhisattvena ṣaṭpāramitāḥ paripūrayitavyā iti saṃdarśanārthe ekaikapāramitāntarbhāvaḥ sarvapāramitānāṃ bhagavatā sandarśitaḥ / na punarekaiva pāramitā sevanīyeti / tathā coktaṃ sarvadharmavaipulye- "yo 'pyayaṃ maitreya! ṣaṭpāramitāsamudāgamo bodhisattvānāṃ saṃbodhāya taṃ te mohapuruṣā evaṃ vakṣyanti, prajñāpāramitāyām evaṃ bodhisattvena śikṣitavyam, kiṃ śeṣābhiḥ pāramitābhiriti / te 'nyāḥ pāramitā dūṣayitavyā maṃsyante / tat kiṃ manyase, ajita! duṣprajñaḥ sa kāśirājo 'bhūt, yena kapotārthena śyenāya svamāṃsāni dattāni? maitreya āha- no hīdaṃ bhagavan! bhagavān āha- yāni mayā maitreya! bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktāni kuśalamūlānyupacitāni / apakṛtaṃ nu taiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ? maitreya āha, no hīdaṃ bhagavan, bhagavān āha- tvaṃ tāvad ajita! ṣaṣṭikalpān dānāpāramitāyāṃ samudāgataḥ / evaṃ yāvat ṣaṣṭikalpān prajñāpāramitāyāṃ samudāgataḥ / tat te mohapuruṣā evaṃ vakṣyanti / ekanayenaiva bodhiryaduta śūnyatānayeneti te caryāpariśuddhā bhavanti" ityādi / kevalaṃ śūnyātām eva sevamānāḥ śrāvakavannirvāṇe patanti / ataḥ upāyasahitā prajñā sevanīyā /
ata evācāryanāgārjunapādaiḥ sūtrasamuccaye 'bhihitam- "na copāyakauśalarahitena bodhisattvena gambhīradharmatāyāmabhiyoktavyam" iti / atra
body.translated_text: If [someone says:] 'Since the six <s>pāramitās</s> are included within <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) itself, by cultivating that alone all the <s>pāramitās</s> are cultivated; therefore giving (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest [need] not be cultivated separately' — that is unreasonable. For in that case, since the six <s>pāramitās</s> are included even in a <s>maṇḍala</s> [made of] cow-dung for a <s>Buddha</s>, one would only need to make the <s>maṇḍala</s> and not [practice] <s>dhyāna</s> and the rest. Even for a <s>Śrāvaka</s> who has attained the cessation-<s>samādhi</s> (<s>nirodha-samādhi</s>), since there is no active engagement through [conceptual] signs at that time, the consequence would be the fulfillment of the six <s>pāramitās</s>; and then no distinction between <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> would be established. But the Blessed One has shown the inclusion of all the <s>pāramitās</s> within each individual <s>pāramitā</s> for the purpose of demonstrating that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> must fulfill the six <s>pāramitās</s> in all states — not that only one <s>pāramitā</s> should be cultivated. As stated in the <s>Sarvadharmavaipulya</s>: 'That which, <s>Maitreya</s>, is the practice of the six <s>pāramitās</s> for the awakening of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — those deluded persons will say: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train only in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; what need for the remaining perfections?" They will think the other perfections should be disparaged. What do you think, <s>Ajita</s>? Was the king of <s>Kāśī</s> of poor wisdom, who gave his own flesh to a hawk for the sake of a pigeon? <s>Maitreya</s> said: No indeed, Blessed One! The Blessed One said: The roots of merit connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s> accumulated by me while practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct — were those roots of merit harmful? <s>Maitreya</s> said: No indeed. The Blessed One said: You yourself, <s>Ajita</s>, practiced the <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> for sixty <s>kalpas</s>, and so on up to the <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> for sixty <s>kalpas</s>. Those deluded persons will say: "There is only one approach to awakening, namely the approach of emptiness" — [and claim that] their conduct is purified' — and so forth. Those who cultivate emptiness alone fall into <s>nirvāṇa</s> like <s>Śrāvakas</s>. Therefore, wisdom accompanied by skillful means should be cultivated. For this very reason, the master <s>Nāgārjuna</s> stated in the <s>Sūtrasamuccaya</s>: 'A <s>Bodhisattva</s> lacking skill in means should not engage in the profound nature of <s>dharmas</s>.' Herein,

body.text: āryavimalakīrtinirdeśādijñāpakastairūpanyastaḥ, na cācāryanāgārjunapādīyaṃ vacanam / yuktayāgamopetaṃ tyaktvā bhagavadvacanaṃ ca parityajya anyasya mūrkhajanasya vacanaṃ prekṣāvatā grahītum ayuktam / āryaratnakūṭe ca- "sakaladānādikuśalopetatayā sarvākāravaropetaśūnyatā sevanīyetyuktaṃ na tu kevalā /" āryaratnakūṭe coktam- tadyathā kāśyapāmātyasaṃgṛhītā rājānaḥ sarvakāryāṇi kurvanti evam eva upāyakauśalyasaṃgṛhītā bodhisattvasya prajñā sarvabuddhakāryāṇi karoti /
body.translated_text: the <s>Āryavimalakīrtinirdeśa</s> and other [sūtras] are the indicators, not the word of the master <s>Nāgārjuna</s> [alone]. Abandoning what is supported by reasoning and scripture, and discarding the word of the Blessed One, it is unreasonable for a discerning person to accept the words of some foolish person. And in the <s>Āryaratnakūṭa</s>: 'It is said that emptiness endowed with all the best aspects (<s>sarvākāravaropetaśūnyatā</s>) should be cultivated, being replete with all wholesome [qualities] of giving and the rest — not emptiness alone.' And in the <s>Āryaratnakūṭa</s> it is stated: 'Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, kings supported by ministers accomplish all tasks, so too the wisdom of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, supported by skill in means, accomplishes all <s>Buddha</s>-activities.'

body.text: ata eva kevalāṃ śūnyatāṃ sevamānasya mā bhūnnirvāṇapraveśa iti / bhagavatā āryatathāgataguhyasūtre" coktam- "naikāntanirālambanaṃ cittamātrasevanaṃ kartavyam api tu upāyakauśalyam api sevanīyam iti pradarśanārtham uktam- tadyathāpi nāma, kulaputra! agnirupādānād jvalati / anupādānaḥ śāmyati / evam evārambaṇataścittaṃ jvalati, anārambaṇaṃ śāmyati / tatropāyakuśalo bodhisattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāpariśuddhārambaṇopaśamam api jānāti / kuśalamūlārambaṇaṃ ca na śāmyati / kleśārambaṇaṃ ca notthāpayati / pāramitārambaṇaṃ cotthāpayati / śūnyatārambaṇaṃ ca pratyavekṣate sarvasattvamahākaruṇārambaṇaṃ ca prekṣate iti hi kulaputra! upāyakuśalaḥ prajñāpāramitāpariśuddho bodhisattvo 'nārambane vaśitāṃ pratilabhate" iti vistaram uktvā punaśca vadatyevaṃ hi- "nāsti tat kiṃcid ārambaṇaṃ bodhisattvasya yat sarvajñajñānābhinirhārāya na saṃtiṣṭhate / yasya bodhisattvasya sarvārambāṇāni bodhipariṇāmitāni, ayaṃ bodhisattva upāyakuśala sarvadharmān bodhyanugatān paśyati / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra, nāsti tat trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau yat sattvānām upabhogāya na syāt /
