body.translated_text: For this very reason, lest one who cultivates emptiness alone enter <s>nirvāṇa</s> [prematurely], the Blessed One stated in the <s>Āryatathāgataguhya-sūtra</s>: 'One should not exclusively cultivate the mind-only practice that is without an object; rather, skill in means should also be cultivated.' For the purpose of demonstrating this, it is said: 'Just as, O son of good family, fire blazes due to fuel and is extinguished without fuel — so too the mind blazes due to an object and is calmed without an object. Therein, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> skilled in means knows the calming of the object purified by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; and he does not extinguish the object of roots of merit; and he does not activate the object of afflictions; and he activates the object of the <s>pāramitās</s>; and he examines the object of emptiness; and he regards the object of great compassion for all beings. Thus, O son of good family, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> skilled in means, purified by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, attains mastery over objectlessness.' And having spoken at length, [the sūtra] says further: 'There is no object of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> that does not contribute to the accomplishment of omniscient knowledge. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose every object is dedicated to awakening — this <s>Bodhisattva</s> skilled in means sees all <s>dharmas</s> as following after awakening. Just as, O son of good family, there is nothing in the great trichiliocosm that is not for the enjoyment of beings,

body.text: evam eva, kulaputra nāsti tat kiṃcid ārambaṇaṃ yad upāyakuśalo bodhisattvo bodhāya copakārībhūtaṃ na paśyati" iti vistaraḥ / evam anantasūtrānteṣu bodhisattvānāṃ prajñopāyapratipattirnirdiṣṭā / tatra yadi nāma svayaṃ na śakyate dānādidpuṇyasaṃbhāravīryam ārabdhuṃ tathāpi anyeṣām evam upadeśo dātuṃ na yuktaśceti svaparadrohaḥ kṛtaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: so too, O son of good family, there is no object that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> skilled in means does not see as conducive to awakening' — and so forth in detail. Thus, in innumerable <s>sūtras</s>, the practice of wisdom and skillful means (<s>prajñā-upāya</s>) is taught for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Therein, even if one is unable oneself to begin the vigor of accumulating the merit of giving and the rest, still it would not be right to give such instruction to others [telling them not to practice these] — that would be harmful to both self and others.

body.text: tad evaṃ yuktyāgamābhyāṃ pratipāditaṃ yathā bodhisattvenāvaśyaṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā kartavyā sakaladānādipuṇyasambhāraścopārjayitavyaḥ / tataḥ prekṣāvatālpaśrutānām ābhimānikānāṃ vacanaṃ viṣam ivāvadhūyāryanāgārjunādividvajjanavacanāmṛtanugatena sakalasattveṣu mahakāruṇām upajanayya māyākāravad aviparyastenānuttarasaṃbodhipariṇāmitasakaladānādikuśalacaryāyām aśeṣajagaduddharaṇe cābhiyuktne abhāvitavyam / yathoktam āryadharmasaṃgītau-
body.translated_text: Thus it has been demonstrated by reasoning and scripture that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> must necessarily perform the investigation of reality (<s>bhūtapratyavekṣā</s>) and also accumulate the entire merit of giving and the rest. Therefore, a discerning person, shaking off like poison the words of the ignorant and conceited, following the nectar-like words of learned ones such as the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and others, generating great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) for all beings, should engage — like a magician, without error — in the wholesome conduct of all forms of giving and the rest dedicated to unsurpassed awakening, and in the rescue of the entire world without remainder, [keeping in mind] what was stated. As stated in the <s>Āryadharmasaṃgīti</s>:

children.translated_text: Just as a magician, intent on releasing a magical creation,

children.text: na cāsya nirmite saṅgo jñātapūrvo yato 'sya saḥ //
children.translated_text: has no attachment to [his] creation, since he has known it for what it is —

body.text:
tribhavaṃ nirmitaprakhyaṃ jñātvā saṃbodhipāragaḥ /
sannahyanti jagaddhetoḥ jñātapūrve jage tathā // iti tasyaivaṃ /
body.translated_text: knowing the three realms of existence to be like a magical creation, those who have reached the far shore of awakening gird themselves for the sake of the world, having known the world for what it is. Thus for him:

body.text: prajñām upāyaṃ ca satataṃ satkṛtyābhyasyataḥ krameṇa [cittaṃ] saṃtatiparipākād uttarottaraviśuddhataratamakṣaṇodayād bhūtārthabhāvanāprakarṣaparyantagamena sakalakalpanājālarahitaṃ sphuṭataraṃ dharmadhātvadhigamaṃ vimalaṃ niścalanivātadīpavallokottarajñānam utpadyate / tadā ca vastuparyantatālambanam pratilabdhaṃ bhavati / darśanamārgaṃ ca praviṣṭo bhavati / prathamā ca bhūmiḥ prāptā bhavati / tatastaduttarā bhūmīḥ pariśodhayan krameṇa kanakavad aśeṣāvaraṇāpagame sati asaktam apratihataṃ jñānaṃ pratilabhya buddhabhūmim aśeṣaguṇādhārāṃ prāpto bhavati / kāryapariniṣpattiṃ cālambanaṃ pratilabhate / tasmād buddhatvādhigamārthinā madhyamapaddhatau tāvad abhiyogaḥ karaṇīya iti /
body.translated_text: For one who constantly and respectfully practices both wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), gradually, through the maturation of the mental continuum, through the arising of ever-purer supreme moments, reaching the culmination of the cultivation of ultimate reality — there arises supramundane knowledge (<s>lokottara-jñāna</s>) that is free from the entire net of conceptual construction, that clearly realizes the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharmas</s>), that is stainless, unmoving like a lamp in a windless place. At that time, one has attained the object [of knowledge] that is the ultimate limit of things. One has entered the path of seeing (<s>darśana-mārga</s>). The first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) has been attained. Then, progressively purifying the subsequent stages, like gold [being refined], when all obscurations have been removed without remainder, having attained unobstructed and unhindered knowledge, one attains the <s>Buddha</s>-stage, which is the foundation of all qualities without exception. And one attains the object [of activity] that is the accomplishment of all tasks. Therefore, one who seeks the attainment of <s>Buddhahood</s> should apply effort in the middle path.

children.text: prakāśya yat prāpi mayā śubham asamapaddhitam /
children.translated_text: Having illuminated [the path], may the merit I have attained — an incomparable achievement —
may beings through that [merit] attain the middle path.
The virtuous, having cast off the defilements of envy and the rest, are insatiable for qualities, like the ocean for water;

children.text: vivecya gṛṇhanti subhāṣitāni haṃsāḥ payo yatpayasi prahṛṣṭāḥ //
children.translated_text: they discriminatingly accept well-spoken words, like <s>haṃsas</s> (swans) delighting in milk mixed with water.
Therefore, a mind disturbed by partiality has been cast far away by the wise;
all that is well-spoken should be accepted, even from a child.

body.text: ācāryakamalaśīlena ante nibaddho bhāvanākramaḥ samāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhāvanākrama</s>, composed at the end by the master <s>Kamalaśīla</s>, is complete.

body.text: tṛtīyaḥ bhāvanākramaḥ samāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: The third <s>Bhāvanākrama</s> is complete.
